Each brush is medium-sized. The brush glides through my hair wet or dry and detangles it as well. It also feels great in my hands and does not slip out like some brushes do. Note that I have fine short to medium curly hair.  Although I really like these brushes, I would never buy them because they are no better than what I can buy locally at half the price.

The current price of $16.99 is too expensive for these as I can get one brush like this at my local store for $3.99 each.

title: Wonderful oval brush that glides & detangles my dry hair; best for short/fine hair
text:
The brush is the best part of this ensemble. There is also a long teasing comb and a metal brush for removing hair from the hair brush. However, neither item is great and I will not be using them.

Nevertheless, I love the hair brush. The wooden handle feels great and is curved a little, which provides me with a good grip. There are boar bristles interspersed with nylon bristles. Since the bristles are short, this is best for shorter hair and fine hair. I have both short to medium fine wavy hair, so this works very well.

The brush glides through my hair and detangles it as well. It also feels great in my hands and does not slip out like some brushes do. 

I really love this brush but it is not for everyone. The current price of $9.95 is competitively priced for this.

title: Lasted me 12 hours until my next shower; surprisingly effective; nice fresh scent
text:
I usually use nothing but Old Spice Swagger solid with the active ingredient of aluminum zirconium tetrachlorohydrex gly 17%. This Schmidt's solid has no aluminum and only natural ingredients. Usually, products like these only last me about 2-3 hours; however, the protection lasted 12 hours until my next shower. Of course, it is winter, so that might be why.

I take a shower every 12 hours because I sweat a lot, so I can never attest to 48-hour protection. This has a fresh cucumber scent. I would not say it is cucumber but it is lovely. I really love the scent.

This works better than other non-aluminum deodorants I tried previously. The current price of $31.13 comes to an expensive $7.78 per 2.65 ounce solid stick as this is a 4-pack. I would never purchase this due to the high price. However, if the price were more in line with my aluminum deodorant, I would consider it.

title: Nice fragrance; moisturizing; only fizzes & I needed strainer to catch petal pieces when done
text:
[[VIDEOID:d5dd1373fa830ee17cd7e836dd7a2f67]] There are 6 individually wrapped small bath bombs in this set in one nice fragrance combination of patchouli and buriti. Unfortunately, that is all that is positive to me. Each bomb fizzes and dissolves in about two minutes. There are no suds and only floating chopped petal pieces in the water. The bath looks a bit oily but I did not feel my feet (as I used this in a foot bath) to be moisturized by soaking them in this. Also, my foot bath had to be washed out because the oil adhered to it.

Since these are white, there were no color rings to adhere to my skin, my foot bath, or my towels. When I was done, I needed a sink strainer to catch all the debris that washed away. I am glad I did not use these in an actual bath.

The current price of $10.81 ($12.72 minus 15%) comes to a reasonable $1.80 per bomb; however, these bombs are so lackluster to me that I would never order them. I love the fragrance and the fact that there is no color to rinse off, but that is all I love.

title: Lathers and cleans well but can scuffs up my acrylic shower
text:
This body lotion is very nice. It has a weird fragrance to it that I can't describe and which I neither like nor dislike. It sort of reminds me of fabric softener. This washes and lathers well and leaves me feeling clean.

There are two negatives. First, I do not like at all that it comes in a can. When I was using the pump in my shower, the bottom of the can immediately left gray scuff marks on my acrylic shower shelf. As the can moves around slightly while I pump, it leaves the same type of scuffs marks that a pot would leave on a porcelain sink. I absolutely hate this about the can. The other negative is that this comes packaged in a box with the can and pump separate. There is no need to wrap this in a box. To me that is very wasteful. Also, when it is shipped, that is another box, over the product's brown box, to ship it out. I wish they would dispense with the can cap, especially since I needed a pliers to open the top, and ship it with the pump closed but inserted and perhaps some shrink-wrapped plastic over the top to keep the soap from spilling out.

In summary, the body wash itself is good but I hate the can it comes in, particularly because of the scuff marks it causes. I also wish the soap had a fragrance that I found enticing and that the packaging was reduced. At the current price of $15.99, this is on the high side of competitively priced for a 10-ounce tin of body wash.

title: Moisturizing body lotion but I do not like that it comes in a tin can
text:
This body lotion is hydrating. It also has a nice subtle fragrance to it. I really like the results. I applied this to my skin and it left it moisturized and feeling quenched.

However, there are several negatives with regard to this. First, I do not like that it comes in a can. Since the pump is separate, I had to take a wrench to unscrew the cap as I could not get it off. It was nice that it came with a lot of body lotion, but the act of inserting the pump top had it spilling out all over--see photo. They should not have filled the can to the top. Second, this comes packaged in a box with the can and pump separate. There is no need to wrap this in a box. To me that is very wasteful. Also, when it is shipped, that is another box, over the product's brown box, to ship it out. I wish they would dispense with the can cap and ship it with the pump closed but inserted and perhaps some shrink-wrapped plastic over the top to keep the cream from spilling out.

Other than this, I really like this lotion. At the current price of $17.99, this is on the high side of competitively priced for a thick 10 ounce tin of body lotion.

title: Thick like body butter & very hydrating but it’s over packaged
text:
This cream is thick and hydrating. It also has a nice subtle fragrance to it. I love, love, love, the creaminess of this. It reminds me of body butter and I would actually call this body butter. I applied this to my skin and it left it moisturized and feeling smooth. This really quenches the skin in the winter.

The only negative is that this comes packaged in a box. There is no need to wrap this cream in a box. To me that is wasteful. Also, when it is shipped, that is another box, over the product's brown box, to ship it out.

At the current price of $15.29 ($17.99 minus 15%), this is competitively priced for a thick 6.7 ounce tin of thick body cream that is more like body butter.

title: Mildly hydrating but I can’t get past the color of product; it looks like molasses and coffee
text:
The color in these bottles and tub is a turn off to me. I like my shampoo and cream rinse to be clear or creamy white--preferably clear. I was almost afraid this was going to change the color of my hair. However, the shampoo lathers up nicely with a white lather. The conditioner is not overly hydrating--just enough for my fine curly hair. I did not try the masque because I do not need intense moisturizing.

I do like the results but the color of the product is such a turn off that this is not something I would order again. If it were not for the color, I would have rated this 4.5 stars. The Shea Moisture products are wonderful  but this ensemble is just not for me. Also, the current price of $23.49 ($27.63 minus 15%) comes to $7.83 per item.

title: Fragrance lackluster; moderate lather; moisturizing
text:
There are four bars of soap in the sampler box of macadamia, blue almonds, activated charcoal, and coffee and cocoa. None of the soaps smell anything like their names. In fact, the fragrance is subpar and lackluster.

I tried the macadamia bar and it lathered moderately. I do feel this soap is moisturizing and that is the nicest feature.

These soaps are on the soft side and are not made to last too long. At the current price of $23.95 ($25.95 minus $2), this comes to almost $6 per bar, which is expensive but still competitively priced.

title: Large oval brush that glides & detangles my hair, wet or dry; best for fine hair
text:
First of all, I love the color of this brush. It is marbled with variations of pink, blue, green, yellow, purple, and teal. It goes well with both my pink and purple bathroom.

The brush is large. It glides through my hair wet or dry and detangles it as well. It also feels great in my hands and does not slip out like some brushes do. Note that I have fine short to medium curly hair. The nylon bristles on this brush are thin and very pliable, so I do feel that this works best with fine hair and not thick hair.

I love this brush; however, the current price of $9.99 is a bit pricey as brushes like this can be purchased in my local Home Goods for half that.

title: Nail clippers have an exceptional cutting edge; file just okay
text:
This set includes one very sharp toenail clipper, a small glass file, and a carry pouch.

The nail clipper feels great to hold and cuts exceptionally well. In fact, I am surprised at how well. I have very hard nails on my big toes, so much so that I feel as if I need an industrial wire cutter to clip my nails. This clipper cut the nail easily.

The file works but I do not like glass files compared to the stand sandpaper type files. Also, the sanding area is small. I was able to wash off the nail dust when I was finished but I am not impressed with the file.

The current price of $11.99 is competitively priced for this set.

title: Small lightly fragrant bath bombs; performance mediocre; bomb dissolved in 10 min
text:
[[VIDEOID:bb5edda514909261ac36f99d8cf04678]] There are 12 individually wrapped small bath bombs in this set in different fragrances. The fragrances are subtle and are rose, coconut, mint, lavender, lemon, strawberry, green tea, rosemary, lily, peach, orange, ocean.

The bombs dissolve in about 10 minutes but the suds only hold for about 8 minutes; at least in a foot bath. The bath fragrance is mild and lasts the same amount of time. I tried the lily bomb and it dissolved into lemon-colored water.

Since I personally do not like the color rings caused by bath bombs in my bath, I used this in a foot bath. The color of this bomb, which was a flourescent yellow, did not adhere to my skin, my foot bath, or my towels-- at least the color of the lily one I tried.

In summary, these are not the best performaing bath bombs around but they are nice. The current price of $29.99 is really expensive for this as it comes to $2.50 per small bath bomb which, considering the performance, is about double what I would expect to pay.

title: Barely fragrant bath bombs with surprises inside; zero performance--a total dud
text:
[[VIDEOID:6f9dd63ada8df8a61f673f2263ce1a59]] At the current price of $29.99, I had high expectations for this bath bomb set. It comes with six bath bombs (lemon, grape, strawberry, orange, apple, and blueberry). In addition there is a small change purse, a nice pink super thin marker pen, and a bracelet. Each bath bomb has a surprise inside.

I tried the grape bomb in my foot bath. As soon as I opened the bomb, it fell apart as can be seen in the photo and the gift popped out. The fragrance was okay but nothing to cheer about. The fizz was almost non-existent and within 30 seconds (after my video was done) I just had purple water and nothing else. The little necklace in the surprise was the nicest part of the bomb. I am thoroughly disappointed as every other aspect of this set is great.

In summary, the performance of these bombs is a dud as the fizz is instanteneouly gone and there are no suds; it's just colored water. Yes the suprises are nice but at an expensive $5 per bomb, they forgot to deliver on what makes a bath bomb special--long-lasting suds, nice fragrance, and fizz. Also, no child wants their bomb to fall apart before it even goes in the bath.

title: Like a true SPA shower experience; love the intoxicating fragrance blend but pricey
text: At the current price of $40 for 16 ounces of body wash, this is expensive as it comes to $2.50 per ounce. However, the blend of warm vanilla, tonka bean and cedarwood with a hint of pepper makes showering with this like a SPA experience. The fragrance is wonderful. It washes well and feels moisturizing as well. This provides an intensely luxurious shower experience that is intoxicating to my senses. I love it.

title: Nice brush / blender set; bristles stay put
text:
This brush set comes with two small foundation/cheek powder brushes, two blending sponges, and a large brush for applying translucent powder or bronzer.

The two smaller brush heads do have a slight paint smell to them that will wear off. The bristles stay put and they are perfect for applying powder blush.

The large brush comes with its own snap-closure plastic case to keep the brush from smudging the rest of the products in my make-up case. That brush is great for dusting on translucent powder or bronzer. I prefer using it with powders only or for blending on the entire face.

The two egg-shaped blending sponges are great for liquid applications. They are soft and of medium-density. I also like the neutral colors.

The current price of $10.98 means each piece comes to $2.20 per item for this 5-piece set.

title: Decent medium hold; nice fragrance - 3.5 stars
text: This light foam styling mousse provides a decent medium and all-day hold. I do like that my hair did not look sticky after using this but I usually prefer thicker foams.  The current price of $25.11 ($27 minus 7%) is on the high side of competitively priced.

title: Hydrating face cream; leaves a barrier on my skin; do not care for tan color
text:
This face cream is thick and moisturizing and perfect for winter and fall. It has a nice fresh scent that I am unable to describe but which I like very much. The only negative to me is that I do not like the tan color of the butter. Otherwise, this is great. I applied this to my face and neck and it left a barrier on my skin. It left my skin feeling moisturized and protected.

At the current price of $51, this is pricey for 1.69 fluid ounces.

title: Like a true SPA shower experience; love the intoxicating fragrance blend but pricey
text: At the current price of $40 for 16 ounces of body wash, this is expensive as it comes to $2.50 per ounce. However, the blend of oriental rum, coffee, and sandalwood makes showering with this like a SPA experience. The fragrance reminds me a bit of ZEST soap but more elevated. It washes well and feels moisturizing as well. This provides an intensely luxurious shower experience that is intoxicating to my senses. I love it.

title: Intensely hydrating vegan cream; smells lemony
text: This is a small jar of intensely hydrating vegan cream. I use this on my hands and it absorbs well but leaves a slight barrier on my skin. Even though they say this is for the face and body, I personally would not use this on my face because it feels too hydrating for that. I love this, which is surprising because I rarely love vegan creams.

title: Thick and creamy; leaves my face and neck super silky but I do not care for the fragrance
text: This face moisturizer is thick and creamy and left my face and neck feeling super silky. I absolutely LOVE the results. However, I do not like the fragrance and that, besides the high $69 price, is the only reason I rated this 3 stars.

title: Lightly scented; lathers and cleans well
text:
There is one standard-size bar of soap in this package. This has a light aroma that barely smells like tea tree oil to me but that is not a bad thing. This lathers and cleans well. It is also slightly moisturizing. This bar should last me about one week.

The current price of $6.99 is pricey but competitive for this. Note it also comes with one mesh soap bag.

title: Good disposable nail buffers for a salon or for travelling
text:
During COVID, these are great for manicurists who want disposable buffers to use with customers. It is also great for just someone who wants to take a few of these traveling with them. These do not have to be disposable as I am able to use mine several times.

Each mini buffer has a coarse (pink) and not so coarse (black) side. They are small but they do the job.

The current price of $7.99 for 50 mini buffers comes to almost $.16 cents per buffer which is reasonably priced.

title: Medium-weight cream that is wonderfully moisturizing & has a great fragrance
text: I never tried or heard of 100% pure morocco argan oil butter lotion. This comes in a one gallon jug. The biggest negative is that it takes work to dispense the lotion. However, it is wonderful. It is of medium to light-weight consistency and absorbs into my skin quickly. It leaves my skin feeling silky, smooth, and incredibly hydrated. I also love the intense fragrance. This is a great year-round lotion. Also, the current price of $29.74 ($34.99 minus 15%) is reasonable for this as it comes to $.23 per ounce.

title: Smells like old lemon but soak is soothing; feels tingly; I use as a hand soak
text:
This lemon and ginger epsom salt has a slightly unpleasant lemon fragrance that smells old to me. I used 1/4 cup to about 8 cups of warm water to soak my hands to reduce swelling and aches. This worked well and was soothing. Of course, since my hands are always in water, the essential oil and epsom salt in this provides a tingly or slightly burning feel---like rubbing salt in a wound. However, that should not be typical if one does not have such raw hands.

There are about two to four servings in this 15-ounce package depending on how much is used. They recommend no more than half a cup for a full standard size bath for the first use.

The current price of $7.99 is pricey but competitive.

title: Menthol-like fragrance is too strong for me; sort of burns; I use as a hand soak
text:
This peppermint and eucalyptus epsom salt has a strong menthol-like fragrance which is too intense for me. Nevertheless, I used 1/4 cup to about 8 cups of warm water to soak my hands to reduce swelling and aches. This worked well but the fragrance was difficult to inhale. Also, since my hands are always in water, the combination of the oils and salt made my skin feel like it was burning. It was almost like I had cuts on my hands and there was salt in the wounds.

There are about two to four servings in this 15-ounce package depending on how much is used. They recommend no more than half a cup for a full standard size bath for the first use.

The current price of $7.99 is pricey but competitive.

title: Fragrant and soothing; feels tingly; I use as a hand soak
text:
This lavender epsom salt has a nice but strong fragrance. I used 1/4 cup to about 8 cups of warm water to soak my hands to reduce swelling and aches. This worked well and was soothing. Of course, since my hands are always in water, the essential oil  and epsom salt in this provides a tingly or slightly burning feel---like rubbing salt in a wound. However, that should not be typical if one does not have such raw hands.

There are about two to four servings in this 15-ounce package depending on how much is used. They recommend no more than half a cup for a full standard size bath for the first use.

The current price of $7.99 is pricey but competitive.

title: Astronomically expensive bobby pins; they have a great hold
text:
I really love these pins. There are only five bobby pins in this package but they are stylish/decorative pins. They hold my hair tight and work exactly like a bobby pin, except they are a little bit thicker.

The only reason I took off one star is because of the astronomical price. Most bobby pins are no more than $.04 or $.05 cents each and these are $1.40 each pin at the current price of $6.99. These may be great pins but they are too expensive to justify the cost. I would rather purchase a more decorative pin with glitz rather than something like this at that price. I personally feel these should no be priced at more than $.40 or $.50 cents per pin

title: Pins have air space in-between; these are roller pins & not actual bobby pins
text:
There are supposedly 100 pins in this package; I did not count them. I did not realize these had an airspace in-between the pins. These are the type of bobby pins used with rollers (a.k.a. curlers) and not the type for an updo. I tried this around a lot of hair and they would not hold because my hair is too fine. I cannot use these but because I did not pay attention to the photo, that is my fault. They hold the hair very loosely or cause the style to fall out when using loose pins like these. I think they are perfect for rollers, however, because they will go over the roller easily.

The current price of $3.83 comes to $.04 cents per pin.

title: Nice, small nail clipper set; file is a bit short handled
text:
This set includes two sharp nail clippers, one small and one large, with a file embedded into the handle of each clipper. It also includes a small metal file with a short handle and a nice case with snap closure.

The nail clippers are comfortable to hold and cut well. The file works nicely too and I usually do not like metal files; however, it has a very small handle which makes it difficult to work with.

The case is attractive. However, the current price of $15.99 ($19.99 minus 20%) is on the high side of competitively priced for this set.

title: This protected me for about 6 hours
text:
I usually use nothing but Old Spice Swagger solid with the active ingredient of aluminum zirconium tetrachlorohydrex gly 17%. This Dove solid has no aluminum and only plant-based ingredients. Usually, products like these only last me about 2-3 hours; however, the protection lasted about 6 hours for me and definitely not the 24-hours specified.

I take a shower every 12 hours because I sweat a lot, so I can never attest to 24-hour protection. This is Eucalyptus scented but I have to put my nose to the stick to detect any scent and it is only slight--neither offensive or great to my senses.

This works better than other non-aluminum deodorants I tried previously. The current price of $24.14 ($28.40 minus 15%) comes to an expensive $8.05 per 2.6 ounce solid stick as this is a 3-pack.

title: Basic blow dryer that works well; comes with concentrator only; pricey
text:
At the current price of $57.84 this is a pricey blow dryer but it is also a nice one.

In the box is the blow dryer unit, a user pamphlet, and a concentrator. Besides the RESET button on the plug, there are five selections/buttons ( ON/OFF button, lock button to set the temperature, temp up and down selections, and snowflake selection for cool air). Pressing the ON/OFF button turns the dryer on and off. A quick press of the snowflake selectio, turns on the cool air. Toggle it off to turn on the heat. The lock button in the front of the handle, locks the wattage setting during blow drying so that no accidental changes occur.

The cool wattage settings cycle through 140W, 160W, 180W, 200W and 220W. The hot wattage settings cycle through 420W, 690W, 1100W, 1500W, and 1875W.

This dryer dried my hair well. Note that there is a burning smell on first use but that wears off. This is typical of some blow dryers.

The concentrator screws on and pulls off the unit easily.

Note that the cord is not a swivel cord but I find that is not needed.

In summary, I do love the white color of this dryer and its simplicity. A smidgen of finish was scratched off on mine but not enough to reduce the beauty of this dryer. I do feel, however, that the current price is a bit too steep for this. I have tried other Hot Tools blow dryers in the past and was not overly excited about them; however, I like this one the best so far.

title: Decent mini-liquid foaming soap bottles; turns my regular liquid soap into foam; pump a bit tight
text:
There are 35 60ml (2.029 fluid ounces) empty foaming pump soap bottles in this set, all in a pale pink. This works well as designed. The bottles have a wide mouth and they are easy to fill. These are perfect for crafters who make their own soap or just to use personally by turning regular soap into foaming soap.

Based on my Internet search, bottles like these imbue the soap with air as a result of going through the pump dispenser.

The current price of $22.99 for 35 bottles comes to $.67 cents per bottle. The pump is a bit tight or takes pressure to press but that is the only negative.

title: Very fragrant & soothing hand lotion; leaves my hands silky; way too pricey & not refillable
text:
There are three small pocket-sized tubes of lotion in this package in coco cooler, fig fizz, and carrot kick scents. The lotion is of medium thickness, absorbs quickly. and leaves my hands feeling super silky.

The package says that this is ready to refill and I just do not understand that. Even after I pulled off the top, I do not see any way to refill such a small bottle. That's the first negative. The second is that this is so expensive at $32.90 which comes to $10.97 per travel-sized bottle of only 1.69 fluid ounces each. They say that 20% of profits fund water projects in developing countries. Unfortunately, I always had a belief that one should not buy a product because part of the profits go to a good cause. However, that is only my opinion.

This hand cream is very nice and lovely. The scents are nice too. However, this is too expensive and not refillable, in my opinion.

title: Simple but heavy blow dryer; works well
text:
For the current price of $41.39 ($45.99 minus 10%), this blow dryer is a good deal.

In the box is the blow dryer unit, a user guide, two comb concentrators (one with a comb front that is called a smoothing nozzle and the one attached without it), a diffuser, a velvet carry bag, and a blowdryer barrel brush.

Besides the RESET button on the plug, there are three buttons ( ON/OFF button and temp/wind up and temp/wind down). A long press of the ON/OFF button turns the dryer on and off. A quick press provides cool wind (recycle icon) and another quick press provides heat. The wind speed goes from 50 to 99 and the hot wind goes from 50 to 90C (122 to 194F).

The tools snap on and off the head of the unit easily. I originally thought they screwed on but discovered that was not working and snapped them on instead.

Note that the cord is not a swivel cord but I find that is not needed. The only true negative to me is that the unit is heavy.

In summary, I love the results this dryer provides. It dried my hair quickly and beautifully without the frizz. I have short to medium fine curly hair and it looked good after using this. I love the simplicity of this unit.

title: Pump bottle DOES NOT pump; shampoo is very nice but if I can’t get to it, forget it
text:
I hate nothing more than a product that either does not work or that I cannot get to. The pump on this bottle never opens and I tried three different times for over 20 minutes. I absolutely HATE this.

I had to remove the top to pour it out of the bottle. As a shampoo, it has a nice fragrance and lathers and cleans well. I have fine curly hair and my hair dried without relaxing the curls too much, so that was nice. As a shampoo it gets 4 stars but being able to get to the product gets 0 stars and the high $27 price 1 star--hence the 2-star rating.

title: This is both a beautifully designed and functional file
text:
There is one beautifully designed double-sided file in this package with a rope loop for hanging. The handle is long and feels great to hold. The black side of the file is the coarse side and the brown side the fine pumice. I actually was unable to tell the difference between the two sides until I looked at the Amazon site. They felt both the same to me.

Nevertheless, this works well and has a great reach. The current price of $9.99 is reasonable for this as well. This is definitely a keeper.

title: The fragrance is divine; detangles well
text:
My favorite thing about this spray is the wonderful fragrance. It is a pleasure to use.

I sprayed this on my damp hair and then used my fingers and then a pick to detangle. It worked well and left my hair smelling wonderful.

The current price of $11.99 is competitively priced for this.

title: Gorgeous electric blue wig; a bit thin & not easy to affix to thin hair but curls & length are great
text:
This wig has many uses. Of course, it is perfect as a regular wig except it is a bit thin; I would have preferred it thicker. The wisps of hair in the front is a bit difficult to deal with as well as getting it on a person with very fine hair. Nevertheless, this does work well once affixed appropriately. It is also great as part of a costume or even when dressing up a mannequin.

The hair is soft and I just love the curls and the color. The length is also super attractive as it comes to the middle of my back. If this were thicker and easier to put on a person with thin fine hair, then I would have rated this 5 stars.

title: Super cheap small plastic flower clips w/mild hold
text:
These clips are small and made of a super cheap plastic like the plastic prize one gets out of a gumball machine. The clips are not easy to open because it is hard to get leverage on the edge of the clip that is lined up with the dip (hole in the flower). If it were in a position where the flower piece comes out it might be easier to open.

There are also two cheap elastic hair ties included.

At the current price of $8.99, I am not impressed with this ensemble. A young girl might like this but from a quality standpoint, one can purchase better.

title: These make great stocking stuffers or Easter basket gifts; blenders are great
text:
This is a lovely set of two hot pink sponges, both with a flat side. I love these sponges, particularly because they have a flat angled side. The sponges are of medium density. The flat side is great for smooth applications. These feel good in the hands, blend reasonably well, and feel soft against my skin. These blenders make a great gift for the make-up obsessed. I love that the sponges do not smell. I tried other colored sponges and they smell like pencil shavings or other chemicals and these do not. The hot pink color is also attractive, at least until make-up discolors then.

The sponges themselves are similar in style to all of the others that I tried before.. To me what set of sponges to buy all comes down to the price and the angles one wants on the sponges as well as whether it is for gifting or not. The colors are important too - at least to me.

At the current price of $6.38 this comes to $3.19 each which is on the pricey side. Blenders like these can be purchased for less than $1 each and they are just as good. This was the only reason I took off one star.

title: I use this as a skin moisturizer; the label can be confused w/olive oil which is a NEGATIVE
text:
This is a 6-pack of 4 fluid ounce bottles of oil that can be used as a make-up remover or body oil for moisturizing. I use this as a moisturizer. It glides on my skin and absorbs quickly. The fragrance is wonderful but it dissipates immediately, which is a negative to me.

Note that this arrived leaking through the box even though it is packaged in plastic. Another negative is that the bottle is labeled OLIVE OIL. If someone does not read what this is, it is possible this could be mistaken as actual food grade olive oil. Vendors need to think of this when they come up with the packaging and wording.

The possibility of this having a mistaken identity is huge and for that I give it 1 star. The moisturizing ability I give 4 stars. The fragrance 5 stars but I lower that to 3 because it goes away immediately and leaves my skin smelling like oil. The current price of $5.52 ($6.49 minus 15%) comes to $.92 cents per bottle which I consider very reasonable and a 5-star price.

It's a good moisturizer and leaves my skin soft and hydrated. Just do not put it in the cabinets with the food. I do not use this for make-up.

title: These bandages have many uses; sticks to itself and not to skin or fur; not only tattoo grip tape
text:
These bandages have many uses. There are 6 black rolls that are individually wrapped and each roll is 5 yards apiece and 2 inches tall. These self-adhere as the bandage is wrapped around a hand, leg, arm, etc. This sticks well to itself. The stretch allows this to be used like kinesiology tape with the exception that one cannot shower with this successfully and each wrap is for one-time use. There are just so many useful possibilities besides using this as tattoo grip tape. Tattoo grip tape is used to cushion the grip on tattoo grip tubes to provide the artist with a more comfortable grip.

The entire roll does not have to be used at once as it depends on the amount needed. This is perfect to use as a lightweight version of a carpal tunnel brace by wrapping it around a bad wrist, hand, and thumb as I did in the photo. It does not stick to my skin nor to a pet's fur, which is wonderful. It is also versatile enough to wrap around the handle of a tennis racquet to get a good grip or an umbrella or cane handle.

In summary, this is not only good as tattoo grip tape. I feel these are good bandages to also have in one's medicine cabinet. At the current price of $8.09 it comes to $1.35 per roll which is double the price of other brands. These are really self-adhesive bandages rebranded as tattoo grip tape. When it is labeled as a self-adhesive bandage, the price is a little cheaper.

title: Functional blush brush with no bristle shedding; would have preferred long bristles
text:
This is a nice foundation brush. It works well for applying powder blush. The brush feels great in my hands--although I do wish it had a silicone grip on it. The bristles do not shed and the head provides good coverage. I do wish the bristles were just a little bit longer or perhaps angled. The bristles are soft against my skin. In general, this is a decent foundation brush.

The current price of $8.27 ($8.99 minus 8%) is competitively priced.

title: Nice curly hair shampoo and conditioner trio; did relax my hair just a tad
text:
I have short to medium-length fine curly hair and am always looking for a curl shampoo. This set is good. I tried this both with their wash out and leave-in conditioner.

The fragrance is nice, which is a plus for my senses. All three items are thick and creamy. The shampoo lathers and cleans well. I air dried my hair and it dried curly but slightly relaxed, moisturized, and fragrant. At the current price of $12.74 ($14.99 minus 15%) this comes to $4.25 per product.

title: The large size is best for someone with big hair; very basic caps & pricey
text: There are six caps in this package in two of each color (purple, blue, and pale pink). I ordered the large ones and realized I should have ordered the mediums or smalls. This looks like a chef's cap on my head. However, the elastic holds around the base. These are very basic caps that are slightly a step above disposable caps. I do not feel these should be more than $.75 cents each; however, at the current price of $9.99 they are $1.67 each which is high. Nevertheless, these work as designed. I just recommended ordering a smaller size unless one has big hair.

title: The fragrance is okay & does not match their shampoo but the results are good
text:
I have short to medium-length fine curly hair and am always looking for a curl conditioner. This one is pretty good.  I used this with their complementing [[ASIN:B09GTX8NXW  shampoo]]. I love their shampoo ; however, this conditioner does not have the wonderful intense fragrance of their shampoo even though it has the same "flavor."  However, it lightly conditions without weighing down my hair. As a result, my hair dried bouncy and curly and looked great. It smells great too but that is thanks to the shampoo and not this conditioner. Had the scent of this conditioner been the same as their shampoo, this would have received 5 stars from me.

The current cost of $9.53 ($11.21 minus 15%) is competitively priced.

title: The fragrance is deliciously divine and the results are excellent
text:
I have short to medium-length fine curly hair and am always looking for a curl shampoo. This one is great. I used this with their complementing [[ASIN:B09GTW7N1H conditioner]].

The fragrance is deliciously divine and intense, which makes this a pleasure to use. It lathers copiously and cleans well. I air dried my hair and it dried all bouncy, curly, and just overall lovely and fragrant. I would definitely buy this shampoo at the current price of $9.28 ($10.92 minus 15%).

title: Creamy white serum that absorbs rapidly & leaves my face & neck silky; love the citrus scent
text:
This serum is more hydrating than it is firming. Nevertheless, I love it. The citrus scent is wonderful. I love the pump bottle. I also love that the serum is a cream white of medium consistency. It is perfect in all seasons. I applied this to my face and neck and it absorbed easily and left my skin feeling utterly silky.

The current price of $26.40 is reasonable too.

title: A great deodorant that is comparable to my Old Spice Swagger I love; but it is scented
text:
I love this deodorant. I usually use nothing but Old Spice Swagger solid with the active ingredient of aluminum zirconium tetrachlorohydrex gly 17%. This Secret solid has aluminum zirconium pentachlorohydrex gly 18%. Based on my Internet research, it appears both ingredients are the exact same thing but just another name for it.

I take a shower every 12 hours because I sweat a lot, so I cannot attest to the 24-hour protection--I never can. However, it definitely lasts me until my next shower.

This does say it is unscented but if I put my nose to the stick, it actually has a lovely fresh scent. To me this is a BIG plus but others might not be happy about that. Therefore, this is not unscented as it claims. Nevertheless, I love this deodorant so much, I'm not making it down for those claims.

The current price of $17.80 ($20.94 minus 15%) comes to a very reasonable $2.97 per 2.6 ounce solid stick as this is a 6-pack . I may just switch from Old Spice to this once I'm done with my stash of that.

title: Bobby pins are too small and difficult to handle; comes in a nice tin
text:
These bobby pins come in a very nice tin the size of a deck of cards. There are four packages of 50 pins each; I did not count them. Unfortunately, other than the tin, I dislike this set.

They are too small to open. I had so much trouble trying to pry the pins apart, that they kept flying out of my hands. If one can get a grip on the pin, they hold marginally well. My recommendation is to buy their [[ASIN:B09KX3XPZM larger]] size bobby pin; those I love and rated 5 stars. These I cannot recommend.

The current price of $8.99 with the storage tin is competitively priced. Since there are 200 bobby pins in this container, it comes to almost $.05 cents each.

title: Attractive set of 4 Haitian soaps; honey of Moringa is the last ingredient in every bar - 3.5 stars
text:
I never heard of Moringa oil nor have I ever had a product from Haiti. This soap's last ingredient is "honey of Moringa," which I assume is Moringa oil.

There are four 100-gram (3.527 ounce) bars and all but one is green in color. The citrus, lavender, and leaf powder are all green and the baby roots powder is white. I like the fragrance of the citrus and lavender bars but not so much the other two. The etched design on the bars is very nice and is most likely an etching of the Moringa tree.

The soap lathers and cleans well. I must admit that I was very confused by the Amazon title and unsure if this is a face soap, hand soap, or skin soap since it had everything in the title. I believe this is a face soap that can be used as all-purpose soap.

The current price of $23.75 comes to $5.94 per small bar. I give this set 3.5 stars rounded down to 3 stars.

title: Excellent bobby pins; not too large and not too small; the perfect size in a nice tin
text:
These bobby pins come in a very nice tin the size of a deck of cards. There are two packages of 50 pins each; I did not count them. They are sturdy and hold well. I have had bobby pins that are a bit larger and are flat. These are more of medium size but bigger than the standard size and work very well for an updo.

The current price of $8.99 with the storage tin is competitively priced. Since there are 100 bobby pins in this container, it comes to $.09 cents each.

title: I did not notice any difference to my face or neck after using this
text:
There is a small tin of gel mask in this set along with the eyedropper serum. I do not like the gel mask at all but that is because I do not like gel masks in general. Therefore, my review rating is based on the serum.

The mask takes about 30+ minutes to dry and is not easy to peel off. So this is not for me.

The serum is not easy to get into the dropper. I had to try a couple of times. Nevertheless, I tried this for several days over my face and neck and under my eyes. It is safe for the eye area. My face felt smooth but did not look tighter or any different. I also did not like that I had to add moisturizer on top of this. I figured this would suffice but that is not recommended.

Overall, this is not for me. The current price of $46 is pricey for something that I do not feel delivers the results I expected. It is just okay.

title: Love the bath salts and foaming bath; eye mask is too tight and it's not adustable
text:
I love the smell of roses and that is what this set reminds me of. This set contains four items and they are 16 ounces of Rose Scented Epsom salt bath salts, 5.7 ounces of foaming bath, 1 ounce of rose potpourri, and one attractive pink eye mask.

I love the bath salts and the foaming bath. The fragrance is great. However, the eye mask is not adjustable and just constricts around my eyes which is bothersome. The dried rose petals are okay but not fragrant.

The current price of $15.83 ($19.79 minus 20%).

title: Not sharp or tight enough for cuticles; best for cutting price tags off clothes
text:
I ordered these due to the 5-star reviews and unfortunately, these are subpar. They cut paper fine and the plastic price tags off clothes. However, they do not cut cuticles well at all. The handle has a lot of play in it so I used a screwdriver to tighten the center screw. That still did not help much. I recommend them for cutting thread and other small tasks but not for what they were intended. There is nothing premium about these cuticle scissors.

The best part of this ensemble is the leather case.

title: Cream is as solid as a rock; like Turtle Wax for cars
text: I kept running my warm fingers over the solid "cream" and was able to get a whisper of cream on my finger.  What I did use was very good but this reminds me of Turtle Wax for cars. If this were more easily spreadable, I probably would have rated this 5 stars. Since it is almost impossible to extract any product to use, it is disappointing to me.

title: Lightweight cream that glides on easily & absorbs quickly
text:
When I opened the jar, it looked like it was half full with empty air space to the bottom.

I tried this on my face and neck after a shower. The cream is slick and glides on easily. It is extremely lightweight which is not what I was expecting. However, it absorbs quickly and leaves my face extremely hydrated once it dried. I feel this is a good summer cream and I don't feel like one has to have eczema to use it. Note that I do not have eczema on my face but I have had other places on my body; therefore, I cannot tell how well this works for face and neck eczema.

The current price of $19.99 for 2 ounces is a little pricey but still competitive.

title: Highly fragrant large bath bombs; suds & fragrance lasted 20 min; also moisturizing
text:
[[VIDEOID:5767631d4ab61d86931148d6279b1f26]] There are 12 individually wrapped large bath bombs in this set in different, unnamed fragrances. There is also a plastic cutter to remove the plastic wrapping on the bomb.

The bombs dissolve in about 8 minutes and the suds hold for about 20 minutes; at least in a foot bath. The bath fragrance is strong and lasts the same amount of time. My entire room smelled fantastic. I tried the mixed yellow/green colored one and the fragrance was wonderful. Also, my skin felt moisturized after using these.

Since I personally do not like the color rings caused by bath bombs in my bath, I used this in a foot bath. The color of this bomb, which was a flourescent yellow, did not adhere to my skin, my foot bath, or my towels-- at least the color of the rose one I tried.

The current price of $19.79 ($21.99 minus 10%) comes to a reasonable $1.65 per bomb.

title: SUPREMELY FRAGRANT small heart bath bombs; suds & fragrance lasted over 20 min
text:
[[VIDEOID:c9a38fddf332ee96bd8b766d904736ff]] The bombs dissolve in about 10 minutes and the suds hold for over 20 minute; at least in a foot bath. The bath fragrance is strong and lasts over 20 minutes. My entire room smelled wonderful. I tried the violet-colored one and the fragrance was incredible.

Since I personally do not like the color rings caused by bath bombs in my bath, I used this in a foot bath. The color of this bomb, which was an electric purple, did not adhere to my skin, my foot bath, or my towels-- at least the color of the rose one I tried.

The current cost of $19.99 comes to $2.50 per bomb, which is expensive for such a small bomb but I consider it worth it due to the wonderful performance.

title: Slightly coarse bristles that work up a good lather with soap
text:
This brush has two ends. The larger end is for the entire face and the smaller end is for precision areas like around the nose. The bristles are not as soft as I expected but they are not too hard either; I would consider them slightly coarse. As a result they are exfoliating.

Since the bristles are densely packed, it is easy to work up a good lather but not as easy to clean if using on a face full of makeup. This does the job it is supposed to do.

At the current price of $9.49 ($9.99 minus 5%), this is a competitive online price.

title: Moisturizing, not-exactly scentless soap with decent but slippery lather
text:
Although this soap is supposedly scentless, it is not exactly without an aroma. It smells a little bit like Castille soap, which I am not crazy about. However, it lathers and cleans well and also feels moisturizing but the suds are a bit slick.

The current price of $9.87 is expensive for one bar but it is competitively priced.

title: Love the colors and softness of these make-up sponges; perfect for an Easter basket
text:
This is a lovely set of three blending sponges in bright colors. At the current price of $9.99, however, it is overpriced at $3.33 each. Most blender sponges of similar quality are half this price.

These are all hourglass sponges which are good for blending or any large make-up application.

These feel good in the hands, blend well, and feel soft against my skin. These blenders make a great gift for the make-up obsessed. I love that the sponges do not smell. I tried other colored sponges and they smell like pencil shavings or other chemicals and these do not.

The sponges themselves are similar to all of the others that I tried before this and are on the soft rather than dense side. This means they soak up more liquid than others do. To me what set of sponges to buy all comes down to the price and the angles one wants on the sponges as well as whether it is for gifting or not. The colors are very important too--at least to me as I am color obsessed.

title: Extremely sturdy wands; passes through my mascara tubes easily; great for eyebrows too
text:
For the current price of $8.99, which comes to $.3 cents per wand, I thought this was going to be close to garbage. However, I am pleasantly surprised.

The wands are very stiff and sturdy. They pass through my mascara tubes easily and work well during application. I particularly love these for my eyebrows as I have bushy eyebrows.

There are 300 wands in 6 compartments of one carry case with 50 of each color.

title: Stunning clips with a great hold; very stylish
text:
There are eight boxy claw clips in this package. The clips are absolutely stunning with their marbleized look. They are medium-sized and well-made. They grip my short to medium fine curly hair perfectly and really hold on. They would work even better with longer hair.

At the current price of $9.49 it comes to a very reasonably priced $1.19 per clip. The quality of these clips is excellent and they are beautiful as well.

title: Not a professional brush set but very functional; use written on handles; no mascara wand
text:
I ordered this to actually see if this was a professional set but it really is not. Nevertheless, this set is very functional.

There are 12 make-up brushes in this set and the use of each brush is written on the side of the handle, which I love. Note that the Amazon picture shows a mascara wand but no such "brush" is included. There are 12 brushes but this is not one of them.

This is an attractive brush set especially since the brush tips are red. The bristles are soft. There was no shedding. Their soft bristles feel great against my skin and work like many other brushes I tried previously.

This set has all the brushes I needed except for a fan brush and lip liner brush. The brush heads do have a slight smell to them; they smell like paint, which I do not care for. The current price of $25.89 comes to $2.16 per brush and I am not counting the pink silicone exfoliator that was thrown in. There are other brushes on the market similar to this that are slightly cheaper. I took off two stars due to the price, lack of mascara brush that was advertised in their photo, and the fact that this is NOT a professional set.

title: Great for cleaning vegetables or picking up pet hair; definitely not skin exfoliating
text:
I do not care for this as a bath brush but I love it as a vegetable cleaning brush. The brush is very pliable and is gentle on my vegetables because of that. I tried one on my skin and did not feel it was sturdy enough to have any effect as a massager or skin exfoliator. This also works well as a dry brush to pick up pet hair off a couch or other flat surface. Therefore, this is 5 stars as a vegetable or pet hair cleaning brush and 2 stars as a skin exfoliator.

Note that a cheap wash mitt is included in the box but to me it is just cheap junk.

The current price of $8.99 is also a bit pricey for this as a 2-pack can be purchased [[ASIN:B093PWHGHP here]] for $14.99.

title: Almost like a clay; very thick & hydrating but leaves a barrier on the skin
text:
I rubbed this into my face and neck after a shower. It is super thick and pasty and does not fully absorb but leaves a barrier on the skin. It is perfect for night. My face feels super hydrated after using this.

The fragrance smells a little bit like unrefined Shea butter, which I do not care for. However, I really like the results of this cream, so I'll put up with that. If it were more creamy and less pasty, I would have rated this 5 stars.

The current price of $24.89 is competitively priced for this.

title: Lightweight cream that absorbs easily and moisturizes lightly; has a light coconut aroma
text:
This is a lightweight cream that absorbs easily and moisturizes lightly. I applied this to my neck after a shower. It is perfect for summer and I like the light coconut aroma.

Note that the top has a protrusion to give the illusion that one is getting more cream than they actually are. There is only 1.69 ounces in this jar and it comes in an oversized box. The current price of $12.95 ($14.95 minus $2) is certainly very reasonable for this cream.

title: Lightweight cream that absorbs easily and moisturizes lightly; do not care for smell
text:
This is a lightweight cream that absorbs easily and moisturizes lightly. I applied this to my face after a shower. It is perfect for summer; however, I do not care for the smell. It smells like unrefined shea butter. If I liked the smell this would have gotten 4 stars.

Note that the top has a protrusion to give the illusion that one is getting more cream than they actually are. There is only 1.69 ounces in this jar and it comes in an oversized box. The current price of $14.95 is certainly very reasonable for this cream.

title: Excellent scentless soap; I use this as is but it can be used to create one’s own fragranced soap
text:
There are two one-pound mounds of soap in this package that can easily be cut down into 5 to 7 bars of soap per pound depending on the width. I use this as is. It is scentless, cleansing, and moisturizing and has a decent lather.

However, one can melt this down with their own essential oils and other ingredients to create customized bars of soap. At the current price of $19.95 this comes to $9.98 per pound. I get about five little more than half inch bars of soap per pound, which comes to $2 per bar. Although I love scented soaps, I like that this soap base has simple ingredients and works well without all the fragrance.

title: Excellent scentless soap; I use this as is but it can be used to create one’s own fragranced soap
text:
There are two one-pound mounds of soap in this package that can easily be cut down into 5 to 7 bars of soap per pound depending on the width. I use this as is. It is scentless, cleansing, and moisturizing and has a decent lather.

However, one can melt this down with their own essential oils and other ingredients to create customized bars of soap. At the current price of $18.95 this comes to $9.48 per pound. I get about five little more than half inch bars of soap per pound, which comes to $1.90 per bar. Although I love scented soaps, I like that this soap base has simple ingredients and works well without all the fragrance.

title: WOW, this cream is incredible; left my hands silky & hydrated
text: This cream is really incredible. I applied a little to my hands and it absorbed immediately and left my hands ultra moisturized and super silky. The current price of $24.95 is expensive for 4 ounces but this cream is so good that I didn't deduct any points for the high cost.

title: Well-made dual-head back brush with long handle
text:
This brush is two-sided. I was skeptical as to whether I would like this brush or not because the photo on the Amazon site does not do this justice.

The clear bristles are soft and the vanilla-colored ones are more coarse. The handle is long, so it provides me with a good reach. This brush is sturdy and is perfect for soaping up my back. The clear handle is also attractive and has ridges on it for a good grip. In addition, there is a loop for hanging.

In summary, this is a great dual-headed back brush with long reach and exfoliating bristles. The current price of $13.99 is a bit steep but this brush is really nice so I did not deduct any points for the high cost. I particularly love the look of the handle and the quality of the bristles on the brush heads.

title: Excellent facial razor with moisturizing strip; new strips must be purchased separately
text:
This facial razor is excellent and simple to use. It comes with the unit itself, a charging base, a USB cable but NO A/C adapter, a cleaning brush, and a manual. Mine was almost fully charged to 100%. The center of the blade has a moisturizing strip that can be replaced but new strips must be purchased separately.

Operation is simple. Just press hold the power button until it turns on. There are two speeds. Tap the power button again to change the speed to high. It keeps a tally of the running time and will turn off after 15 minutes of use. It needs to rest for 60 seconds before powering on again. The head is easy to remove for cleaning and lubrication.

There is supposedly a child lock feature but I did not understand how to engage it. It says to press and hold the button for 3 seconds. I am not sure what button they are talking about unless they mean the power button.

Nevertheless, this razor works well and is sleekly designed. So far I am impressed. The current price of $37.99 ($39.99 minus 5%) is competitively priced.

title: Moisturizing soap with decent lather; charcoal is my least favorite
text:
There are three bars of soap in this set (charcoal aloe, hemp mint, shea butter citrus). I love the fragrance of the charcoal soap but do not like the black lather. Shea butter is my favorite. It lathers pretty well and cleans well but also feels moisturizing.

The current price of $19.97 comes to $6.66 per bar.

title: Sleekly designed automatic hair curler but not easy to feed hair into the chamber
text:
This automatic hair curler is sleekly designed and very attractive. Unfortunately, it does not work as well as I expected for my medium length hair in the back of my head. I just could not get the hair to feed in the chamber easily and the instructions are not clear on how to do this. The Amazon site is a better guide. I feel this type of curler is best for someone with long and straight hair.

In the box is the curling unit, USB cable (but no A/C adapter), user guide, crushed velvet carry satchel, a teaser comb, and two clips.

I charged the unit less than 30 minutes before first use because it arrived fully charged. Note that the box instructions are wrong with regard to the buttons.

POSITIVES
- Unit is sleek and attractive

- Temperature can be shown in Celsius or Fahrenheit by setting with adjustment key

- Temperature setting goes from 150-200C or 300-390F

- Curling rotation can be left or right--use adjustment button to set. It says it can be mixed but I did not see that option.

- Turn the unit on by "hold pressing" the ON/OFF button; this prevents accidental operation

- Operation is simple once the hair is in the chamber; just press the start button and release to stop process when done

- A nice carry satchel is provided

NEGATIVES
- Previous temperature, rotation, and timer settings are NOT remembered once the unit turns off - THIS IS A BIG NEGATIVE TO ME

- It's difficult to feed the hair into the chamber

- Unit beeps a lot which is annoying

- The box instructions are wrong as it reverses the on/off and adjustment buttons in the diagram

- Instructions are written in broken English

In summary, this is a nice unit with simple operation but only those with long straight hair will achieve the most benefit. There are a few quirks that make this disappointing, particularly the fact that my settings are not remembered once I turn off the unit. Also, it is not easy to feed hair into the chamber. Other than this, this works as designed. The current price of $36.99 is competitively priced for a unit like this.

title: Moisturizes & absorbs quickly; not crazy about the pump mechanism
text:
This cream comes in a pump jar as shown. I press down on the top and then I use my fingers to apply even though this looks like a thick roll-on. The thick cream goes on easily and absorbs quickly. My face and neck felt moisturized. However, I prefer creams that come in jars I can dig my fingers into as I always feel there is a lot of moisturizer lost with a pump dispenser. The current price of $37.99 is pricey but competitive.

Note that the cap on the jar arrived cracked even though the box was not damaged.

title: Like a hydrating lip gloss with color
text: This reminds me of a colored Vaseline I tried a long time ago but it is not sticky. It has a light pink tinge to it, goes on glossy, and is highly hydrating. If it did not have color and it was $12 instead of the current high price of $24, this would have received 5 stars.

title: Thick, hydrating cream; takes a while to absorb and dries slightly tacky; love the jar
text:
This cream is thick and more of an opaque white. It is scentless and goes on easily. I applied this to my face and neck and it took about 5 minutes to absorb; however, it never fully absorbed and left a slight tacky feeling behind. Nevertheless, my face was extremely hydrated and this provided a protective barrier on my skin. I consider this more of a winter lotion.

What I love the most about this is the jar it comes in. Everything is hinged including the interior protective cap. There is also a plastic applicator provided. If this cream did not dry tacky, it would have received 4 stars. If it were also cheaper than the current $65 and it were not tacky, it would have received 5 stars. I expect a cream like this to go for $45 or less and not dry with a tacky feel.

title: Superb blow dryer for home use; less so for a professional due to cord length; pricey
text:
[[VIDEOID:60dfadf785cef4c3a72d3fb92bca2063]] For the current price of $169.99 ($219.99 minus $50), this blow dryer is expensive. In its current condition, it should be priced around $115--see dislikes.

In the box is the blow dryer unit, a user guide, two concentrators (small and large), and a diffuser.

Besides the ON/OFF button and RESET button on the plug, there are 4 icons with a total of 8 LED selections available:

- blow dryer icon - fast dry mode; high air/temp; there's only one LED corresponding to this feature

- mid - middle air/temp for first LED; middle air/high temp for second LED

- low - low air/temp for first LED; low air blow/middle temp for second LED

- recycle or circular air flow icon is the cool/hot air alternating mode that blows various temperature cool air for 5 seconds then hotter air for 7 seconds; the first LED is low air/ temp; the second LED is middle air/temp; and third LED is high air/temp; however, pressing this button all the time dispenses cool air continuously.

FEATURES I LIKE:

- Unit is extremely lightweight--great for both professionals and home users

- Unit folds with the touch of a button and turn of the handle but it cannot be stored in the case that way

- The concentrators magnetically attach to the unit with ease

- The diffuser easily screws on and off the unit

- The unit comes with a nice case that zippers easily

- It has negative ion technology which reduces frizz and allows hair to retain its natural moisture

- The cap on the business end easily screws off for cleaning

MY DISLIKES:

- High price

- Cord is not long enough for professional use unless the chair is close to the socket. The cord from tip-to-tip is 7 feet long but I feel a 9-10 foot range is better, especially at this price.

- The cord is not a swivel cord

- Per the box, this is Model MS3002 which is1300W and not 1400W as the Amazon title currently states and also not 2000W as their video states

In summary, I love the results this dryer provides. It dried my hair quickly and beautifully without the frizz. I have short to medium fine curly hair and it looked like my hair was salon styled after using this. I love that the dryer is lightweight and that it dries my hair quickly. I also love that the attachments attach and detach with ease. I would have preferred a swivel cord. Since this is for personal use, I do not care about the cord length. However, a professional would usually require a cord that is 9-10 feet for comfortably styling their customers. If one can work with 7 feet, then this is a nice dryer. The wattage is mislabeled on the Amazon site as I believe what is written on the box is correct but I have no way of knowing for sure. The price is also a bit steep. Certainly this is the best dryer I ever had the pleasure of using even if it is not perfect.

title: Non-irritating and cleansing; nice foaming net supplied; wish soap had more fragrance
text: There are two femine wash bars in this set along with two soap net bags that are very nice and help generate a lather. The bars are not really fragrant and I would have liked more fragrance. However, they are non-irritating and cleansing. I also love the color of the bars as they match my pink bathroom.

title: Produces brown lather; feels exfoliating & moisturizing but I had to it throw out - SEE UPDATE
text:
SEE UPDATE BELOW

After trying this, this is not a soap that I would order again. The main reason is because I do not care for the brown colored lather that comes off of the soap. The bar does feel exfoliating and I found it to be moisturizing in the sense that it took a bit to wash off because my skin felt oily. It is okay but is not for me. The list price of $9 is pricey too; however, the current price with the 35% discount comes to a competitively priced $5.85 per bar.

UPDATE - Even though I kept this soap on a silicon brush that drained the liquid, it kept breaking apart and became a soppy mess. This soap breaks off into little pieces that kept going down the drain. I had to throw it out. I absolutely hate this soap.

title: Bulky mesh puffs whose puffiest section creates copious suds
text:
Mesh buff puffs are the only thing I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. The full mesh area is similar to the ones I buy except these have an extra section or sections to look like a Christmas tree and snowman.

The Christmas tree loofah is actually a stretchy back puff. The other one is the regular puff. Both work but they are a bit bulky to use. I like the snowman one the best because I can use the top part as a handle while washing with the lower puff. After trying these, this is okay but not ones I would ever order again.

The current price of $8.59 comes to an expensive $4.30 each puff.

title: Very functional brushes(16) but brush heads have slight smell; brushes stand up; LOVE color
text:
There are 16 make-up brushes in this set. This is an attractive brush set especially since the handles are purple and match my bathroom. The bristles are soft. There was no shedding. Their soft bristles feel great against my skin and work like many other brushes I tried previously. I like that they stand up (see photo); however, they are easy to knock over so that negates the purpose of that ability. I actually had them produce a domino effect by accidentally tipping over the brushes.

This set has all the brushes I needed except for a fan brush and lip liner brush. The brush heads do have a slight smell to them; they smell like paint, which I do not care for. The current price of $15.99 ($16.99 minus $1) is a decent buy as this comes to $1 per brush.

title: Cheap dollar store combs; work as designed but will break easily
text: These combs are so cheap that they feel like they are from the dollar store. They work as designed but I feel like they won't last. Just combing through my hair makes it feel like the tines will break. The current price of $8.99 is too much for this as it comes to $2.25 per comb. I would not expect to pay more than $.75 cents per comb based on the quality.

title: Very nice moisturizing lip balm in 6 flavors; love the rose flavor
text:
This is very nice lip balm. It goes on smoothly and is moisturizing. I felt like it provided a nice, somewhat waxy barrier on my lips.

There are six flavors (rose, coconut, peppermint, vanilla, lime, and orange ginger). Since I never heard of rose lip balm, I had to try that one. It definitely smells and tastes like rose.

The current price of $12.99 ($13.99 minus $1) is a competitively priced $2.17 per tube.

title: Nice set of creams, bubble bath, etc. in an advent calendar
text:
There are 24 items in this calendar extending from Dec 1 to Dec 24. The "doors" to the calendar are not easy to rip open, so the calendar looks sloppy unless one is careful to "score" the perforations before opening.

The 24 items included are:

- 1 Christmas keyring

- 2 0.7 fl oz of body lotion (lemon and raspberry)

- 3 1.2 fl oz of foot cream (berry bliss, jasmine, and coconut macaroon)

- 1 medium bath bomb in the shape of a tree

- 2 shampoo bars each in a tin (fragrances unknown but in red and yellow and not for colored hair)

- 8 0.7 fl oz of hand cream (jasmine, coconut macaroon, 2 raspberry, berry bliss, lemon, grapefruit, and eucalyptus mint)

- 1 1 oz berry bliss candle in a tin

- 2 1.7 fl oz shower gel (candy cane and jasmine)

- 2 1.7 fl oz bubble bath ( ocean breeze and eucalyptus mint)

- 2 0.7 fl oz body scrub (ocean breeze and candy cane)

There really is not much in this set insofar as product. Also, nothing has a flip top cap, so the product is not always easy to dispense. Also, one of the body wash containers leaked even though it was sealed. In addition, the product listed on the back does not match with the insert in the box. For instance, it lists 8 hand cream on the box but the insert says 6 hand cream.

I tried the foot cream which is lightweight and nice; I like the Jasmine version. I also tried the body scrub of which there is only enough for one partial wash. There is not much scrub to it and there is absolutely no lather; I felt waxy afterward. I also tried the bubble bath. That has a nice lather but the fragrance of the one I tried (ocean breeze) was not enticing.

In summary, this is a nice set to be purchased more for the surprise of what is behind the day in an Advent calendar around Christmas time but the product amount is limited and the performance of some items are lackluster. The current $19.99 price tag is competitive.

title: Small attractive clips with a great hold; very stylish
text:
There are four small metal claw clips in this package and they are stunning. They are sturdy and well-made. They grip my short to medium fine curly hair perfectly and really hold on tight.

At the current price of $9.99 it comes to a reasonably priced $2.50 per clip. The quality of these clips is excellent and they are beautiful as well.

title: Nice gift set with a few cheap items; a bit pricey - 3.5 stars
text:
At the current price of $40.18 ($42.49 minus 5%), this set is a bit pricey for what it is. I feel anything over $35 is a bit much for this especially since there are a couple of cheap items included.

In the box is:
- 1 small package of lavender with a burlap bag

- 1 50ml (1.691 fluid ounces) jar of skin toning cream - this cream is lovely, lightweight, and moisturizing but there is not much of it.

- 1 50g (tiny bar) of french lavender handmade soap which is very nice

- 1 50g lavender candle; also very nice

- 1 super cheap razor that I consider almost garbage

- 1 white microfibre face towel that I also consider almost garbage because it is so thin

- 1 tube of lip balm - this balm melts easily but is very nice and moisturizing

- 1 pair of white bed socks

- 1 pair of purple exfoliating gloves

- 1 shower steamer

- 1 tiny bath bomb

- 1 15ml jar of orange bath oil for the bath - the scent is very nice

- 1 15 ml jar of eucalyptus bath oil for the bath - the scent is nice and not overpowering

- 1 15 ml jar of lavender bath oil for the bath - the scenter is very nice

Note that there was a wet spot on my box but I could not tell what bath oil item it came from. In total there are 11 items but I consider 2 junk, so to me there are only 9 items which comes to $4.46 per item if excluding the 2 lousy ones.

I already used several of the items (cream, lavender sachet, and lip balm and do like them very much. I honestly wish they removed the razor and cloth and gave more of the other items.

Overall, this is a nice set but the inclusion of the razor and cloth cheapen the set because they are so substandard.

title: Decent rough skin grinder; cap does not stay on unit
text:
I have a foot grinder that has barrel-shaped pumice stones and I like that one better than these thin disk shaped surfaces. This unit comes with the grinder, three heads (smooth, medium, and coarse), a cleaning brush, a USB cable w/o any AC adapter, and some curved white plastic piece I have no idea what to do with. There is also a cap on the grinding head that continually falls off the unit.

I just charged this with the supplied USB cable until it reached 100%. I then held down the on/off button for a couple of seconds until the unit turned on and applied it lightly to the heels of each foot. It did a good job. I held the on/off for a couple of seconds to turn it off. I then rinsed everything off under water. The grinding head and body can be rinsed with water.

It did a decent job. What I do not like is that it is not easy to pull the grinding head and insert another one. I have to get a good grip on the head to remove where the indentations are. Second, the cap does not stay on the unit and there is no mention of what the white piece is. Lastly, except for the fine head, I feel the "holes" in the other grinding heads reduce its effectiveness. I still prefer my [[ASIN:B08G477XQS barrel grinder]] over this one.

The current price of $21.99 is reasonable, however.

title: Tingles going on and left me with what looked like a sunburn
text: I used this on my face and neck and it tingled going on. I waited 15 minutes before washing off. The results were terrible. My entire face looked like it had a severe sunburn (see close-up photo of redness on my skin). It took three hours for the redness to go away. I must be allergic to the ingredients.

title: Light scentless moisturizer; label on bottle in Korean only plastic packaging in English
text:
This is a lightweight, almost scentless moisturizer for the face and body. It absorbed quickly into my skin and left if feeling hydrated and soft. The only thing I do not like is that the bottle label is in Korean. Only the plastic packaging includes the English ingredients.

Also, the $32.99 price tag for 10 ounces is outrageous.

title: Marvelous body butter; thick and moisturizing; lovely scent; SPF not listed
text:
This body butter is incredible. It is thick and moisturizing and absorbs quickly. The scent is lovely too. After using this my skin felt incredibly silky and hydrated. Also, the current price of $11.01 is reasonable for this. The only thing I don't like is that the jar is oversized for the amount within. When I opened the jar it looked like one third of the product was gone. Note that there is only 6.8 ounces of product in this large container.

Since I do not stay out in the sun or have UV damage, I cannot say if this is protective as there is no SPF listed on the package. This is the only reason I took off one star.

title: Stunning clips with a great hold; very stylish
text:
There are four claw clips in this package. The clips are absolutely stunning with their marbleized look and very sturdy. They are medium-sized and well-made. They grip my short to medium fine curly hair perfectly and really hold on. They would work even better with longer hair.

At the current price of $8.27 ($8.99 minus 8%) it comes to a very reasonably priced $2.07 per clip. The quality of these clips is excellent and they are beautiful as well. They even come in a nice protective box perfect for gifting.

title: Set of 12 travel 3-in-1 cotton sets; nice case
text:
There are 12 individually packaged sets of 10 cotton balls, 100 swabs, and 10 cotton squares. The cotton balls are small but work well and the cotton squares are good for toner. The cotton swabs are excellent and sturdy but because one side has a pointing tip, it is more for make-up application or precision nail polish removal than for the ears.

I love that each set comes with a sturdy plastic case.

The current price of $26.91 ($29.90 minus 10%) comes to an expensive but competitively priced $2.24 per set.

title: Good medium-sized buff puffs that create copious suds but pricey
text:
Mesh buff puffs are the only thing I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. These are medium-sized and similar to the ones I buy at Walmart for $2 each. There are four dual-colored puffs and they work like any other large mesh loofah I regularly use. I really like that they are not wound too tight or too loose; it is enough to generate good suds..

The current price of $13.99 comes to an expensive $3.50 each puff. If these puffs were more reasonably priced, they would have gotten 5 stars from me.

title: Fragrant bar of mint soap; moisturizes and lathers lightly
text: This soap has a lovely mint fragrance; I do not smell the cardamom. It is lightly moisturizing and lathers lightly as well. I really like this soap.  However, the current price of $10 for this one bar of soap is way too expensive in my opinion. It is a very nice soap but still not as good as my all time favorite which is [[ASIN:B007OC7E2E Shea Moisture Three Butters Men's Utility Soap]] that is half the price.

title: Beautiful & functional brush; large coverage and no bristle shedding
text:
This is an impressive and beautiful foundation brush. It works exceptionally well for dusting translucent powder over the face or applying a bronzer. The brush feels great in my hands--although I do wish it had a silicone grip on it. The bristles do not shed and the head provides great coverage. It is also soft against my skin. I can even use it to apply blush as long as I want wide coverage.

The current price of $10.39 ($12.99 minus 20%) is competitively priced.

title: Absorbs quickly; leaves my face hydrated; almost scentless; I dislike color
text:
I have an aversion to creams that are anything but white and this one has a custard color to it. It is not staining or anything like that but I never like colored creams.

This cream is thick. I applied it to my face and neck and it was absorbed in seconds. My face felt hydrated after use. The cream is almost scentless but the color is a turnoff to me. The current price $33.25 ($35 minus 5%) is competitively priced. If the cream were white, I would have rated this 4 stars.

title: Arrived with broken pump on one bottle; fragrance lovely; lotion lightweight
text:
This is a lightweight body lotion. There are two heavy 10 ounce pump cans in this package. Unfortunately, one arrived with the pump broken.

I love the poppy (i.e. tangerine and lily) fragrance. The lotion is lightly moisturizing and leaves my hands silky. Overall, this is a nice lotion but they must package this better for shipment. Luckily, I can use the other pump when the one bottle is finished.

title: Provides nice powder blush/foundation coverage; bristles stay; smaller than expected; has case
text:
This brush is a work of art and I really like it. It comes with its own snap-closure plastic case to keep the brush from smudging the rest of the products in my make-up case.

The brush provides good blush and powder foundation coverage. I prefer it for powder but it also works with liquid. I also love that the bristles do not fall out. The only negative is that this is smaller than I expected. I wanted to use this for finishing powder but a larger brush is more suited to that. Other than this, this brush is lovely.

However, the current price of $9.79 ($10.79 minus $1) is competitively priced.

title: Small, tightly-wound buff puffs that must loosen up to create copious suds
text:
Mesh buff puffs are the only thing I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. These are small-sized and very tightly wound. There are four puffs and they do not create a good lather compared to my larger mesh and more loosely-wound loofahs I regularly use. I wanted to love them but I do not, although they should get better as they get older.
