The current price of $9.99 comes to an expensive $2.50 each puff; these are expensive because they are so small and not as good as others I tried. Note they also pack them so tight into the plastic bag it comes in that it looks like two puffs.

title: Absorbs quickly; leaves my face firm and hydrated; fragrance okay; too pricey
text:
I have an aversion to creams that are anything but white and this one has a peachy salmon color to it. It is not staining or anything like that but I never like colored creams.

This cream is thick. I applied it to my face and neck and it was absorbed in less than one minute. My face felt hydrated and firmer after use. The scent is okay but not one I particularly like. Also, the current price tag of $76 is a bit steep for this cream especially since the color and fragrance are not my favorite.

title: Assemble, add water, shake & 4 ounces turns into 16 ounces of soap per refill; lather not great
text:
In an over packaged box is one plastic bottle and two tiny four ounces of concentrated soap. I just twisted the soap bottle onto the empty bottle, squeezed out the liquid, added 12 ounces of water to the 16 ounce fill line, shook the bottle, and used it.

The fragrance of the soap is perfumy, strong, and lovely to my senses. The lather, however, is lackluster.

I like the idea of reducing waste but the packaging it comes in is very wasteful. Also, the end product is not as good as their regular Dove soap. After having tried this, I am disappointed in the results. I like a lot of lather and this does not deliver.

title: Excellent large-sized buff puffs that create copious suds; comes with 4 hooks
text:
There are four large and colorful mesh puffs in this set in summer colors of light blue, green, yellow, and pink. In addition, four stick on hooks are included.

Mesh buff puffs are the only thing I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. These are large-sized and similar to the ones I buy at Walmart for $2 each. There are four puffs and they work like any other mesh loofah I regularly use. I notice no difference in sponge quality or performance over my typical Walmart sponges. However, I do love the colors and the addition of the hooks is a nice touch.

The current price of $13.70 ($14.89 minus 8%) comes to an expensive $3.43 each puff if not counting the hooks or $2.74 per item if including the package of hooks as one item.

title: Good medium-sized buff puffs that create copious suds
text:
Mesh buff puffs are the only thing I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. These are medium-sized and similar to the ones I buy at Walmart for $2 each. There are four puffs and they work like any other mesh loofah I regularly use. I notice no difference in sponge quality or performance over my typical Walmart sponges.

The current price of $14.96 comes to an expensive $3.74 each puff which is somewhat pricey.

title: Moisturizes & absorbs quickly; not crazy about the pump mechanism or smell
text: This cream comes in a pump jar as shown. I press down on the top and then I use my fingers to apply even though this looks like a thick roll-on. The thick cream goes on easily and absorbs quickly. My face and neck felt moisturized. However, I do not care for the chemical scent of the cream nor the pump. I prefer jar creams I can dig my fingers into. I also feel the $40.99 price tag is outrageous even though this supposedly has SPF 30 in it. Since it is winter here, I have no idea how well the SPF works.

title: Six cheap clips that work as designed
text: There are six banana clips in this package. The clips are very cheap and feel like they will break easily. Nevertheless, they do work to hold the back of my hair. At the current price of $11.99, it comes to $2 per clip which I feel is very expensive for the quality.

title: Thin and a bit wrinkled; good for someone with very long hair; a bit slippery
text:
There are four polka dot ponytail scrunchies with tails (forest green, black, burgundy, and white). The material is thin and is very wrinkled. Because the material is a polyester type, it does slip out of shorter hair. These are good for someone with long and not medium-length hair like I have. I consider these just okay. They work as designed but are not the best quality.

The current price of $6.50 ($12.99 minus 50%) comes to $1.62 each which is competitively priced.

title: Good cuticle trimmers for the price & colorful too
text:
There are three cuticle trimmers in this package. For the current price of $8.99 this comes to $3 each which is a reasonable online price.

I tried one pair on my nails and they cut the cuticles well. I am also able to cut easily along the side of my nails. I would not call these top-notch professional trimmers but they are of decent quality. I also love the lime green color of the set I got.

title: Nice selection of 7 scrunchies; material can be slippery on hair; long hair required
text:
There are seven "autumn-colored" scrunchies in this set. The material feels like polyester, so it is a bit slick which increases the chance these will slip out of the hair. I have medium length hair in the back and these stay in my hair but will fall out if I just pull a little bit on them. These are best for long ponytails.

I do feel these are really attractive and I do love the size. The current price of $8.99 comes to a competitively priced $1.28 each.

title: Under eye cream / NOT eye cream; moisturizes but does nothing else
text:
When I quickly ordered this, I thought this was eye cream. The package says eye cream and so does the pump bottle. However, it is under eye cream. I applied as per the directions under my eye from the inner to the outer corners. I already used this several times and all I notice is that it is moisturizing. It did nothing for the bags or dark circles under my eyes.

I was looking for a full eye cream anyway but am still disappointed that a product currently priced at $68 is just moisturizing and nothing else.

title: Beautiful & functional brush; large coverage and no bristle shedding
text:
This is an impressive and beautiful foundation brush. It works exceptionally well for dusting translucent powder over the face or applying a bronzer. The brush feels great in my hands--although I do wish it had a silicone grip on it. The bristles do not shed and the head provides great coverage. It is also soft against my skin. I can even use it to apply blush as long as I want wide coverage.

The current price of $11.60 ($12.89 minus 10%) is competitively priced.

title: Decent blow dryer but attachments are "sticky" when removing & cord is not a swivel cord
text:
For the current price of $59.99, this blow dryer is expensive. However, it works well with only one exception and that is that removing the attachments are not as easy as they should be. In the box is the blow dryer unit, a user guide, a concentrator, and a diffuser.

Before first use, the red button on the plug has to be pushed in or it won't turn on. There are three controls on the front. The cool shot button is more like a cool shot toggle. The middle button is the high, medium, and low for the heat. There is also a high, low, and off for the speed, which is the last button.

Installing the attachments is a cinch but removing them requires a bit of a wiggle. The cord is NOT a swivel cord which is another negative. Nevertheless, this dried my hair well without any static.

In summary, this is a nice blow dryer but it's not perfect. If the attachments were easier to remove, the cord was a swivel cord, and it was listed about $10 cheaper, then I would have rated this 5 stars.

title: Feels like liquid marshmallow; doesn’t absorb; also do not care for the light green color
text: I never like creams that are any other color than white. This is a light green. The consistency going on my face and neck reminds me of spongy liquified marshmallows. The cream also stays on top of the skin and does not absorb; therefore, my face feels tacky until I wash it off. Personally, I do not care for this vegan cream at all.

title: The hand creams are wonderful and the soap is moisturizing but soft; love the creams the best
text:
This set gets 4.5 stars from me. There is one 30ML tube of day hand cream and one tube of night hand cream. There is also a bar of detoxifying hand soap and a carry pouch.

The creams are wonderful. The day cream is a little lighter than the night cream. Also, the fragrance is lovely. The soap I do not care for as much as the cream. The bar is soft but it lathers well and is a bit oily / moisturizing. I felt it took a little longer to wash off the oily feeling than a normal bar of soap.

Two things that would make this set five stars is for the bar to be harder and less oily and for the hand creams to have flip top caps.

The current price of $9.99 for this quality set is competitively priced. Personally, I could do without the soap. I would love to buy a larger tube of each one of these hand creams because they are excellent; however, I do not see them on Amazon yet.

title: Definitely provides a hydrating barrier to my face and neck; lightweight; good for the summer
text: This is a nicely scented barrier cream that is perfect for the summer because it is lightweight. I applied this to my face and neck and it leaves a moisturizing barrier on the surface of my skin that I can feel. I actually like this cream and the scent is pleasing to me. My face felt incredibly hydrated after using this. Of course, I do prefer creams that soak in instead of leaving a "film" on my skin; however, this is what it claims to be--nothing more and nothing less.

title: Attractive travel brush; no bristle shedding but brush moves too much in the handle
text:
This is an attractive travel foundation brush. It works relatively well (see negative) with blush or highlighting. The brush feels good in my hands, the bristles do not shed, and the head provides decent coverage. It is also soft against my skin. Since this is a travel brush, it slides in and out of the tube flawlessly. My only issue is that the brush wobbles a bit in the hollow handle when it is in its fully opened position. I do not feel like I have a solid brush in my hands because of this.

The current price of $7.70 is competitively priced for this brush.

title: This is only shampoo & no conditioner; fragrance is SUPER INTENSE
text:
This is just shampoo and no conditioner. It is supposed to be a moisturizing shampoo but I found it to be super cleansing and I had to use my own conditioner after washing with this. Also, the fragrance is SUPER INTENSE. I love fragrance but the aroma is just okay but very strong and I do not care for that. It lathers extremely well, cleanses well, and leaves my hair feeling squeaky clean. I have short to medium fine curly hair and it did not weigh down my curls. Had the fragrance been better and the product was what it claimed to be (shampoo and conditioner), this would have gotten 5 stars.

The current price of $16 ($20 minus 20%) for a 10.1 fluid ounce bottle is on the high side of competitively priced.

title: This applicator is excellent due to the textured surfaces & long handle; 2 textures / 2 sizes
text:
This lotion applicator comes with several non-slip bathtub strips, four different heads in two sizes and two textures, and a handle.

Years ago I purchased two of these type applicators and originally hated them due to the Styrofoam cup feel to them. However, this one is the same except the applicator area is textured which helps lotion to adhere better and it doesn't feel like I'm applying lotion with a Styrofoam cup.

As a result of the raised surface, this lotion applicator is excellent and it has a long handle. There is only one head with a waffle texture on both sides. The other three heads come with a slightly textured surface. I personally prefer the waffle cut because it holds lotion better. In addition, one of the four heads is a tiny version of the slightly textured surface.

The handle is long enough to provide a full reach of my back from the top and the bottom. The rope loop allows me to hang this. It is also easy to clean except for the ridges around the applicator.

The current price of $12.49 ($13.88 minus 10%) is competitively priced.

Unfortunately, I find that these almost last forever. I still have my two other applicators that I use daily and they have not broken or become worn yet and I have them about 8 years already.

title: Fragrant but feels like it is burning my skin; I use as a hand soak
text:
I tried several of their other fragrances and find them hit or miss. This tropical fragrance is wonderful but it is strong with the eucalyptus oil and almost menthol-like making this difficult to inhale. I use this as a hand soak instead of a body soak and my skin felt like it was burning. It was almost like I had cuts on my hands and there was salt in the wounds.

There are about two to four servings in this 16 ounce package. I used about a half cup.

The current price of $11.99 ($12.99 minus $1) is expensive. This is not my favorite soak as I prefer the  [[ASIN:B07797LLNL Vitabath Lavender Chamomile Epsom Salts]]  instead.

title: Lotion leaves my skin silky; fragrance is okay but PUMP is AWFUL
text:
This body lotion is over packaged and comes in a box which comes in another box. The pump is separate. After I installed the pump, it took me over five minutes to get the top to pop up. I was ready to give up. Nevertheless, it finally opened and I was able to pump out some lotion.

The lotion is thick and creamy and absorbs quickly. It also left my skin feeling great. The fragrance is okay but not great to me. The current price of $14.67 for this 8 fluid ounce pump bottle is competitively priced. I actually took off one star for the okay fragrance and one star for the lousy pump.

title: Really cleans and then softens my hair w/o weighing down my curls
text: This  shampoo and conditioner smells nice. I particularly like the citrusy fragrance of the shampoo. The shampoo is clear and lathers extremely well. It also cleans deeply. The conditioner is mild.  My hair dried soft and my curls were not weighed down. This is a nice shampoo and conditioner combo. There is some tea tree oil in this but it is toward the end of the ingredients list and there is no tea tree aroma---thankfully. The current price of $19.99 is a reasonable price for this duo.

title: Excellent large-sized buff puffs that create copious suds that are perfectly wound; love the colors
text:
Mesh buff puffs are the only "sponge" I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. These are large and similar to the ones I buy at Walmart for $2 each. There are four puffs and they work like any other mesh loofah I regularly use. They are wound perfectly meaning the mesh is not too loose and not too tight.

I absolutely love the colors of these puffs. They remind me of summer.

The current price of $14.99 ($15.99 minus $1) comes to an expensive $4 per puff and is the only reason I rated these 4 stars.

title: Really cleans and then softens my hair w/o weighing down my curls; tea tree is the middle ingredient
text:
This tea tree and peppermint oil shampoo and conditioner does not smell like the ingredients. It has a nice fragrance but tea tree oil is in the middle of all the ingredients in both products.

I love the shampoo. It is clear and lathers extremely well. It also cleans deeply, almost like a detergent. The conditioner is mild.  My hair dried soft and my curls were not weighed down. This is a nice shampoo and conditioner combo; however, do not expect any hint of tea tree oil or peppermint aroma.

title: Like moisturizing with petroleum jelly mixed with paraffin wax; best for winter only
text: This looks like Vaseline and spreads like a thinner version of petroleum jelly mixed with paraffin wax. I put it on my face and neck after a shower and even after 30 minutes it still has not absorbed. It actually puts a protective barrier on the skin. After having tried this, I would only use it in winter when my face and neck is super dry. However, this is not a skin sauve I would order again. I personally prefer thick creams.

title: Vibrating facial brush; it does not spin
text:
For the current price of $20.9 ($29.90 minus $9 off), this is an okay facial cleansing tool.

IN THE BOX:
- Cleansing "ball" with one brush head attached
- USB charging cable
- Flat, sleek stand with charging port
- Three cleansing brushes in total (thick brush, thinner soft brush, and silicone pad)
- User guide

I charged this for 30 minutes. In order to use it, I had to remove the cover on the ball base and press the power button on the bottom center of the ball. There are three vibration modes of low, medium, and high.

I do not find the vibration useful. I expected a brush that rotated and this does not. Every other facial wand I tried before has a rotating brush. It is for this reason that I don't really like this. It looks beautiful and is functional, but is a disappointment to me.

Note that the instruction manual is super basic and has grammatical errors.

In summary, I really love the style of this unit. It is very artistic and elegant looking. I love that everything is discreet as they pack a lot of style into a small package. It is also nice that the cover has air holes in it so the brush can dry. However, without a rotating brush, it is not very useful and becomes more of a vibrating massager than a facial cleaner.

title: This applicator is excellent due to the textured surface & long handle; too many heads
text:
This applicator is excellent due to the textured surface and long handle. Years ago I purchased two of these type applicators and originally hated them due to the Styrofoam cup feel to them. However, this one is the same except the applicator area is textured which helps lotion to adhere better and it doesn't feel like I'm applying lotion with a Styrofoam cup.

The handle is long enough to provide a full reach of my back from the top and the bottom. The rope loop allows me to hang this. It is also easy to clean except for the ridges around the applicator. In addition, the current price of $15.99 is on the high side of competitively priced for this.

I find that these almost last forever. I still have my two other applicators that I use daily and they have not broken or become worn yet.

title: Thin if using a ½ sheet; thick if not; great for toner
text: There are 40 double sheets in this set. One sheet can be separated into two at the perforation but then it is too thin, in my opinion. I use each double as one sheet to apply toner. These work well but I still prefer my cotton rounds a tad better. Insofar as the claims that this saves water, I do not believe it nor understand that. In addition, the current price of $8.99 ($9.99 minus 10%) comes to almost $.23 cents per double sheet which is a bit pricey.

title: Acts as a light facial moisturizer; good for the summer; almost scentless
text:
This moisturizer dispenses easily with the pump bottle. It is lightweight and absorbs quickly on my skin. It is a good summer cream for my face and neck. I do detect a whisper of the product's aroma but for the most part, it is scentless. It is a very nice cream, although not my absolute favorite.

The current price of $42.99 is a bit pricey for this in my opinion. Note that this comes from Korea and the writing on the bottle is all in Korean. However, there is an English sticker on the side of the box.

title: Lathers and cleans well and has a lovely orange fragrance; price is steep
text: This is packaged well in shrink-wrapped plastic with a plastic collar that prevents the pump from engaging in shipment. The soap lathers and cleans well and has a lovely orange fragrance; however, the current price of $15.99 for an 11.8 fluid ounce bottle of soap is steep. This is the only reason I rated this 4 instead of 5 stars.

title: Fragrant bath bombs with 4-min suds & color staining
text:
[[VIDEOID:8cf2e6e7a96ab00f323c2c8bcfd4f6cd]] There are 12 individually wrapped regular size bath bombs in this set in 9 fragrances. They all do not smell as I expect but I still like that the aroma is strong. The fragrances are:

- Rose (essential oil is Rose)
- Chamomile (essential oil is Geranium)
- Perfume (essential oil is Lemon)
- Bluebell (essential oil is Jasmine)
- Water of Life (essential oil is Lavender)
- Lemon Green Tea (essential oil is Lemon)
- Neroli (essential oil is Neroli)
- Eucalyptus (essential oil is Eucalyptus)
- Milk and Vanilla (essential oil is Rose)
- Freesia & Mint (essential oil is Mint)
- Natural Honey (essential oil is Bergamot)
- Freesia (essential oil is Neroli)

The bombs dissolve quickly in about 4 minutes and the suds hold for the same time; at least in a foot bath. The bath fragrance is strong. I tried the rose one and the fragrance was good.

Since I personally do not like the color rings caused by bath bombs in my bath, I used this in a foot bath. The color of this bomb, which was an electric pink, adhered to my skin and my towels. It did not stain my foot bath; at least the color of the rose one I tried.

The current cost of $15.99 comes to $1.33 per bomb, which I consider reasonable for this size. However, the bombs lackluster performance and the color staining is a negative to me. These are giftable based on the package it comes in. I also love that the bombs are fragrant even though they don't necessarily smell like what they are. I also have no clue what the 12 +1 means on the Amazon site. There are only 12 bombs in this set and nothing more. One thing I really like is that the bombs do not have an internal shrink wrapped plastic that I have to remove. I only have to untie the twist tie and remove it from the package.

title: No tea tree oil smell; lathers well, feels moisturizing, but nothing special
text:
There are three 3.52 ounce bars of soap in this package for the current price of $19.54 ($22.99 minus 15%), which comes to a pricey $6.51 per small bar.

I tried this and it lathers well and feels a bit moisturizing or oily. However, it does not WOW me. Also, there is absolutely no tea tree oil aroma. In addition, all the writing on the package is in Korean except for the words on the front that says "Control BHA Soap."

title: Lovely cherry almond fragrance; moisturizes & absorbs well but expensive  - 3.5 stars
text: This is a lovely body oil. I do really like the fragrance which smells like cherry almond to me. The oil absorbs well and gives my skin a glow without feeling overly greasy. The only negative is the outrageous price of $59.99 ($64.99 minus $5) for 3.4 ounces. I am skeptical of the claims that this is anti-inflammatory. It is good oil but there are other moisturizers on the market that are equally good and not so expensive. If this were $30 or under, it would have received 5 stars from me.

title: Requires 3 AAA NOT included or must use USB cable; magnification too much - 3.5 stars
text:
This mirror is big and bulky. It is too large for a vanity mirror hanging off of one's medicine cabinet. There is a battery compartment in the back that requires three AAA batteries. It can also be powered by the supplied USB cable but no A/C adapter is included.

To secure this via the suction cup, the base feature has to be turned counter clockwise and then turned clockwise to secure to the surface. There is an on/off button on the back that has to be pressed in to activate the on/off button on the mirror on the front. Once the button on the back is ON, then touch the circle on the front of the mirror to light the rim. The light is dimmable with a long touch.

The mirror angle can be rotated due to the ball and socket base.

The magnification is 10x so the image is really enhanced. I have to be looking straight on to see anything. If I tilt my head up or down, the image gets blurry.

I consider the current price of $19.98 competitively priced for this. This mirror is definitely not useful for me but it is what it says it is and functions as designed.

title: Thick, scentless, and intensely hydrating face cream
text: This face cream is wonderful. The jar it comes in is gorgeous and the cream is super rich and thick. It is also intensely hydrating. I applied this to my face and neck and it absorbed quickly and left my face feeling plush and super moisturized. I would have preferred this to have a nice scent instead of being scentless. Also, the current price of $42.98 is a bit steep. Nevertheless, this cream is wonderful and perfect for the winter. If this were priced at $35 or less, this would have received 5 stars from me.

title: Love the rose fragrance and hydrating face cream the most – 3.5 stars
text:
This set includes a make-up remover cleanser, a face mist spray, and a super hydrating face cream. I absolutely love the face cream because it is intensely moisturizing and thick. It is the type of cream that is perfect for winter. It leaves my face feeling incredibly hydrated. It also absorbs quickly.  The spray mist is also hydrating and I consider it perfect for summer instead of winter. I really like the rose fragrance of that one. What I do not care for is the cleanser. It is very watery and just not cleansing to me. I also prefer soap to this.

The current price of $27.89 ($28.89 minus $1) is reasonable for this set as long as one is likely to use a make-up remover like this. My favorite item in this entire package is the face cream with a nice rose aroma. At this price, it comes to $9.30 per item.

title: Small bath bombs; highly fragrant; decent performance in a foot bath but too $$$
text:
[[VIDEOID:57ea568ba110cd922c5541fdde55dd84]] There are 12 individually wrapped small bath bombs in this set in 12 fragrances. They all do not smell as I expect but I still like that the aroma is strong. The fragrances are:

- lavender
- jasmine
- tea tree
- chamomile
- rose
- orange
- peppermint
- rosemary
- cinnamon
- grapefruit
- lemon
- bergamot

The bombs dissolve quickly in about 3-5 minutes and the suds hold for a little over 10 minute; at least in a foot bath. The bath fragrance is strong. I tried the rose one and the fragrance was outstanding.

Since I personally do not like the color rings caused by bath bombs in my bath, I used this in a foot bath. The color of this bomb, which was an electric pink, did not adhere to my skin, my towel or to my foot bath; at least the color of the rose one did not adhere.

The current cost of $22.41 ($23.59 minus 5%) comes to $1.87 per bomb, which I consider pricey for this size. These are decent bombs that are giftable but I consider the price too much. I also wish the strong scents all smelled like they are labeled. Since these are so small, I doubt the fragrance or the bubbles will last in a large body of water such as a tub bath.

title: The fragrance is WONDERFUL; I got this for me and love it but the puff’s too small - see UPDATE
text:
For the current price of $19.99, this is a very reasonable and nice man's gift set. However, I ordered this for me because I use men's products and love the sandalwood scent.

This comes overpackaged, in my opinion but that means it is definitely giftable. In this package are the following items:

- A toiletry bag with a TO and FROM gift tag attached

- A tiny shower buff puff

- One 4.23 ounce package of bath salts

- One 4.05 ounce jar of body lotion

- One 4.05 tube of body scrub

- One 8.45 fluid ounce of shampoo and body wash

- One 8.45 fluid ounce of bubble bath

I tried everything but the bath salts and body puff. Note that foil has to be removed from the lotion and soaps. The sandalwood and amber fragrance is divine; I absolutely love it! I use the bubble bath as a body wash but it does suds up in bath water. I also use the body wash only for my body and not my hair, although this can be used for both. The liquid soaps are a clear amber color. The scrub is clear as well and is mildly exfoliating. I do wish it came in a flip top tube instead of having to unscrew the cap.

The lotion is lightweight but it leaves my body and hands feeling very silky. The bath salts are good for one soak. I'll probably use that in a foot bath eventually.

The toiletry bag is okay but the zipper arrived crooked in its track (see photo). It sort of righted itself when I opened and closed the case a few times but I do not feel the case zipper will hold up to heavy use.

In summary, this sandalwood and amber fragrance is intoxicating to my senses. The buff puff is useless, especially for a man. It is too tiny, like those freebies that sometimes come with bath soap. The case looks nice but I have my doubts about the zipper even though it glides easily on the track. Overall, I feel this is a great gift set for the price.

UPDATE: I no longer like the scrub as it does not lather at all. I do not feel clean after using it. Therefore, I lowered my ranking from 4 to 3 stars.

title: Love the pump container but the scentless lotion is just average – 2.5 stars
text:
This lotion comes in a pump bottle. All I had to do was remove the tab and pump out the desired amount. I do love the dispensing mechanism but the lotion itself is scentless and of medium consistency. It absorbs quickly and moisturizes okay but not deeply. However, there is nothing specifically spectacular about this lotion. I personally would not order it again because it does not wow me.

The current price is not listed for this. However, they priced their 3.2 fluid ounce tube of lightweight moisturizer at $32 that I cannot even fathom what insane price they will charge for this 4.9 fluid ounce heavier moisturizer.

title: Love the pump container but the scentless lightweight lotion is just average - 2.5 stars
text:
This lotion comes in a pump bottle. All I had to do was remove the tab and pump out the desired amount. I do love the dispensing mechanism but the lotion itself is scentless and lightweight. It absorbs quickly and only faintly moisturizes. There is nothing specifically spectacular about this lotion. I personally would not order it again because it does not wow me.

The current price of $32 for a 3.2 fluid ounce pump tube is outrageous.

title: Small bath bombs, a whisper of fragrance that smells artificial, decent suds – 3.5 stars
text:
[[VIDEOID:c5ce85d9c57e87c786196050bda0f387]] There are 12 individually wrapped small bath bombs in this set and the fragrance is super faint, similar, and artificial smelling to me.

The bombs dissolve in about 10 minutes and the suds hold for about the same. The bath fragrance is almost non-existent. I tried the green/blue one.

Since I personally do not like the color rings caused by bath bombs in my bath, I used this in a foot bath. The color of this bomb did not adhere to my skin, my towel or to my foot bath; at least the color of the one I tried did not adhere.

The current cost of 13.99 comes to a reasonable $1.17 per bomb. These are average bombs but are still definitely giftable. I do wish it had a stronger scent in the bath.

title: Highly fragrant bar of patchouli soap; moisturizes and lathers well
text:
This soap has a lovely and very strong patchouli smell and is moisturizing. It also lathers well.

The current price of $11.95 for this one bar of soap is way too expensive in my opinion. It is a very nice soap but still not as good as my all time favorite which is [[ASIN:B007OC7E2E Shea Moisture Three Butters Men's Utility Soap]] that is also less than half the price.

title: Tiny gel-like bar; moisturizing but nothing overly special for the price
text:
At the current price of $24.29 ($26.99 minus 10%), this is ridiculously expensive face soap. It is made in Japan and the only English instructions on the package say not to use this on any wound or eczema. As to why that is, I have no idea.

Nevertheless, I tried this and it lathers okay and feels very oily and moisturizing. I personally prefer a bar with more lather, less oily feeling, and certainly more reasonably priced. I also want to be able to read the packaging and ingredients and not have that in another language as is the case on this box

title: Nice soap, lathers well enough, and moisturizing
text:
This soap is nice. It lathers well enough but not copiously, smells okay, cleanses, and is moisturizing. It is also vegan.

The current price of $8.99 is expensive but competitive for soaps like these.

title: One of the largest massaging foot baths I tried so far; first one that works as designed
text:
[[VIDEOID:f0acca35a9eaaed81d337d0c93f817ae]] Besides the food bath, there is an instruction pamphlet in the package and a set of wheels. The instructions are clear but some information is lacking, like what the red light is for, etc.

FEATURES of the Foot Bath
- LED display

- LED controls for ON / OFF, temperature UP / DOWN, red light, massage modes, and bubbles

- Heats from 35 C to 48 C (i.e. 95 ℉ to 118.4 ℉)

- Has massage roller spikes and round balls in the bath and three massage levels

- Has a red light and bubbles option

- Has a reddish pink pumice stone in the middle of the bath

- Has a timer feature from 10 to 60 minutes but starts counting from 30 minutes

- Has a handle for carrying when full (cannot be used with cover)

- Has a drain plug

- The unit has a cover for storage

- It has wheels

LIKES
- Pumice stone in the middle is nice for softening heels and the foot bath is large enough to make this useful.

- The bubbles and full massage with a rotating centerpiece is nice.

- It is a super large unit and can fit large feet

- The wheels provide maneuverability

DISLIKES
- It requires a large sink or tub to fill.

- The unit is SUPER LARGE.

- The red light feature seems useless. Whatever it is supposed to do, like improve circulatio, is hocus pocus to me.

- The manual does not explain what the red light does.

- The handle is only operable with the cover off. I would have liked the ability to be able to carry the foot massager empty when the cover is on.

- The unit is noisy during operation.

- The unit is tall after the wheels are installed, so I have to sit on a chair, instead of a stool, to comfortably use this.

In summary, this foot bath is a SUPER LARGE unit. It actually functions as designed, which is refreshing. The current price of $99 ($119.99 minus $20) is reasonable for this. I give this 3.5 stars rounded up to 4 stars. This unit is too large for me but if one is in the market for a unit that feets one's feet comfortably, then this one is a good option.

title: Fragrant, relaxing, and soothing; I use as a foot soak
text:
This has a typical but moderate lavender fragrance. I use this as a foot soak instead of a body soak. Nevertheless, this is fragrant, relaxing, and soothing.

There are about two to four servings in this 16 ounce package. I used about a half cup.

The current price of $11.97 ($12.97 minus $1) is competitively priced. This is not my favorite soak as I prefer the [[ASIN:B07797LLNL Vitabath Lavender Chamomile Epsom Salts]] instead even though it is much more expensive. That one is more like a spa experience.

title: Fragrant, relaxing, and soothing; I use as a foot soak – 3.5 stars
text:
I tried their lavender fragrance also and I prefer that scent over this one. The citrus is strong and almost menthol-like. I use this as a foot soak instead of a body soak. Nevertheless, this is fragrant, relaxing, and soothing.

There are about two to four servings in this 16 ounce package. I used about a half cup.

The current price of $7.99 ($8.99 minus $1) is competitively priced. This is not my favorite soak as I prefer the [[ASIN:B07797LLNL Vitabath Lavender Chamomile Epsom Salts]] instead even though it is much more expensive. That one is more like a spa experience.

title: A perfect summer moisturizer with a light, fresh scent the has a hint of coconut
text:
This cream comes in a nice pump bottle. It is lightly creamy and perfect as a summer moisturizer. It takes a few seconds to absorb but once it does, it leaves my skin hydrated and silky. Although there is no coconut in the ingredients list, it has a faint hint of that tropical super fruit.

At the current price of $21.14 ($24.87minus 15%), this comes to a competitively priced $7.05 per 13.5 ounce pump bottle.

title: Medium-sized buff puffs that create copious suds during showering
text:
Mesh buff puffs are the only thing I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. These are medium in size and similar to the ones sold at Walmart for $1 or $2 each. There are five puffs and they work like any other mesh loofah I regularly use. Only time will tell how long these last. Usually, one to three months use is typical.

The current price of $9.99 comes to a competitively priced $2 each puff.

title: Five-star hand cream that is super hydrating & smells nice but it’s pricey
text: At 1.7 fluid ounces, there is hardly much hand cream in this tube for the current price of $16. However, what exists is wonderful. It is super hydrating and smells great and left my hands silky.

title: Super soft blender sponges; love the angles
text:
This is a nice set of eight mauve-colored blending sponges with one plastic case that allows the sponges to be displayed like a carton of eggs. The sponges are great even though they are not as dense as others I tried which means they soak up a little bit more liquid make-up.

There are six sponges with a flat / angled side which is great for smooth applications. The two other sponges are typical egg-shaped sponges that are good for blending or any large make-up application.

All the sponges feel good in my hands, blend well, and feel soft against my skin. These blenders make a great gift for the make-up obsessed. I love that the sponges do not smell. I tried other colored sponges and they smell like pencil shavings or other chemicals and these do not.

These are perfect as gifts for the Easter Basket.

At the current price of $7.99 this comes to a very reasonable $1 per sponge if I consider the plastic container as a freebie.

title: Nice toner; almost feels moisturizing and less astringent than my normal one
text:
I used a cotton round to apply this to my face and neck. It takes a lot of hits against my hand to dispense the product through the hole in the bottle. The toner feels less astringent and a little more moisturizing than typical and my face feels great after using this.

The current price of $29.89 is competitively priced for this 6.76 fluid ounce bottle. Note that this comes from Korea and most of the writing on the package is NOT in English.

title: Super hydrating; lovely fragrance to start but a fishy finish
text: This 2.03 fluid ounce tube of rose hand cream is SUPER HYDRATING and creamy and absorbs quickly. It also smells like rose to start but then there is a fishy smelling finish to the cream that I do not like. I absolutely love the results. The price of $6.99 is high but typical for this quality. Unfortunately, the after smell is offensive to me.

title: Really cleansed my hair & has a decent lather but smells like laundry detergent from yesteryear
text:
This shampoo is lightly creamy but smells like laundry detergent from yesteryear. I do not particularly care for the aroma. It lathers relatively well and is super cleansing. I used a little conditioner after shampooing. My hair came out clean and it did not weigh down my curls. I have short to medium fine curly hair and my curls were still visible.

At $26.69 ($31.40 minus 15%) for 8.4 fluid ounces, this is expensive. Also note that it is supposedly vegan. Unfortunately, I would never order this again both because of the off-putting fragrance and the high price.

title: This is the size of one Mini Babybel cheese; it’s super tiny but smells nice & moisturizes well
text: This is the size of one Mini Babybel cheese. It is super tiny. It works by melting with the heat of one's hands. It has a nice lavender fragrance but is a bit oily. It is hydrating but I do not care for the greasy feel or the exorbitant $22 price tag for such a small amount.

title: 320 generously sized and strong disposable tissues; must use soap or a scrub for these to work
text:
There are 4 packs of 80 tissues each pack for a total of 320 tissues. These are stronger than regular facial tissues and are a tiny bit padded. I use these with soap but I can also use these with toner or a facial scrub. They are useless dry unless one is using this to sop up moisture.

The current price of $25.99 ($30.99 minus $5) comes to a competitively priced $.08 cents per tissue. The only thing I do not like about these is the package. There is a perforation on top that is impossible to see and I had to use a sharp object to poke at it so that it would release the tissues.

title: I only like the back brush and shower puff; the rest is just okay
text:
There are nine pieces in this ensemble.

- 1 back brush puff

- 1 shower puff

- 4 self-stick clear plastic hooks

- 1 super exfoliating back scrubber

- 1 pumice

- 1 shampoo brush

I love mesh puffs (both back and shower) because they lather well and that has become my goto shower "sponge." The back puff with a handle offers the same sudsy experience and the handle is long enough for me to reach all areas of my back when working from both the top and bottom. The airy mesh allows copious suds to be produced in the shower. The body puff is just as good.

However, the back scrubber is too exfoliating and not something I would use. The pumice is okay and I do not like the shampoo brush; it is super cheap. Also, that brush does not have a loop on it so hanging it from the hole in the brush is difficult because it barely fits on the hook provided.

Only time will tell if the puffs unravel or not in less than three months. I think 3-6 months is all the use that can be gotten out of back brushes like these if used daily for two showers per day.

The current price of $12.49 ($14.49 minus $2) is reasonable for this if one uses everything.The silicone shampoo brush is the worst of the batch.

title: Decent mesh puff back brush; handle is sufficiently long; also great regular shower puff
text:
There is one mesh back brush with cloth loop for hanging and one regular shower puff with loop for hanging.

I love mesh puffs because they lather well and that has become my goto shower "sponge." These offer the best of both worlds since I can use the puff for everything I can reach in the front and the back puff for my back in the shower. The airy mesh allows copious suds to be produced in the shower.

Only time will tell if either one unravels or not in less than three months. I think 3-6 months is all the use that can be gotten out of back brushes / puffs like these if used daily for two showers per day.

The current price of $11.99 is pricey for this as it comes to $5.50 each. I can get a shower puff like this for $2 and a back brush like this for $4 at my local Walmart.

title: Decent mesh puff back brush; handle is sufficiently long
text:
This mesh bath back brush has a cloth loop for hanging.

I love mesh puffs because they lather well and that has become my goto shower "sponge." This puff with a handle offers the same sudsy experience and the handle is long enough for me to reach all areas of my back when working from both the top and bottom. The airy mesh allows copious suds to be produced in the shower. The only thing I do not like about these type of brushes is that the mesh is not as soft as some mesh puffs. Other than this they work the same.

Only time will tell if this unravels or not in less than three months. I think 3-6 months is all the use that can be gotten out of back brushes like these if used daily for two showers per day. Also, since the handle is plastic, it tends to break in the shower during use. I already broke two back brushes like these with vigorous scrubbing.

The current price of $9.99 is pricey for this. I can get ones like these at my local Walmart for about $4 and the handle on those feels a bit stronger.

title: Supremely hydrating; very thick; I like the chocolate aroma
text: This cream is super hydrating. It melts easily and absorbs quickly. It left the skin on my elbows and hands incredibly moisturized. I also like the chocolate aroma. Also, the current price of $14.99 is a good deal for this cream. Not everyone will like the aroma, however.

title: Lightly moisturizing but the fragrance combination has a sour smell to me
text: This is a summer moisturizer as it is a light cream. It absorbed rapidly but only lightly moisturized my hands. I was going to use this on my body but I can't get over the smell. At first it reminded me of sour milk but now it is just a sour smell. The mixture of lavender and sage and the other stuff in this just does not go. It is disappointing because it is a nice light summer cream but I just can't stand the scent.

title: Really cleansed my hair; nice fragrance; good lather
text:
This shampoo is creamy and smells nice with a fresh floral aroma. It lathers relatively well and is super cleansing. I used a little conditioner after shampooing. My hair came out clean and bouncy and it did not weigh down my curls. I have short to medium fine curly hair and my curls were still visible.

At $26.78 ($31.50 minus 15%) for 8.4 fluid ounces, this is expensive. Also note that it is supposedly vegan.

title: I had no idea this was tinted as I wanted a clear lotion
text: The title of this nowhere says this is a tinted lotion with SPF. I ordered this thinking this was ordinary suntan lotion for the face with SPF 30. Unfortunately, I cannot use this because of the tint and am disappointed by that. I might have rated it 5 stars otherwise.

The current price of $13.99 is pricey for this as it comes to $7 each. I can get ones like these at my local Walmart for about $4 and the handle on those feels a bit stronger.

title: Wonderful bath bombs w/large dinosaurs inside;  very fragrant & volcanic with suds
text:
[[VIDEOID:eaaec47cbc183d9c5fadf31ddc6858d3]] These bath bombs are wonderful. There are six kid bath bombs with surprise dinosaurs inside. They come in six fragrances of sweet orange, lavender, green apple, sweet strawberry, cotton candy, and bubble gum. All of them smell absolutely wonderful both inside and outside the bath--meaning both dry and in use.

I tried the green apple bomb in my foot bath. The fragrance was delightful. I used hot to tepid water and a volcano of suds was created in the foot bath. In fact, the bomb's suds just kept getting bigger and bigger and it dissolved in less than two minutes. The suds lasted about 10 minutes and started to fizz out after a while as I bathed my feet. The dinosaur was ejected immediately in the bath and it is somewhat large for a standard-sized bath bomb.

What I do love is that the color of the bomb did not turn my foot bath, feet, or drying towels green. Many bombs stain and this one did not.

The performance is outstanding in my opinion and so is the fragrance.  At the current price of $18.95, they come to a pricey $3.16 each but the quality surpasses many others I tried. I love them..

title: Lightly fragrant; produces rainbow-colored suds; color adheres; no face on bomb; $$$
text:
There is one super large individually wrapped bath bomb in this package. Based on the Amazon picture, I expected to have a face on the bomb or the bomb plastic and that is not the case. It is just an XL white cloud bath bomb.

It has a nice light fragrance when dry and in the bath. The ingredients are sodium bicarbonate, citric acid, aqua, fragrance, PVP, and benzyl benzoate.

It performs well, produces a lovely rainbow of suds, and dissolves in about 10-15 minutes. Since I personally do not like the color rings caused by bath bombs in my bath, I use them in a foot bath. When I was done, some color did adhere to my foot bath and my drying towel. I suspect if I used this in a bathtub I would not have had the same problem due to the water disbursement.

The current cost of $8.49 ($9.99 minus 15%) for one bomb is too expensive for this in my opinion especially when there is no face on the bomb and not even on the plastic.

title: Has a slick consistency I don’t care for but cleans well; okay scent; vegan
text: At $14.92 for 8.45 ounces, this hand wash is expensive. I used a generous amount on my hands and it has a slick consistency to it, which I do not care for. However, it lathers reasonably well and cleans gently. This is not for me but for those who are looking for a vegan cleanser, then this might fit the bill.

title: Decent set of reusable make-up pads, hairband, and exfoliating lip brush
text:
In this set is one pouch with 3 double-sided exfoliating lip brushes, 1 headband, and 10 reusable makeup pads.

Besides the case, my favorite items are the exfoliating lip brushes. I have really been getting into silicone spatulas/brush sets for applying face creams, bacitracin on a scar, etc. These three brushes are double-sided and have two different ribbed ends - one with large soft nubs and the other with smaller nubs. What I really love is that the wand is stiff which allows me to apply pressure when using a lip scrub.

With regard to the headband, it fits and enables me to hold my hair back temporarily if needed. The make-up remover pads will work with soap and water or a scrub. Note that even after washing they will become stained after first use. If one is into such an item, then this is perfect.

The current price of $12.99 is competitively priced.

title: I am not crazy about the fragrance of the lotion but I love it in the body wash; $$$
text:
At the current price of $9 this is a pricey duo. These are 1.69 ounce bottles of both lotion and body/hand wash.

This moisturizer is lightweight and lightly hydrating; however, I do not like the smell. It is a strong and artificial smelling lemon/lime scent. However, the body/hand wash smells better to me and I like it very much. It lathers and cleans well.

Unfortunately, there is hardly any product in this set. The body wash will only last me about three showers but the lotion (since I use it for my hands only) will last me longer.

UPDATE - I'm lowering my rating from 3 to 2 stars. The body wash lasted me two showers only. Also, the hand cream is impossible to get out of the container. They should have used a squeeze tube for this.

title: Good large-sized buff puffs that create copious suds that are perfectly wound
text:
Mesh buff puffs are the only thing I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. These are large and similar to the ones I buy at Walmart for $2 each. There are four puffs and they work like any other mesh loofah I regularly use. They are wound perfectly meaning the mesh is not too loose and not too tight.

I absolutely love the colors of these puffs. They remind me of summer.

The current price of $10.49 comes to a competitively priced $2.62 each puff.

title: This is so moisturizing I didn’t use conditioner; otherwise, same as other shampoos
text:
This shampoo is creamy and smells nice with a spicy floral aroma. It lathers relatively well and is super moisturizing. I found it so moisturizing that I did not use conditioner after shampooing. My hair came out with a bit of a sheen to it with fewer curls. I do not feel this is any better than other shampoos / conditioner combos I use except that I do not have to use conditioner. I have short to medium fine curly hair and my curls were slightly relaxed.

I think those who have damaged hair from colors and perms might find this shampoo wonderful for them. I have neither type of hair.

At $27.71 for 8.4 fluid ounces, this is expensive.

title: This wrinkle cream is a typical, hydrating facial moisturizer
text: I love this cream. It smells nice and is rich. It also absorbs well. I applied this to my face and neck and after a little while my face felt subtle. However, this is typical of most creams that smooth out the skin. The fragrance is nice too.

title: Fragrant bath bombs with animals inside; color stains body; animals not as pictured - 2.5 stars
text:
[[VIDEOID:85468c847e50ca0594d31466027a099f]] This is an attractive and giftable set of six bath bombs in six fragrances (rose, orange, lavender, lemon, mint, vanilla). They are made with essential oils.

I tried the rose bomb in my foot bath. The fragrance of this and each of the others is subtle but nice. I used hot to tepid water and suds were created in the foot bath and the bomb fizzed and the rabbit (encased in a plastic bubble) popped out. It eventually (in about 10 minutes) dissolved in the water as I bathed my feet. I felt clean and loved the scent. My feet also came out feeling very soft.

However, I am surprised that the color of the rose bath bomb did stain my feet badly--see photo. I had tried these bath bombs before in a set that included the chamomile and not the vanilla and did not have a problem with the rose bath bomb. Perhaps this set included too much color. In addition to the color staining, the animals pictured on the Amazon photo are not the same as in the bombs. For instance, I got a rabbit in mine and there is no rabbit shown in the Amazon photo but there is a rabbit on the box.

It is for these reasons that I rate this 2.5 stars. At the current price of $16.99, they come to a pricey $2.83 per bath fizz.

title: Lightweight moisturizer but am not crazy about the fragrance
text: This moisturizer arrived with the top dislodge from the bottle. However, I was able to re-seat it and it works fine. For $25, there is only 10 ounces of product which is a lot of money. The moisturizer is lightweight and lightly hydrating; however, I do not like the smell. It is a strong and artificial smelling lemon/lime scent. Besides the strong scent, the price would prevent me from purchasing this.

title: Definitely not exfoliating but this is a wonderful face wash brush
text:
This is really a 5-star face brush. It is well made and the bristles are super soft against my skin. The bristles also help work up a nice lather with the appropriate face wash product. The only reason I rated this 4 stars is because the Amazon site says this is exfoliating. This is not exfoliating at all; it is just an excellent and very gentle face wash brush. I suppose if one uses a sandy face wash, then it will be exfoliating but that would be the result of the scrub and not the brush.

The current price of $11.89 ($13.99 minus 15%) is competitively priced for the quality of this brush.

title: Smells like burnt strawberry; it's crumbly & gets all over my sink
text:
This works to soften the lips and remove dead cells; however, I hate it. It smells terrible--like strawberries that were burned on the stove. The first ingredient is sugar and it is just a crumbly mess. I rubbed a little into my lips and the scrub's sugar granules went all over my sink and bathroom counter. I hate this. I'd rather use a baking soda paste or a sugar paste I create myself.

UPDATE - I decided to try this again with an exfoliating lip brush and I still hate it. It is crumbly and goes everywhere. The smell is also offensive to me. I immediately threw this out after my second try.

title: Keeps my lips moisturized all night; jar incredibly difficult to open
text:
I was almost going to throw this product and give it one star because I was unable to open the jar. I tried for over three minutes and also used several grippers. Finally, the last gripper worked. Note that this jar top feels like it is cemented on. Subsequent openings were fine.

It comes with a small silicone lip applicator. It looks like Vaseline but the viscosity is more fluid. I actually thought this would not work and would wear off after an hour or so during bedtime. I actually woke up in the morning with lips that felt hydrated and not as dry and parched as is typical. Shockingly, this lip mask worked for me. The only reason I gave this 4 stars is because it is practically impossible to get to the product because the lid is on so tight.

The current price of $14.39 seems reasonable for this.

title: Highly fragranced soap; cleans well and lathers moderately
text:
This is a nice soap set in a presentable box. I consider this giftable. There are three bars of purple rose soap. In addition to the soap, there are two mesh pouches that can be used to hold the bar when it gets small; at least that is what I use them for.

I love this set. The fragrance is wonderful. It cleans well and has a moderate lather. The current price of $20.69 comes to $6.90 per bar if I consider the two mesh pouches freebies.

title: Three wonderful fragrances; cleans well and lathers moderately
text:
This is a nice soap set in a presentable box. I consider this giftable. There are three different soaps (tea tree, lavender, and purple rose). The lavender and purple rose are my favorites. In addition to the soaps, there are two mesh pouches that can be used to hold the soaps when they get small; at least that is what I use them for.

I love this set. The fragrances are wonderful with the tea tree bar being my least favorite. I tried the purple rose and it cleans well and has a moderate lather. The current price of $20.69 comes to $6.90 per bar if I consider the two mesh pouches freebies.

title: Wonderful fragrance; cleans well and lathers moderately; no tea tree oil aroma
text: I love this soap. The fragrance is divine and does not have that typical tea tree oil scent. It also cleans well and has a moderate lather. I have no idea how much this will be priced at but any price at $6 or below would be reasonable. Most likely it will be priced higher, however.

title: Decent mesh puff back brush; handle is sufficiently long
text:
There are two mesh bath mesh back brushes with cloth loops for hanging.

I love mesh puffs because they lather well and that has become my goto shower "sponge." These puffs with a handle offer the same sudsy experience and the handle is long enough for me to reach all areas of my back when working from both the top and bottom. The airy mesh allows copious suds to be produced in the shower. The only thing I do not like about these brushes is that the mesh is not as soft as some mesh puffs. Other than this they work the same.

Only time will tell if they unravel or not in less than three months. I think 3-6 months is all the use that can be gotten out of back brushes like these if used daily for two showers per day. Also, since the handle is plastic, it tends to break in the shower during use. I already broke two back brushes like these with vigorous scrubbing.

The current price of $14.99 is pricey for this as it comes to $7.50 each. I can get ones like these at my local Walmart for about $4 and the handle on those feels a bit stronger.

title: These colorful blenders work well but there's color bleed making this not giftable
text:
There are six blenders in this set; three in pink and three in green. I love the sponges as they are of medium density. Their colors are vibrant but all the green sponges had pink color bleed from the pink sponges, which is terrible if these were purchased for a gift as the sponges look used. For personal use, it does not matter much.

The green sponges have a flat / angled side which is great for smooth applications. The pink ones are the typical egg-shaped blenders that are also good for blending or any large make-up application.

All the sponges feel good in my hands, blend well, and feel soft against my skin. The sponges have a slight "paint" smell to them but it is a pleasant smell.

These are good for personal use but pass if these are intended to be a gift.

At the current price of $8.99, this comes to an expensive $1.50 per blender. Most blenders today sell for under $.90 cents each.

title: Large, high performance, highly fragrant bath bombs in two scents (lavender & eucalyptus)
text:
[[VIDEOID:9c1afa9dfe6838e5bad786209f4eb635]] There are six individually wrapped and super large bath bombs in this set with a leaf design. There are three in the lavender scent and three in the eucalyptus scent. These bombs are highly fragrant. I personally do not care for the eucalyptus fragrance of these bombs but others might like that scent.

I tried the purple one (i.e. lavender) and the fragrance was intense and came through in the foot bath. The bomb dissolved in about five minutes. The performance was exceptional with suds that lasted about 10 minutes. The end result of the bath was what looked like lavender-colored water. There was no staining to my skin, my towel, or to my foot bath; at least the color of the one I tried did not stain. A little bit of the bath bomb purple salt adhered to the sidewall of my bath but that rinsed off easily with water.

The current cost of $18.95 for 6 super large bombs comes to a competitively priced $3.16 per bomb. These are nice bombs and definitely giftable. Performance is outstanding and they are very fragrant. If I loved their eucalyptus fragrance, I would have rated this 5 stars.

title: Nice gift set; highly fragrant bath bombs with good performance; only 4 bath bombs
text:
[[VIDEOID:12d7ae3f7f0ac75bd62b9c2faf3f1628]] There are 4 individually wrapped medium heart-shaped bath bombs in this set. Each bath bomb is highly fragrant and the same scent and color. In addition, there is a jar of eucalyptus bath salt, one container of rose essential oil, one container of lavender essential oil, a sleep mask with matching carry pouch (counts as one item), a pair of disposable ear plugs, and one small fragrant candle in a tin. 

I do not like the eucalyptus bath salts at all because I find the aroma offensive. I have tried eucalyptus bath salts before but this one is just different. I love that the essential oils come with a flip top cap underneath the regular cap as this ensures they won't spill.  I like the rose essential oil. I used it in my diffuser and the scent was subtle and fresh; like a delicately scented bouquet of roses. The lavender essential oil barely has an aroma to me.

The sleep mask is comfortable but even when the elastic is extended the most, it still rests tightly around my eyes. It is light blocking. The earplugs are disposable and okay but only muffles sound.

I tried one of the rose bath bombs and it was absolutely wonderful. The fragrance was strong and lovely and came through in the foot bath. The bomb dissolved in about 10 minutes. The performance was great with suds that lasted about 15 minutes. The end result of the bath was almost clear water that was a pale pink. There was no staining to my skin, my towel, or to my foot bath.

There are only 4 bath bombs in this set but it is a 10-piece set when counting all the other items. Note that the sleep mask with its carry pouch is counted as one item. The current cost of $19.99 comes to $2 per item. This set is very nice and definitely giftable. Of course, it is unlikely that the recipient will love every item in this set because tastes differ.

title: Lovely bath bomb selection for kids; reasonable performance; subtle fragrance
text:
[[VIDEOID:ea2c80b0920ad70592ce9ea9bae8261]] There are 28 individually wrapped small bath bombs in this set in the scents/names listed below. Each bath bomb rattles and has a surprise toy inside inside a plastic container. The bath bombs have different names but there are several of the same fragrance even though the "name" is different.

8 lavender essential oil

4 rose essential oil

12 lemon essential oil

4 mint essential oil

Each fragrance is slightly different but only subtly so. I tried the one called sunset light rose essential oil which was a deep orange ball. It was lightly fragrant in the bath. The bombs dissolve in about 5 minutes. The performance was mediocre with light suds/foam that lasted about 8 minutes. The surprise popped out immediately and was a little rabbit inside a plastic container. The end result of the bath was clear water that looked like Tang. There was no staining to my skin, my towel, or to my foot bath; at least the color of the one I tried did not stain.

The tin this comes in is wonderful and can be repurposed once the bombs are done.

The current cost of $39.99 for 28 bombs comes to a competitively priced $1.43 per bomb. These are nice bombs and definitely giftable. Performance is not outstanding but it is good enough, especially for kids.

title: Smells wonderful, is intensely hydrating, and has SPF 30 (SEE UPDATE)
text:
SEE UPDATE

At the current price of $14.99 this is wonderful. This cream is thick, smells wonderful, and is intensely hydrating. It also has SPF 30.

I slathered this all over my face and neck (but avoided the eye area), and it absorbed quickly and left my skin feeling super moisturized. I would definitely order this again. It is a perfect winter cream.

UPDATE July 18, 2022 - I've been using this religiously all summer and even put it on my boyfriend twice, since it is a face cream with SPF 30. We always avoid the eye area. Unfortunately, this sometimes somehow gets into the eyes and results in my eyes going bloodshot and being irritated. For my boyfriend, it was even worse, where he thought he had to go to a doctor. It looked like he had "pink eye" and he had trouble seeing. If it were not for this, this cream would be fantastic. Therefore, I am lowering my rating from 5 to 2 stars.

title: Good large-sized buff puffs that create copious suds but it's loosely wound
text:
Mesh buff puffs are the only thing I use in the shower besides a back brush. I love them because they generate a lot of suds and they provide good coverage during showering. These are large and similar to the ones I buy at Walmart for $2 each. There are four puffs and they work like any other mesh loofah I regularly use. I have no idea what it means to have this charcoal infused but I notice no difference in sponge quality or performance over my typical Walmart sponges.

However, what I am disappointed about is that they arrived loosely wound (see photo that shows long pieces sticking out). I do not feel these will last long because of this and that is the only reason I rated these 3 stars.

The current price of $9.99 comes to a competitively priced $2.50 each puff. If these puffs were not so loosely wound, they would have gotten 5 stars from me.

title: I rec’d the wood scent & not tangerine; smells terrible & only lasts me 3 hours
text:
This is a 2.5-ounce solid tube of deodorant.I ordered the tangerine scent and was looking forward to it but got the wood scent instead. That scent smells horrible and is nothing like wood. However, it glides smoothly. Since it does not have aluminum, it is only effective on me for three hours.

The smell is one star for me and the performance two stars. For me this is a complete fail. I'll go back to my Old Spice with aluminum in it.

title: Great for parties or walking at night but a bit gimmicky; 3 light modes
text:
[[VIDEOID:a223ea7f2ca0addb8a6c0cc97445e6cb]] At first I didn't like these because the wires and two battery packs inside the scrunchies make this difficult to maneuver. However, after I tried them, I think these are cool. They are great for holiday parties or just to wear in my hair when walking at night.

There are six ponytail scrunchies and each one has two battery packs with wires sewn into the holder. In order to operate, I had to pull out the two paper stubs from the battery. Note that this has to be done blind because there is no access from the outside. I had to feel through the material to do this. Also, to turn on, I had to feel for the buttons on the battery pack and squeeze. There are three light modes: steady, blinking lightly, and blinking fast.

The current price of $15.98 comes to $2.66 each. I have no idea how long the batteries will last. However, because the unit is sewn into the scrunchie, they cannot be replaced.

title: Very nice body scent that lasts a couple of hours; sprays on with ease
text:
There are three small cans of deodorant/body spray in this package. The cans are a lot smaller than they look online as they are only 3.4 ounces apiece. In this set are three of the same coconut water and sandalwood scents which is my favorite of all their scents. Previously I tried their variety pack and liked this fragrance the best. The aroma is very nice and the scent is balanced and not overpowering. The aroma lasts a couple of hours but not all day.

I like men's fragrances, so I use this for myself. The current price of $35.99 comes to an expensive $12 per can.

title: Very nice body scents that last a couple of hours; sprays on with ease
text:
There are three small cans of deodorant/body spray in this package. The cans are a lot smaller than they look online as they are only 3.4 ounces apiece. In this set is fresh citron and driftwood, fig leaves and white musk, and coconut water and sandalwood. All of the fragrances smell nice and are balanced and not overpowering. I love the coconut water and sandalwood blend the most. The aroma lasts a couple of hours but not all day.

I like men's fragrances, so I use this for myself. The current price of $35.99 comes to an expensive $12 per can.

title: Serums is incredibly hydrating & absorbs quickly but dispensing eyedropper is horrible
text:
After using a toner, I applied this to my face and neck. It absorbed quickly and left my face and neck incredibly hydrated. I absolutely love the results. However, it is super difficult to get the product out of the container. The eyedropper does not suck up the fluid and I had to try about five times just to get enough for one application. I will have to hit this against my palm to dispense the product. For $36.95, the package it comes in should work flawlessly. This is the only reason I rated this 3 stars. If I have difficulty getting to the product, it is not worth much to me.

Note that everything except for the directions and one other sentence are in written Korean.

title: Pump top very difficult to open; shampoo has lovely fragrance & lathers well; too pricey - 3.5 stars
text:
It took me almost 10 minutes to get the pump top to pop up so that I could dispense the shampoo. I almost gave up

This shampoo smells great and lathers well. After my short to medium fine curly hair dried, it had a sheen to it, which was nice. However, it did weigh down my curls a little bit.

The current price of $35.99 is outrageously expensive for this but then this is being marketed as a salon-quality shampoo. I think it is a good shampoo but the price is a bit too steep in my opinion and the results are good but not great. If it did not relax my curls a little bit, then I would have loved this and given this 4.5 stars. If they also made the pump easier to open, then it would have received 5 stars.

title: Cloyingly fragrant steamers that dissolved quickly & left no stains; too much menthol
text:
There are six different shower steamers in this package in six scents that are cloyingly fragrant.

1 - Eucalyptus with Menthol Crystal
2 - Peppermint with Menthol Crystal
3 - Orange and Lemon with Menthol Crystal
4 - Lemongrass with Menthol Crystal
5 - Lavender with Menthol Crystal
6 - Grapefruit with Menthol Crystal

I tried the grapefruit one in my shower and made sure to put it away from the full stream of water. Nevertheless, it dissolved in less than three minutes before I was even done with the shower. However, the fragrance is overwhelming to me. There is just too much menthol in these and that makes all the steamers smell almost the same.

I like these much better than some others I tried but the menthol is just too overwhelming. I do love that it did not stain my tub.

The current price of $18.95 comes to a very expensive $3.16 per steamer.

UPDATE - I had my neighbor try a couple of these and she said they were terribly dissapointing. They dissolve too quickly and she barely detects any fragrance. She hates them and would rate this 1 star.

title: A bit larger than a typical blender & cute but it's pricey and it smells
text:
There is one pink, large blender sponge with a pig face and one very CHEAP PLASTIC holder. In addition, a tiny blender for the eye area was included as a gift. I have no idea if purchasers receive the gift or not.

The sponge is of medium density but it is a little larger than typical blenders. It feels good in the hands, blends well, and feels soft against my skin. I do love the tiny sponge because that is great for make-up blending around the eye area.

However, I do not like the plastic holder at all. I would have preferred a metal one as it is cheap and tacky looking. I also do not like that the blender smells.

Except for the size, the sponges themselves are similar to all of the others that I tried before this. I think the only reason to purchase this is for its cuteness (i.e. the pig face) which will get mostly covered by make-up. The current price of $8.24 ($10.99 minus 25%) is pricey for what amounts to one sponge if I consider the holder a freebie. There are many sponges like this on the market that come with a holder and four or five slightly smaller blenders for the same price.

title: Not as smelly as most other unrefined  shea butter; it’s ultra-moisturizing
text:
This shea butter smells natural and unrefined so it does have a little bit of that "burnt tobacco" smell. However, it is not as bad as some unrefined shea butters I previously used in a body butter recipe.

I got this to use "as is" as a moisturizer. It is super moisturizing and makes my hands and body feel incredibly hydrated. Since I have been using shea butter for a while now, I am getting used to the smell.

In summary, I feel this shea butter is great. This shea butter is chunky and perfect for use in body butter recipes or by itself. This is ultra-moisturizing and absorbs well. The current price of $9.99 for 10 ounces is also competitively priced.
