title: Excellent Trimmer
text:
I have a Braun shaver that I really like as well as an immersion blender in the kitchen that is also a solid performer. I have come to trust Braun as a brand. So, I was very interested in this trimmer as a replacement for a Remington which is slowly circling the drain. So far I am very pleased with it.

This is not a simple trimmer for just the head or the beard but is a multi-purpose tool for cutting all kinds of hair. It comes with multiple attachments including a nose hair trimmer, a detail trimmer and a couple of combs for cutting head and beard hair. It is easy to adjust with the wheel so that different lengths are available.

This trimmer does a great job. It has very sharp blades (at least right out of th ebox) so cutting and trimming take a minimal amount of time and effort. The detailer makes quick work of unruly eyebrows and other edge areas where some control is needed. And, this is not an especially loud trimmer so it doesn't wake the house when in use.

So far I have not run this trimmer all the way down, either. It has at least 30 minutes of run time, though the box says it runs for up to 50. I haven't run it down all the way yet so I am not sure how long it will go on a charge.

I had high expectations for this trimmer and it has not disappointed me. It works very well, it has multiple attachments for doing different tasks, it works quickly because of the sharp blades, and it isn't cost prohibitive.

title: Effective and Expensive
text:
I have used Head & Shoulders for years for keeping dandruff in check. I selected this bottle with the hope it would work as well as the original. It does, though I don't think it works any better for the price.

This is a good-sized bottle and unless you're in a habit of washing your hair several times a day it should last quite a while. A bottle this size usually lasts me about 6 months under normal circumstances.

This stuff smells nice and it does a decent job of controlling dandruff, though I don't think it is any more effective than the original Head & Shoulders - at least not in my case.

My primary complaint is actually the price. The per-ounce price is quite high ($0.84/oz as I write this). Because the original works well enough for me, as does the 2-1, I probably will not buy another bottle of this stuff when it's gone just because there are less expensive options that work for me.

Don't get me wrong, this is good shampoo. It's a generous amount in the bottle, it smells nice and it works. But, it's expensive. In my particular case the other variants of Head & Shoulders are a better value; this particular version may be more effective for others.

title: Good Foot Scrubber; Less-Than-Good Accessories
text:
I struggle with cracked heels more than callouses and I thought this device would help with that versus using a rasp. So far it has worked decently for that. It's a good package and I like it, though there is some room for improvement.

The main component of this kit is basically a skin sander, for lack of a better description. It employs a powered rolling drum that effectively sands away rough skin and exfoliates as it goes. It is very comfortable and actually feels really good while it's working. It does a decent job of buffing away the cracks in my heels, though it does take a bit more effort than a rasp. On the flip side, it seems a lot less likely to cut my heel so it's a trade-off.

I like that it can be charged via USB and used wirelessly. That makes it much more convenient.

The kit comes with some accessories and here is where my complaint lies. There are some good tools in there - a rasp and buffing file, a razor and more. All of these are good, but they're much smaller than most I have seen and are bordering on uselessness. I won't use the tools that came with this kit as I have a full-sized kit with tools that are more sturdy.

I like this scrubber and will use it on my heels regularly. It feels good while it's working and it does a decent job, though a little slower than using a rasp. I don't particularly care for the accessories that come with it but it's hard to argue with the asking price.

title: Inexpensive and Fairly Complete Manicure Kit
text:
I needed a cheap manicure kit to keep in the car and I selected this one for that purpose. There's nothing special about this kit and it is not a high-end package by any stretch of the imagination, but it does the job for which I got it and it's not overpriced.

This is a simple and straightforward kit. It has everything you will need in a manicure kit, plus a little more - nail clippers, scissors, a lance, cuticle pusher, tweezers, and more. There are 9 different tools in this kit, and they come in a clamshell type case that keeps them together. It's smaller than a typical man's wallet so it will fit easily in a pocket, a toiletries bag or a glove box in the car with room to spare.

The tools in this kit are fairly basic and are not the highest quality. However, this is a very inexpensive kit and it is worth the asking price for what it is. It's small, compact, easy to stash and it's fairly complete.

title: Excellent After Shave Lotion
text:
I have used an electric shaver for years and I have struggled with irritated skin after shaving for a while. I have been looking for a solution that would help moisturize my skin and help with chapping. I gave this lotion a shot after trying others. This one seems to be decent, and it smells nice too which is a bonus.

I was a little concerned when I opened the package as the contents of the bottle is very thick, almost pasty. I received a pump bottle of lotion, not a squeeze bottle, so I wasn't sure it would actually come out properly. However, it does, and it comes out in just the right amount per pump.

It goes on smoothly and it definitely feels nice. It does a good job of moisturizing my skin and it has kept the irritation down too, which is really the main consideration for me.

This stuff definitely has a scent to it, and it reminds me of coconut tanning lotion. It's a pleasant smell and it isn't strong, and it does fade over time (could not smell it after an hour).

This lotion works well and I do like it. It goes a good job of reducing skin irritation after shaving, it keeps my skin soft, and it smells nice too which is a plus. I'll buy more when my current bottle is gone.

title: Very Nice Comb; Expensive
text:
I have a son who has a full beard and while he keeps it trimmed up and neat most of the time, I still look for grooming products that might help him along. I selected this comb with that thought in mind, and while it's a nice comb in a nice package, it is a bit overpriced.

This is a sandalwood fine-tooth comb and it does a nice job with grooming a beard. Out of the box it has a nice though subtle smell to it, and it is sanded smooth with a nice inlay. I wasn't able to find any obvious rough spots that needed to be sanded, any gouges or pits in the wood, or any warps.

It comes with a nice little carrying pouch that fits nicely in a shirt picket.

The main negative I have found with this comb is the high price tag. As I write this, it sells for about $40 here which is unusually high. A suitable substitute can be found for less than $10.

This is a nice comb that seems to be made well. It will get the job done and it looks really nice. The real question though is if it's worth the high price tag. As a gift option, an argument can be made for the asking price, but as a personal purchase for daily use this is a hard sell.

title: Decent Clippers
text:
One of the things we need around the house (and never seem to be able to find) is nail clippers. I selected this one for keeping on the main level of the house so that we could find at least one set when we need it. It's a decent set though it isn't quite as good as I had hoped.

This set of snips is fingernail sized, though they'll work for toenails. The cutting edges are plenty sharp so they're good for cutting through tough nails and snipping off pieces of dead skin. They're comfortable to use and they work well for the most part.

The one issue I have with them is the plastic sleeve on these that is supposed to catch clippings. There are two issues with this. First, it doesn't work so well and catches very little. Second, it is not removable so it is not easy to get out what it does manage to catch. I would rather have not had the sleeve at all, and I would remove it if I could but I can't get it to come off.

These are good clippers, though they would be better without the catch sleeve. They cut well and are comfortable to use.

title: Effective but Expensive
text:
I have seen and ordered epilators and hair removal systems in the past, and all have some measure of usefulness. Some are more painful than others while others are less effective. I was unsure of what to expect with this system; it's expensive and packed with features so I thought it would be a good solution. I am not so sure the cost makes this a good value, but it does work well regardless.

This is my first experience with an IPL ("intense pulsed light") system. For testing I used it on my hands, where I have a couple of odd hairs on my knuckles that bug me. This seemed like a good test scenario with minimal risk and a low chance of failure.

This is an interesting device. It has an LCD with touch screen controls to control operation. It has several intensity levels and you can use filters with it to more fine-tune operation. It's relatively quiet, and it works quickly. Most importantly, it just works. I was able to clear away the unwanted hairs on my hands with no difficulty and the cooling function is actually very pleasant.

Included in the box are eye goggles and a razor.

The one reservation I have with this system is that it is very, very expensive when compared to other similar devices. Where most systems run about $300 on the high end, this system is double that as I write this. I have no basis of comparison for value as I have not used any other IPL solution for any purpose; this seems steep, though.

This is a good working solution for hair removal and it works quickly and cleanly, It has a generous feature set and seems to be well-made. The cost is very high, though, and should be considered when looking for this type of system.

title: Good for Detail Work on Facial Hair, Too
text:
Ok... I did not get this product for its intended use but instead got it as a detailer for sideburns and eyebrows, both of which are problems for me. So far I am pleased with this trimmer, and though I have not used it for the purpose for which it is marketed (body hair) I can see why it would work in that capacity.

This is a small battery-powered shaver that is good for detail work. It cuts very close without nicks and cuts, and it is small enough to get very detailed without being a contortionist or spending a lot of time.

It's comfortable in the hand which is important. It's waterproof so it works in the shower, though for me I use it at the sink where I can see what I'm doing. Usually when I am trimming it takes a minute or less, so I have not managed to kill the battery yet. For those using it for body hair, I imagine the battery will need to be charged more often than I will have to charge mine.

Although this is marketed as a body hair trimmer, it works well for detail work on facial hair too. It's efficient, it doesn't nick or cut, and it has a decent battery.

title: Effective but Expensive
text:
One of the issues I have had with underarm deodorant sticks, in particular the smooth glide varieties, is that they have a very bad tendency to cause me to break out with a painful rash. I have had this problem enough that I am apprehensive when trying a new brand or a new product. With that apprehension, I tried this one, and so far it hasn't given me any troubles.

This package comes with 4 sticks, and at the time I write this it works out to close to $7/stick. That's expensive and it represents the one major issue I have with this product.

It smells nice and it goes on easy. It seems to work well enough that I don't need to apply daily. The important thing for me , as mentioned, is that it does not irritate my skin and cause me to break out with a rash. That's the biggest plus I can ever give a deodorant product like this one.

Other than the unit pricing, I am pleased with this product. It works well enough for my needs and it doesn't cause me any skin irritation. The price will need to come down before I consider buying more, though.

title: Large Scrubber Head and Comfortable Bristles
text:
I have used a scrub brush in the shower for quite some time, as it enables me to wash my back without any assistance. My previous brush has passed it’s usable life span and I was ready for a new one. This one has filled the gap nicely for me.

To summarize quickly, this brush has a long bamboo handle, an array of bristles set in a plastic base, and a rope handle that makes holding on easy. It also has a small loop at the tip of the handle that makes this brush easy to hang.

Checking this over, the brush has a nice finish and I wasn’t able to find any rough spots in the bamboo. The bristles are set nicely and seem to be tight and don’t pull out easily. I expect the rope wrapped around the handle will be the first failure point, though I am speculating.

There’s a lot to like about this brush. I love the large, round head which gives a little better coverage than my smaller oval-shaped brush. The bristles are fairly soft, but the length (5/8" from the plastic base to the tips) makes them stiff enough to be effective but not so stiff to cause discomfort. The rope handle makes hanging on to this brush when it’s wet easy.

This is a replaceable item so I have no expectation that it will last indefinitely; eventually I will need to throw it away and get a new one. My expectations are high, though, that this one will last for a good while, based on the apparent quality. I love the coverage the head gives too which is a big plus. If you use a scrub brush like this in the shower, this one is very much worth a look.

title: Seems to Work; Need More Time to Know How Well
text:
This is an interesting device that is supposed to help tighten skin and help with aging and wrinkles. It's a device that takes some time to work and so far we have not given it enough time to know for sure that it will work in the long term. However, there are some things I can say about it in the meantime.

This is a small, handheld device that is about the same size as a flashlight. It works with infrared light to prod the body into healing itself, much like red light therapy, though dealing with loose skin is not exactly an injury that requires healing. After the first use it is clear it's doing something to which the skin reacts because the skin feels mildly irritated (almost itchy) after it's used.

Do read all of the documentation first. There is a lot of information about how to use this and what to avoid. In fact, I'd recommend paying special attention to the warnings on overuse.

This item is packaged well and it seems to hold a decent charge when it is fully charged up. I do not know how long the full runtime is, but it lasts longer than a single session and it does not need to be continuously charged.

So far I haven't enountered any negatives with this device. It seems to work (or, at least it does do something) and all indicators are that it is made decently well. Once I have nore data I will return and update this.

title: Decent Clippers; Not an Improvement Over Less Expensive Clippers
text:
We have a few pairs of clippers in our house and we each have a set that we prefer. I selected these for one of the household members who did not have a nice set for himself, and so far these have worked out well. These are decent clippers. That said, I think these are priced a bit high and don't have much advantage over cheap pairs you can find at the local drug store.

These are big clippers so they are suitable as both fingernail and toenail clippers. These are sharp and they get the job done easily. They include a nice little leatherette case for storage which is nice for travel.

My main issue is the cost, which is actually not unreasonable. That said, these do not outperform cheaper clippers that can be found at the local pharmacy, and when that is taken into consideration these seem priced slightly high.

I like these clippers. They do a good job and they seem to be decently made. They're not an improvement over a cheap pair that can be found locally for a lower cost, though.

title: Nice Bath Scrubber Puffs; Unit Price is High
text:
I have been using bath puffs like these for years as they do a good job of exfoliating the skin and they generate a lot of suds, which at least makes me feel like I am getting clean. These are good scrubbing puffs, on par with what I can find locally, but are quite a bit more expensive per unit.

These are very much like a typical bathing scrubber puff - plastic mesh pinned together in the center. They seem to last about the same amount of time as well, approximately a month each though that will depend on how often you use them.

As I write this, these are priced at about $3.50/unit. I can find the equivalent locally for closer to $2/unit, which is almost half the cost. While it’s nice being able to buy them in quantity, and these certainly aren’t expensive in the grand scheme of things, the price difference is not negligible.

Other than the price difference I like these and can recommend them based on usage. However, if you consider the per-unit cost, there are better options.

title: Decent Trimmer that Works Well
text:
My adult son is still at home and sports a beard so I selected this trimmer kit for him, thinking it would be a good tool for him to keep his beard tidy and clean. It’s a decent trimmer kit and it works well, though it is not perfect.

This is an all-in-one kit that includes the cordless trimmer itself, several combs and guards and even a foil for detail shaving. It’s everything you need to shave and trim without having to break out a separate razor for detail work or another trimmer. That said, this does not mean it is an expert in all things. The shaver foil is small and while it does work as a shaver it is not intended to be a full-face shaver. It will work in that capacity if absolutely necessary but it will take much longer than if using a shaver dedicated for such. On the flip side, it does mean that a separate shaver is not needed when packing for travel.

The trimmer itself is well-made and is built to survive small drops and jostling. I wouldn’t deliberately drop it on a concrete floor, of course, but it doesn’t need to be babied either.

The combs and foils attach and detach easily and make this trimmer easy to adapt to the need.

As a beard trimmer, this works well. The different combs make getting the length right relatively straightforward and easy. My son has had no difficulty getting his beard to look the way he wants with this trimmer.

Where this trimmer comes up short is in two areas. First, this isn’t a very quiet trimmer and it makes a fair bit of noise when in use. It won’t wake the house, but it can be heard fairly well through a closed bathroom door. Second, it is on the higher end price-wise. The price can be partially justified with the inclusions of the foil and number of combs, though if you already have a unit sufficient for shave detailing then the foil is an added cost you won’t need.

This is a decent beard trimmer and shaver that works well. The cost is a little on the higher side, and it’s a little on the loud side when it use, but it’s well-suited for someone who wants a single trimmer/shaver that is got for home and travel use.

title: Great Tools with Zero Documentation
text:
I have been dealing with cracked heels for years. Usually they don’t hurt, but they do get unsightly and I have tried using a different kind of foot file on my heels with limited success. I was hopeful that this foot rasp and corresponding tools would help. It has worked far and away better than I had hoped and I am very pleased with it.

This is a tool kit, not just a single tool, and the main attraction is the foot file which somewhat resembles a large cheese grater. There is also a callus razor with multiple blades, another foot rasp that is for smoothing, a cuticle tool and a nail pick.

That main attraction to this kit is the foot file. It looks intimidating and I was concerned that it would cut my foot. The key is gentleness and patience, and when I worked on my heels it didn’t hurt and it didn’t cut me. It removed a lot of dead and ugly skin and left my heels looking much more pleasant. The smoothing rasp did a good job of reducing down the picked surface to a smooth shine, and afterward a little lotion on my heels has kept them from drying out. Where my previous routine was working on my heels a little bit every day, this rasp and file has done more good in a week than I could get done in a day, without cutting.

The callus cutter resembles a miniature cheese slicer and there is potential there to really harm yourself if you’re not careful. The razor blades are sharp and they do their job well.

I have a couple of cuticles that tend to pull out as the nail grows (on my hands as well as my feet), so the cuticle pusher has helped get those back in place without any effort. Again, the rule is patience and a gentle hand.

I have not needed the nail pick.

So, the one thing missing in this kit – documentation. There is absolutely no documentation with this kit at all. While you can get the information you need from the product listing, that’s not helpful if you’re traveling and do not have access to the network. Even a one-page guide showing what each tool is used for and how to install the blades in the callus cutter would be helpful.

This is a great kit and it works well, better than I had expected and hoped. It has done more for my heels in a one session than in a week’s worth of work with my previous solution. Except for completely lacking any documentation, this is a great kit.

title: Smells Nice
text:
I selected this shampoo based on the claim that it helps to slow hair loss and thinning. That’s an interesting claim and I was curious if it would live up to the claim. So far I haven’t seen much difference for those of us that have tried it.

I’ll start with what I know and can speak to. I think this stuff smells nice. It has a nice fragrance and lathers up decently when washing my hair. It does a sufficient job of getting rid of the “greasies”. And afterward my hair feels clean and my scalp feels good. The bottle is decent and doesn’t leak, too, which is always a plus.

As for encouraging hair growth and impeding hair loss, this hasn’t yet worked out for any of us. We haven’t seen much difference at all, positive or negative.

I will revisit this and update if I notice a change, but all indicators so far (having had this a month) are that it’s just a nice-smelling and expensive bottle of shampoo.

title: Exfoliating or Moisturizing?
text:
We have used SoftSoap products for years and we especially like the hand soap. However, we’re no strangers to body wash either and were interested in trying this body wash. It works well and smells great but I would hesitate to call it exfoliating unless it is used with a scrubber sponge or a loofa.

First off, the bottles came packaged with tape over the caps so they would not burst open in shipping. I was glad to see that – that could have been a horrible mess had even one of these opened enough to leak in the box.

It smells strongly of coconut and the fragrance transfers when you wash with it. After a good shower with this body wash I feel clean; that is, I didn’t notice it leaving a film behind like some soaps do.

This is marketed as an exfoliating soap but I didn’t feel anything in the soap that feels remotely abrasive enough like most exfoliating washes so I am not convinced of the claim that it will exfoliate on its own without scrubbing sponge or cloth. Where this body wash excels, however, is as a moisturizer. After a shower I noticed that my normally dry skin was softer and less dry. Maybe that’s what was meant by exfoliating?

It does work well as a hand soap – if you like coconut-scented hand soap. At least two of these bottles will end up being used for just washing hands.

This is decent body wash and hand soap, packaged well and pleasantly fragrant.

title: So Far has Worked Very Well
text:
I have a Braun shaver that has served me well, so I selected this shaver/epilator for my wife, based on my previous experience with Braun grooming appliances. So far it has worked out for her, though she has not used all of the functions it provides yet.

This is a hair removal and trimming system, not just a shaver. It has multiple functions and replaceable heads to give it more use than a simple shaver would be. The head actually swivels so it adjusts as it’s being used to maintain smooth contact with the skin without requiring being a contortionist or avoiding trouble spots (like that little dip in the armpit or just behind the knee).

The shaver does a very nice job and leaves the skin very smooth without irritating it. It works quickly so the process is over and done without a lot of fuss. So far my wife has not tried the epilator so I will have to come back and update for that.

So far the battery has held up well and lasts for close to an hour on a single charge. Unless you are especially meticulous and the process takes a long time, it should last through multiple uses before requiring a recharge.

It comes with a nice pouch for storage and travel.

Up to this point we have no complaints. It seems to work well and it lasts a while on a single charge. My wife has not used all of the functions that this device offers, but those she has used have worked well.

title: Versatile Set, Priced Well
text:
I selected this set of tweezers with the thought of hair removal in particular. I get the occasional eyelash that gets turned inward toward my eye as well as the very occasional ingrown hair. I have used a set of very pointed carbon-tipped tweezers for these tasks and they work well enough but they’re not ideal, so I was hopeful that this set would be a better fit for my needs. I was right.

This is a set of three stainless steel tweezers and one lance. The tweezers each have a different function. One has a very pointed tip that’s useful for “digging” or isolating a single object. Another has a flat tip that is very useful for grabbing surface objects like the base of a hair or a splinter. The third set of tweezers also has a flat top but at an angle, and this is useful in similar ways to the other flap-tip tweezers but for harder-to-reach areas.

The lance is needle-sharp – be careful when handling it. On the opposite end of the point is a loop, and the loop is used for gently extracting blackheads or draining pimples (I know, this is not a pleasant topic, but this is what the set was made for). Because the tip is so sharp and comes to such a point, be careful not to drop it as it can stick into the counter or bend the tip which will make it dull and much less effective.

Because these are all steel tools, I do not recommend using them on electronics.

This is a nice set of tweezers that will serve you well. The price is very reasonable and the set covers most use cases you might have.

title: Designed and Made Well
text:
All right, I will confess that I chose this item for the express purpose of pulling a prank on a coworker, not as a practice head for make-up. While it has served well in it's role for startling the unsuspecting, it is a suitable unit for make-up practice.

So, this is about the same size as a child's face, with the same general features (tissue distribution). Everything seems to be proportional. The description states that it is made of silicone and designed to feel like real skin; that's true to a point. I would say it is similar, but it is firmer to a light touch and softer on a hard push. There's an advantage to that, though. When working with this practice head, the silicone is smooth and taut, meaning that if the head is secured properly while working the surface will not pull like real skin might. Though it is slightly different than natural tissue, it's actually an asset.

The back of the head is flat and it is designed to lay mostly flat on a work surface. It has a plastic port on the back, large enough to stick a finger through, and this permits anchoring on a dowel when working. Of course, you could use it to mount on a spike outside of one's office, but I wouldn't know anything about that... If working on a smooth, slick surface and the head slides while working, a little double-sided tape is a quick and easy solution if using the port is not a good option.

There is no paint, no markings or anything else other than the molding to give it features, so it really is a good unit for practice. Cosmetics apply and stick similarly to the way it does with skin. It cleans easily with warm soapy water and dries with a towel, so it is very definitely reusable.

I might not use this in the intended fashion but it's a good solution for those wanting to practice. It is decent size, the material is well-suited for working on technique and it is washable. The price is also reasonable.

title: Works well, Made Well. Smells Terrible When Wet.
text:
I have wanted a brush like this one for a long time and I was pleased to have the opportunity to try this one. So far it has worked well for me but I have one complaint with it – it smells really gross when it’s wet, especially before it is used for the very first time.

I like the hard, heavy handle which makes it easy to use without flexing much while in use. It’s long enough that, going over the shoulder, it can reach my lower back.

The bristles are not stiff like a grout scrubbing brush but they’re not super-soft either, they’re somewhere close to that of a stiff paint brush. They’re sturdy enough to exfoliate and clean without buffing like a sponge would. Since I have started using this brush, I have had a lot less trouble with itchy skin on my upper back. And in use, it is very comfortable.

As nicely as this brush works, the smell of the bristles when they’re wet is enough to make me gag. They’re especially bad when the brush is brand-new, and I can only hope that the odor fades as it gets exposed to more soap over time.

I do like this brush and it is working for me. It is comfortable, it is long enough to reach where I otherwise cannot and it seems to be made well. My one complaint is the terrible smell of the bristles when they’re wet, which I can only hope will diminish over time.

title: Great Clippers, But Use With Caution
text:
I keep a set of nail clippers in my office where I can find them. I frequently find small cuts around my fingernails, particularly after working with heavy equipment in metal racks, and the clippers come in handy to trim away torn bits of skin. Having them in the office is great, but that doesn’t help me when I am on the go and need a pair in my go-bag. This pair of clippers has answered that need.

These are large, sharp clippers and they open wide. They’re suitable for cutting fingernails, toenails, zip ties, small wires and a lot more. There are a couple of important points I’d like to make.

First, these are very comfortable to use. The lever has rounded edges and the cutting blades are very sharp, so these are very easy to use without hurting the fingers doing the squeezing. If you have worked with dull clippers, clippers that have been damaged or clippers that have a handle with well-defined corners, you know why this is important.

The other point is more of a caution. Being very sharp is important, but these also happen to open wider than the average cheap clippers you find in between the registers at the grocery store. There is a very real possibility of cutting the skin unintentionally if used without a little care. The cut might be clean, but that doesn’t mean it will bleed less or hurt less.

This are very nice clippers and they work well. However, I would recommend a little caution when using them because of how wide they open and how sharp they are.

title: Works Very Well
text:
I have a Remington shaver and I am very pleased with it, so I was interested in this body hair trimmer for my wife who has been looking for a more convenient way to shave her legs. It has proven to be a fine trimmer and though it does not cut as close as a blade razor it is more than acceptable.

I love the hand feel of this trimmer. The rubbery mesh on the body makes it easy to hold even when wet, and the overall unit is balanced and not awkward at all in terms of weight. It is about the right size too, making it a good fit for any sized hand.

It does take a little time to charge it up from completely dead to completely full. I did not time it well but it did take 3-4 hours to charge, which is not bad.

Several other reviewers here have stated that it’s not suitable for facial hair. I agree to a point. It does a good job of evening up sideburns, but it does require a gentle hand and some patience. Using it to shave would be a painful experience, and just trimming down sideburns is not exactly comfortable if you are heavy-handed. Using a comb as a guide and a guard, it does a great job of trimming eyebrows, one of the main uses I have for a trimmer like this.

My wife took this trimmer and used it to shave her legs and it did a good job for her. She said it was not uncomfortable and it left her legs mostly smooth. And, she did not have any cuts or chafes from this trimmer like she does with razors.

This trimmer comes with comb attachments for hair length. These are useful when wanting to shorten hair instead of cut it off completely.

Overall, we are pleased with this trimmer. It does a good job, it’s easy to use and it has good hand feel.

title: Works for Me
text:
I have trouble with dry skin (fortunately not itchy), particularly on my face and forehead. I have tried other lotions and creams to help with the dryness but I have had limited success in finding a solution. I hoped that this particular lotion would be of some help, and it does better than most at relieving the dryness.

Compared to the lotion I had been using prior, this lotion is much thinner and more amorphous, though not runny. It spreads easily and my skin absorbs it easily enough, without feeling oily, greasy or pasty. It doesn’t have much of a fragrance either which is particularly good - I am not a fan of lotions heavy on perfume smells.

After a day’s use, I noticed that my skin is appreciably less dry and I see less flaking on areas where I have applied the lotion. It doesn’t leave my skin feeling oily, a problem I have had with other lotions and creams.

I’m pleased with this lotion. It hasn’t eliminated my dry facial skin, but it has definitely helped.

title: Works Well, but Expensive and I Don't Like the Charging Cable
text:
I selected this little facial massager as I have been using an electric shaver and was hopeful it would make shaving just a touch more comfortable. I will be very up-front in saying that it doesn’t seem to help stimulate my face to where the hair cuts easier, but I will say it’s a relaxing device to use and it does help to ease facial muscles.

This is a small little device about the size of a cordless mouse. It’s contoured to fit comfortably in the hand and it has several very fine rows of rubber bristles that serve as the massaging surface. Being wireless this unit is rechargeable and it seems to hold a charge for a good little while. So far, I have had it for a couple of months and it has only needed to be fully recharged once.

This little gizmo has a couple of different modes and the speed can be adjusted to make it speed up or slow down, so it vibrates and massages the facial skin more effectively. It has a built-in timer function and it will signal you when it is time to move the massager to a different spot on your face or neck. The vibration and bristles work together to stimulate the skin and muscles underneath, and when in use it does make my skin feel more relaxed when I’ve finished.

One of the things I have discovered is that, if you are prone to dry skin, this device does a fair job of exfoliating the skin. If I have used it dry instead of wet, I find it covered in dead skin particles and I need to wash it off to get it clean.

The unit is rechargeable and the plug uses a barrel connector and special cable. This is unfortunate and I am disappointed that it does not use a regular USB connector. If you lose the cable or it breaks, getting a replacement is not as easy as just grabbing another USB cable.

Other than the charging cable, this is a nifty little massager that does help relax facial skin. I am hard-pressed to say it’s worth the asking price ($200 as I write this), but it does work and it does make your skin feel more relaxed and softer.

title: Changing My Perspective on Electric Shavers
text:
I have always used traditional razors for shaving through I have tried an electric shaver in the past. I wasn’t a fan. So, I was apprehensive about using this shaver by Remington. After using it for a little over a week, it has changed my perception of electric shavers. It provides a close shave that is comfortable, though I can still get a close shave more quickly with a bladed razor.

This unit is approximately the size of a compact digital camera. It is a hefty thing for its size and it surprised me when I picked it up - I expected it to be lighter. It’s very solidly built so I think it will survive drops and jostles. So far, no complaints.

It comes with just two modes, on and off (not that it needs anything else). The switch is a silver lever on the side and it is nice and tight so it will not toggle while trying to use the shaver. When on, the shaver is quite noisy but not terrible; it is enough that it can be heard in the next room through a closed door, but not down a flight of stairs. It does vibrate a bit, but even with wet hands it is easy to hang on to the shaver and maintain complete control.

Comfort-wise, this shaver came as a very pleasant surprise. The shaver I used in the past felt like I was pulling the whiskers out of my face instead of cutting them. This shaver doesn’t give me that problem. It does tug very, very gently, but it is not uncomfortable and the majority of the action is cutting, not pulling.

As for the closeness: I can get a shave that is very close to that which I can get with straight razors. However, it takes me a lot longer to get a close shave with this shaver than if I used razors. To get a really close shave I have to go over several areas of my face repeatedly, every morning, and invariably there are a couple of spots that require I be a contortionist to get my skin smooth (and I suspect part of that is my relative lack of practice with shavers like this one). On the flip side, it’s practically impossible to cut myself with this shaver and I regard that as a fair trade.

Maintenance is very simple. The documentation explains how to care for the shaver and states that it can be washed in water. Because I use it to dry shave I have found a much easier method. After I am finished, I pop off the cover and spray the blades and screen with a canned duster which does a fantastic job. Because of this I discovered that the shaver has a side benefit, at least in my case, in that it exfoliates the skin a bit. I have been startled by the amount of skin flakes it captures along with the hairs.

It has a MicroUSB interface for charging. In the time I have had it I have not yet needed to charge it. I have no idea how long it maintains a charge, but it’s good to go for travel.

So far I am very pleased with this shaver. It is easy to use, it shaves me well and it holds a a charge for quite a while. If you favor electric shavers and you want one that does a good job for a good price, this is one to consider.

title: Large and Economical Bottle of Soap
text:
We use liquid soap in the house all the time and we’re always on the lookout for large bottles of soap that will last. This looked like a promising supply that would last for months. Unfortunately, I am the only one in the house that likes the smell of it. In spite of that, it’s good soap and I have no qualms with recommending it regardless of my family’s dislike of it.

This is a gel-type soap, not a cream soap. This is not what you want if you really prefer cream soaps. Just sayin’... It is also not anti-bacterial, which for me is a plus. Anti-bacterial soaps kill good bacteria along with the bad and this can cause skin irritation. If you have problems with anti-bacterial soaps, this one does not fall into that category.

In a foaming dispenser, this soap does well and you get a nice, fragrant lather that helps clean away dirt and some oils/grease.

The fragrance is the sticking point in my house. To me, it has a distinct odor that resembles sun tan lotion, because of the coconut fragrance. For me that’s fine, but my family does not like this fragrance and as a result I found myself being the only one to use it. It’s not a strong fragrance at all (I don’t think so anyway) but the others in the house really just have no use for it and stay away.

This is a nice economical bottle of soap that will go a long way, even in a house full of people unless it is used wastefully. I think it smells nice and it does a nice job of cleaning my hands.

title: Generous Size, Smells Nice, Works Well for Household Hand-Washing
text:
My wife and I use liquid hand soap in the kitchen as well as in the bathrooms, and we have carefully avoided antibacterial soaps when possible. I was interested in trying this hand soap and so far we have been pleased with it.

First off, the bottle is large though affordable. That’s a big plus right out of the gate. Assuming non-wasteful usage, it will last a while.

It smells nice too, very fresh and pleasant. There are two types of smells when it comes to soaps, clean and heavy (like perfume). This falls into the former category and has a very fresh, clean fragrance that you can smell on your hands afterwards but doesn’t linger forever.

It seems to do a reasonable job of cleaning our hands as well. I have not tried it after working on something greasy and filthy like working on the car, but it does a good job of cutting through canola and other coatings like you’d find in a kitchen or household.

This is a decent bottle of soap. It is a good size, smells nice so far has worked well for us.

title: Smells Nice and Does a Good Job of Dandruff Controll
text:
I have been using Head & Shoulders for a while now, and it has worked out for me. It definitely controls dandruff fairly well and it does smell decent. I was unaware that there was an apple scented H&S so this was a pleasant surprise. The fact that it comes in a big bottle is a bonus.

The main difference between this and the regular H&S is the scent. The original smells clean and fresh though it is not the absolute best-smelling shampoo I have used. This bottle is very reminiscent of green apples (the point), though it does still retain the soapy undertones that are typical of scented shampoos. It’s s step up from the regular fragrance, and it does the same job as the original at controlling dandruff.

The bottle itself is large which is great. I like that it doesn’t run out in a couple of weeks (unless you waste a lot). The larger bottle does mean being mindful of how you keep it stored in the shower as it can be a little heavy for some caddy systems and it can potentially just be too big to fit. Also interesting to me is the pump instead of the squirt nozzle. This is cleaner than a typical shampoo dispenser and it also makes it so that there’s no need to actually pick up the bottle to get shampoo out of it, important when it is full and on the heavier side.

This is a good product in H&S’s lineup. It smells nice, comes in a generous size and has a pump instead of a squirt top. It works just as well as the original H&S, but it smells better. This is an easy one to recommend.

title: A Nice Cushion for a Spa Tub
text:
My wife enjoys a good soak in the bathtub when afforded extra time and I thought this bath neck/head cushion would make her time even more pleasant. I was right and it is a comfortable addition to the tub, but it does not fit all tubs equally.

This is a very simple item, really. It is a heart-shaped (more or less) hard foam rubber cushion, angled on the back to contour to the edge of the tub with three suction cups attached to hold it in place. Wet the cups (not necessary but recommended), stick it to the edge of the tub and it provides a very nice cradle for the head and neck when in the tub. I did try it when I positioned it in the bathtub and it seems to be contoured just about perfectly and held my head at the correct angle to give good comfort.

Here’s the catch, though - it is designed for larger, spa-type tubs or standing tubs, not the lower cost standard tub one finds in a spec home or builder’s supply and have a short ledge. The ledge is just too short to support the cushion and even with the suction cups it cannot be secured properly. Considering that this is the majority of the size of bath tubs people encounter, this limits where this cushion can be used. Most newer homes I have seen have a spa tub, but this is not the case in many older homes.

In the right tub, this is a wonderful cushion that works surprisingly well considering its simplicity. It really does provide good neck and head support. Just be aware that it cannot be used everywhere.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.

title: Convenient and Works Well for My Needs
text:
I use electric clippers to clean up between haircuts - sideburns, eyebrows, etc. I would consider this to be light duty for any clippers, and in this role these clippers do a fine job. I have not tried them on larger jobs but I suspect they'd be more than sufficient.

These clippers are very lightweight and compact. Remington did a good job of designing these to be convenient for the traveler, even though that's probably not their intended use... In spite of the built-in rechargeable battery, these clippers are very light which actually makes them easier to use.

I am impressed with the battery life. Having charged them when I received them, I have not charged them since and the clippers are still going strong. The documentation says they will run for approximately 40 minutes on a charge but I have gotten better life from a charge than that.

With a proper cable the clippers can be charged via USB, though I do not have the right size cable for this.

Cleaning the clippers is a snap. With the push of a button the blades pop forward, making cleaning out the blades simple. Using a can of compressed air, getting out any little bits of hair and dandruff is effortless.

Though not something I use every day, these clippers meet my needs admirably. There's no fumbling with an awkward cord when using them, they are lightweight and are easy to adjust and clean.

title: From slightly dry to slightly oily
text:
I struggle with dry skin and I was excited to try this product, as Dove has always made gentle products that have irritated my skin less than some other brands. I have mixed results with this product, though overall I am pleased with it.

First, I appreciate that the bottle is easy to open, which is something I have learned not to take for granted. I have used bath and body products that are packaged such that it is next to impossible to open the packaging. This is not one of them.

The fragrance is actually very pleasant, on the masculine side but not overpowering. After a good shower there is still the slightest hint of the fragrance left behind, enough that it can be picked up when close but not enough to tell when more than a couple of feet away.

The gel lathers up nicely and washes off nicely too.

My only real complaint is that after using it, my skin is no longer dry but is actually slightly oily. I do not have severe dry skin so perhaps this product is meant for people who have more of a problem with dryness. The oiliness is short-term, though, and after skipping a day my skin returns to normal.

This is a nice product for men with dry skin. It smells nice and it leave you feeling clean. If you struggle with severe dry skin this product will please you. If, like me, you have slightly dry skin you may feel a little oily afterward - keep this in mind when shopping for bath products.

Since it says upfront that you should not expect as close of a shave compared to other Gillette products, I think it accomplishes what it is designed to do. If you have sensitive skin, this might be a good option to try. But, if you end up needing to shave twice in one day, the additional shaving may offset the reduced skin irritation.

text:

I had to set it down and give my hand a break because it was too hot to hold for a prolonged period. I would not say I have particularly sensitive hands, and I've never experienced this with any other straightener. That alone is a deal breaker for me.
I did like the on/off button placement and the twist dial at the bottom to easily control temperature. And it was very smooth, with no pulling, as I ran it through my hair. It did however require more passes though my hair to style it, and it took longer to get my hair straight. For reference my favorite straightener is the Babyliss Pro Nano Titanium, which is currently $130 on Amazon. I'd personally pass on this one.

title: Great dryer - the third Babyliss I've owned
text:
I've owned the Babyliss BAB 200 Ceramix, the Nano Titanium, and now this model. When I'm ready to purchase a new dryer, I will get the Ceramix again if it's the cheapest.

In a nutshell, they are all great dryers, far superior to anything I've ever bought from Target in every way, and they are all very similar models with the same wattage. I don't find any noticeable difference in the 3 models in terms of how long it takes to dry my hair or the end apppearance of my hair. Which really only leaves me with small details to compare.

My first Babyliss was the Ceramix and I loved the buttons the most on that one and loved the way the cord wrapped around the head of the dryer for easy storage. It lasted me about three years of daily use before I purchased the Nano Titanium.
I have been using the Nano Titanium the past two years and that is my least favorite of the three. Although it is by far the lightest model, which is nice because the Ceramix can get heavy, I dislike the buttons and am constantly accidentally turning the dryer off or the heat down while I grip the handle. The shape of the head and the slippery plastic make it such that every time I try to wrap the cord around it, it just slips right off in to a tangled mess. So although it dries my hair well, it tends to annoy me.
This Italo falls somewhat in between in terms of weight and ability to wrap the cord, and I haven't accidentally toggled any buttons. The color is fun as well. This will probably end up being my favorite of the three, and if price isn't a concern, I'd recommend this one. Personally I'll likely get the black Ceramix again if it's $20 cheaper!

title: Decent lotion
text:
Before trying this on my skin I went to Enviromental Working Group's website ewg.org and searched each ingredient. They have an extensive skin and cosmetics database that ranks products and ingredients with a hazard rating. The hazard score, a 1-10 scale from low to high hazard, reflects known and suspected hazards. Most ingredients used in this lotion were ranked with little known hazard at 1 and 2. There were a few 3's and 4's and one 5. With those ratings I'm willing to put this on my skin.

The lotion itself is fragrance free and pretty thick. Because it is so thick you really don't need much. I'm only using this on the back side of my arms and I can see it lasting 6-12 months of daily use. Also because it is so thick it doesn't absorb very quickly, but I just put it on before bed and was fine with it slowly sinking in. It's definitely not greasy or gritty, which I like.

After using for 2 weeks, it definitely reduced bumps. They aren't completely gone, but my skin is smoother and the remaining bumps are smaller. Hopefully after using it for longer they will entirely go away.

title: Pleasantly Surprised
text:
I honestly wasn't expecting a ton from this brand I'd never heard of, but I really like this straightener! It worked great on my medium, wavy hair that is a few inches past my shoulders. It took a little less than 10 min to get it completely straight.

I've tried three other $100+ straighteners. A Chi that I loved but was more expensive, a Bio Ionic OnePass (which I hated because it felt like it was pulling through my hair and leaving it scraggly, and paid $30 to send back), and I am currently on my second Babyliss Pro Titanium. The first Babyliss was awesome and the second, supposedly same exact thing, is not quite as good. I'd say this falls between my two Babyliss irons. It glides through my hair very smoothly, leaving it frizz free and very straight. My hair feels silky smooth! It also heats up quickly, about 1 minute. I do prefer a 1 1/4 or 1.5 inch iron myself, but it honestly didn't make that much difference in terms of how long it took me to straighten. I assume it would make a bigger difference for curling.

Since prices tend to fluctuate on Amazon, it's hard to evaluate fairly, but at its current price of $180, that's the only thing holding me back from giving 5 stars. My comparable Babyliss irons were about $120.

title: BABNT5548 Titanium vs BAB2000 Ceramix
text:
Having previously owned the BAB2000 Ceramix, I wasn't sure if I wanted to spend roughly 50% more on this model. I decided to try it and here's my comparison.
Titanium Pros: Lightweight!! The Black Ceramix model is pretty heavy, much heavier than typical models I used to purchase from Target. So heavy my arm would get tired and I really never got used to it after three years of use. In my opinion this would be the main reason to purchase this one over the Ceramix.

I did not notice any significant difference in the speed at which either dried my hair or the shine or hair volume.

Titanium Cons: Buttons. The heat switch and on off switch are very easily toggled on and off. They are also right where you hold it, so pretty much every time I use it I find myself accidentally switching the heat setting from high to medium or turning it off. The buttons on the Ceramix never had this problem.
Shape of dryer. Because of the shape, every time I try to wrap the cord around the head of the dryer it all slides off in to a tangled mess. This is really annoying to me for storing it. I also never had this problem with the Ceramix as that easily wound around itself to store neatly.

Bottom line: I like this dryer for the fast drying power and light weight, but if I had to choose again I would go for the BAB2000 Ceramix Extreme since it's cheaper and easier to use and store.

title: DOES NOT STAY ON IN HOT & HUMID WEATHER!
text:
I was thrilled to receive this product, and yes, I got a legitimate one, not a knock off. And I was ecstatic at how easy it was to apply and how well it concealed my dark under eye circles and other blemishes. Well my happiness was short lived. I had just finished my makeup and was about to head out for the evening when I looked back in the mirror, and to my horror (and soul-crushing disappointment,) saw that it was, for lack of a better word, dissolving in the areas I’d applied it—especially under my eyes. There were bald patches and a ton of seperation.
I had applied a matifying primer before using the concealer, and I applied a good setting powder on top. I had to remove my full face of makeup and start fresh with my old concealer. I was quite pissed, to be perfectly honest! I live in the south where it’s hot and humid. If you’re thinking of buying this product for the first time (and live in a humid area,) you may want to wait until fall or winter. I gave this product a generous 3 stars because it did apply and conceal fabulously, before it all went horribly wrong. And the only reason I’m not returning it for a full refund is that I want to try it again once the weather cools down. I sincerely hope it doesn’t fail me a second time. And on a side note, I would’ve been positively mortified if it had broken down once I was out in public, with no way to fix my face. It was that bad.
