Based on my experience and judging by the other reviews this isn't a frequent thing I can only say buyer beware.

title: Attractive, Well Done
text: These are quite high quality, very reflective and shiny and the adhesive lasts a long time and holds very well. You can get some stunning looks with these. There's a variety of sizes, shapes and colors. Good for all ages. Highly recommended.

title: Works for Clippers and Razors
text: I've used this both on rotary head razors and my hair clippers. I'm fairly certain this would work for sewing machine, knives, knife sharpening. Anywhere a fine light oil is needed. But as there's three or four electric razors and two sets of hair clippers this is probably a lifetime supply of oil since you only need a drop per application.

title: Good Shave
text:
I previously had another brand seven (7) head razor that broke after a handful of shaves. I put these to a workout since I shave my head several times a week. These large razors seem to conform to my head better than the 5 or 6 head models do. This give a good, close, shave and because of the surface area it covers you can shave in half the time a straight foil razor. The only issue I have with this and just about ever round cutting head razors is if, like me, you wear a goatee as you trim around the beard these will rip the hair right out of your face. If you're careful though, you can get a good shave out of this.
See my attached photos for, what I feel, is the best way to hold this razor. Battery body held on the back of the hand, the connecting shaft between the fingers and the razor heads against the palm of your hand.

title: Different
text:
I'd like to kick whomever packed this in the shins. It came done up in feet of heavy plastic wrap and lots and lots of packing tape. Why not put it in a zip top bag and wrap that against damage. This comes in a soft plastic bottle which you really don't want to take a knife to without risking puncturing the bottle. This leaked all over inside the plastic, as well as the box it was shipped in. I smelled good as did the box when I finally got it unwrapped.
The scent is good. Reasonably strong and lasts a good while. It, to me, feels like a mix of the old Mennen aftershave my dad liked and the stuff and the stuff my barber would spritz on me after he shaved my head. The application is slightly different and the spray cap will come off in the protective cover unless you are careful.
I like it.

title: This is a Decent Razor
text:
I've been using a Gillette Fusion I got as a review item right up until I went through the blades for it and I had to go looking for replacements. I just couldn't justify the price, they're TOO expensive. I got this Solimo handle and 14 blade replacements cartridges for less than the price of an 8-pack of Gillette cartridges.
The angle of the Solimo razor is a bit extreme. Much flatter than any other razor I've used in my 40+ years of shaving. I can do my head fairly well though I have to go at a couple spots more than once but I experience that with every razor. The one spot I really have trouble with is my left cheek and neck. I've got some arthritis issues in my elbows and getting my arm to bend the right way to shave there is painful and takes some effort.
I can usually get 6 or 7 head and face shaves before the blades start to dull. This says these have lubricating strips but they don't seem to dissolve or wear away like others do. Once the blades feel dull I can go 1 or 2 more shaves before I have to switch the head out.
For the price this a rather decent razor.

title: Nice, Not Great
text: These stickers are nice. That's about as far as I'm willing to go on their praise. They're nice. The biggest issue is the stickers have a border of additional plastic. I get that it has to be there otherwise they would shred trying to get them off the backing paper. The problem is the plastic they're printed on is cheap. It isn't very clear so even on a light grey background you can see the border standing out like a sore thumb. It's too visible. It detracts from the look. Also, because of their size, the glow in the dark material lasts a couple minutes at best. It just doesn't glow long enough to be cool.

title: An Old Friend of a Scent
text:
This reminds me something of Mennen an old aftershave we used in the 70s and 80s. It's also reminiscent of the aftershave my barber sprayed when he shaved my head.
This was very hard to unwrap and get out of the packaging. It was covered with layers and layers of plastic wrap and packing tape. It leaked a fair amount as I was tearing the packaging off. Because the bottle is thin plastic I didn't want to use a knife or scissors in fear of puncturing the product.
There's a collar and sleep combination that is supposed to keep it from being accidentally sprayed. I've found it just rips the nozzle free when you try and take it off.
I like the scent and there's quite a lot of it. Eight (8) ounces if I'm not mistaken. This should last a while.

title: Nearly Razor Sharp
text: The blade, out of the box will lift the hair odd your arm but the blade is rough, snags and stutters along your skin. Some work with a 3,000 grit stone and a decent leather strop (it comes with one but the quality is lacking). The straight razor is cool. A conversation piece. Something to display or show your friends. I'm not sure I'd trust it shaving my throat. But it is a neat addition to my weird collection of cutting things.

title: (Not So) Great Shave - Edited
text:
Edit: I had reviewed this just the other day. This review hasn't gone live yet. I've used this razor five times to shave my head prior to today. The sixth time, today, I shaved my head with a clean razor. I always clean up when I use it. Today was no exception. I shaved then went to open the shave heads to rinse them out and the very first one snapped, the cover on the bottom fell away. The razor head completely detached from the unit. There are several broken shards of plastic where the hinge that allows the heads to open shattered. Razor is now useless and in the trash. At least I got six shaves before it died. Rating dropped from 4-stars to 1-star. I didn't use excessive force. I own several razors in this style, though this was the first 7-head unit. My 5-head is over a year old, been used a dozen or more times and is fine. Very disappointed in this product.

I have several multiple head razors 5,6 and now this 7 head model. These give a good, reasonably close shave. The only problem I've had with all of these units is I, as you can see in the picture, wear a goatee and every single one of these razors will grab beard hair and tear it the hell out. Besides that though when you use these with a positive grip they're easy to use and give a good shave. Battery life is pretty impressive. I shave my head, neck and cheeks and get easily seven to ten shaves before it's down low enough I feel the need to recharge. Another bonus is it seems all these heads are interchangeable so if one's low on charge or fits your hand better you can just swap to a different handle or head. However you like.

title: I Have a Couple Issues
text:
First I want to say though I haven't tried all of the varieties that came in this box the several I have used smelled great!
But I have run into several issues:
• First this is something you need to unwrap as you're getting into the shower. These are tightly wrapped and the plastic is, while protective, a pain to completely remove. Twice now I've ended up with bits of plastic littering the shower stall.
• Building on the first issue these pucks are quite soft. I've used other shower pucks from brands like Vicks and they're many times harder and to be honest, easier to cut out of their wrappings.
• I guess building on the first two problems because they're so soft these are nearly completely dissolved before I'm even done shaving my head (something I do with a blade razor while sitting in the shower) so half my shower smells good or I have to come up with a way to have a second soft, crumbly, shower puck on hand but dry and within reach so once the first is gone I can start on a second.
So I guess this can be boiled down to two annoying issues:
1 • They're a pain to unwrap. The plastic used is terrible.
2 • They're not pressed hard enough so they dissolve way too quick.
I really like the several scents I've tried and look forward to trying the rest over time. While I'd like to see the pucks pressed a bit harder I wouldn't want them as compressed as the Vicks, those barely are gone at the end of the shower. Somewhere in the middle would be nice.

title: Long Lasting Spicy Scent
text: I found the tang of this cologne to be a bit spicy for me. There's a sharp note I really didn't care that much for. The scent isn't horrible but it's not me. It lasts a seriously long time. I sprayed one wrists, wiped the other with it and 7-8 hours later it was still as potent as when I applied it which is also how I knew this wasn't my scent since it didn't disappear from my knowledge like a good cologne should.

title: I Have Concerns
text: I like the aftershave version of this product. I wear it whenever I go out and even sometimes just lounging around the house. So sure, I'll take another bottle that smells as good. This actually seems a hair stronger and lasts longer than the regular aftershave. My two concerns are there's particles floating around in this bottle. Quite a lot of them in fact. I don't know if those are the pheromones or what but that bothers me to no end. I don't think they can make it out the spray nozzle though they may clog it and who knows what they are. The product also goes on oily and takes a while to dry.

title: My New Scent
text: I have this in a 4oz. bottle and jumped at the chance to have a little more in a travel size. The cologne/aftershave does have an old 60s or 70s vibe but I like the scents from back then and it brings out the nostalgia in me. My godfather wore something that smelled very similar to this and I miss him dearly. With the travel size I can toss this in a carry-on or even in the console of my car and freshen up my scent when I need  or want to.

title: I Like These Wipes
text: I keep wipes around all the time, here in the living room, in the bathroom and in the car. I'm disabled and greasy or slippery hands can cause my hands to slip off my walker's handles and injure myself. These have a pleasant scent and decently thick as well as comfortably soft. They also have a decent amount of moisture so stay damp even in the heat of the car.

title: Smells Good
text: I like the scent, spices and a woody note that lasts quite a while. Goes on almost completely dry and didn't irritate my armpits. I'm trying to think of anything else to say about it and there really isn't. It's a deodorant.

title: Okay For Kids
text: I use bath bombs and Vicks VaporShower units in the shower. This only partially dissolved when I tried it, it was amusing and smelled pretty good. I can see how a kid would enjoy having this in a bathtub before bedtime.

title: Practically Useless
text: I wear cloth, nylon/polyester mostly, masks when I need to and these stickers that had barely any scent to them wouldn't stay on more than half an hour at best. These were useless. I cannot recommend them.

title: Works Well
text: I've been healing tattoos for close to 30 years. Even my recent tattoos done within the last couple years I've used, with the recommendation of my artist of course, using A&D ointment for 3-5 days then switching to a good moisturizing lotion. This goes on easy, stays in place well and I had no issues healing my ink with it.

title: Not Comfortable
text: I tired this a couple times and found it weird. It's strange and not really all that good feeling on the eyes. I didn't like this at all

title: Good Scent, Lasts
text: Goes on easy, it's a spray deodorant. You can spray it all over but mostly it goes on damp and dries quick. Scent lasts though is mild and not overpowering. Has not irritated my skin and I've used it numerous times. Can mix well with other colognes or aftershaves. Does not leave residue behind and doesn't seem to stain clothes.

title: Refreshing Shower Addition
text: My shower's not perfect for these things but I can, from time to time, aim the handheld shower head towards the tablet. I really like the scent and vapor these put off. It reminds me very much of the eucalyptus spray they had in the steam room at the gym I used to go to three times a week. These last for 10 - 15 minutes in my shower which is just about perfect for me.  A good way to freshen up any shower.

title: Really Good Tweezers
text: I somehow lost my last pair of angled tweezers. I keep them by my 3D printer to quick snag the pre-printing ooze that slides out of the nozzle on most 3D printers. The curved tip makes this easier. I've also used them to pull hair and pick debris off my keyboard and electronics. All around handy and well made tweezers.

title: Very Citrusy
text: This a decent man's cologne with a reasonable longevity to the scent. There a very intense citrus note for the first ten to fifteen minutes but that lifts a bit and then the scent lasts a few hours. I enjoyed this. The bottle is striking and makes a very nice gift.

title: Not For Men
text: I don't have a problem with some woman's cologne. There's quite a few with tones and scents that are unisex. This is a bit feminine but a decent scent overall. Right on the box though it says it's to 'Attract Male'. That being said I'm not looking to attract anyone, I just like to smell good on the rare occasions I go out. Wish they'd written the product description better I'd probably have skipped this one but they said it was a scent for men not to attract men.

title: Has a Very Cinnamon Overtone
text: It's not a bad aftershave, once it has had time to settle down it has a nice and reasonably long mellow scent but right after applying there's a very heavy cinnamon scent. Good, I'll use it but not one of my favorites.

title: Good Shaver For the Scalp
text:
I have used five headed head-shavers in the past, in fact until I got this six headed razor I was using it. This seems to contour to my head a little better than the five head razor, they do about the same in closeness which isn't bad at all. I've gotten better shaves from the barber but these do a very good job at home.

I've found the best way to hold these types is to put the head in the palm of your hand and the body on the back of your hand. This lets you cover the whole of your head easily and with a better sense of the contours of your skull. Remember to remove the center head when cleaning the razor.

title: I Like the Scent
text:
The scent is nice, I really do like it. But this goes on oily as it's an oil base, so I can't just spray my scalp or armpits with it. You need to apply small drops with the applicator which means you overly oil your skin or the scent goes away because you didn't use enough. I can't say anything about the attractant of the pheromones, no women tore my clothes off or even noticed the scent when I was around them.
Good scent, kinda oily, doesn't draw in the women (never expected it to).

title: Versatile, More Than Just for Makeup
text: Kinda cheating. I don't wear makeup all that often if ever but I needed a brush to clean the lenses of my camera which had gotten dusty to the point of impacting my photos. I looked at some brushes made for cameras and stumbled upon this brush and it's been perfect. I tested it on my glasses to see that there wasn't anything IN the brush, oils or chemicals that might leave smudges and there weren't. Left no trace on the glass so I've added this to my camera kit to clean my lenses. I'm sure it's great for putting on blush but it's also great for getting spots off your camera lenses.

title: Too Short, Needs a Bend
text:
The first problem I had with this is the handle is kinda short and makes it hard to reach all of my back. Good for doing my legs but the handle needs to be a little longer and needs a bend to make washing your back easier.
Second problem is you're not supposed to use this on your delicate parts or your face. This means you have to put a large amount of soap on this to do the majority of your body and then more soap on your pouf or washcloth to wash the rest of you. It's wasteful.
My third issue is charging. I don't have a big counter in my bathroom and only have one outlet so I need to find a place to stash the proprietary (ugh!) charging cable and then take it out of the bathroom once it's dry to charge it. Too much work. I can get just as clean with a pouf.

title: Terrible Soap
text: It's like taking a shower with 60-grit sandpaper. It was uncomfortable to say the least. There was so much grit it would barely lather up and took forever to rinse the mess out of my shower pouf. I tried this once and absolutely hated it. This was the worst soap I've ever tried.

title: Very Nice
text: Goes on easy, stays on forever. Very kissable with little transfer to the kissee. Makes the lips feel moisturized all day long. Barely had to use chapstick.

title: Utterly Useless
text: Scent is nothing. Not there. Put in a shoe, my walker bag, on my favorite Covid mask. There's a vague scent for a second or two then. . . nothing whatsoever. These are so small they're hard to handle. I had to photograph the back of the box (about the size of two pennies) and blow up the image to read the instructions. I don't know what these are really designed for but I can't smell anything moments after opening the package (no, it's not a Covid side effect) so I can't see any reason to have these around unless you'd like poorly shaped four-leaf clovers to stick to things. Not worth anything.

title: These Are Hit or Miss in Quality
text:
I've had this razor in black for a while now and it's surprisingly good at shaving my head. Better in some areas than a very expensive Braun. This is, despite advertising, a 5-head razor, not a 4-head, the center is a set of blades and most definitely needs to be cleaned with the rest.
I had to replace this under warranty, the first would not snap on in a positive way and retain the connection between the shaving head and the battery body. It would, if you used the grip method detailed in the instructions where you have the heads inside your palm and the battery/control box part outside on the back of your hand. My black version stays together perfectly and comes apart easily for cleaning. The first white razor I received would pop apart the instant your fingers got a grip on the heads. Unit is sturdy as it survived several falls to the floor. Replacement razor was better but still lacking a solid lock on the head unit to the body. I can shave with it but I have to be ready to catch things if it blows apart.
White unit is also in Chinese characters and there is NO option to change the display to English.
Battery life is decent.

title: Nice!
text: Goes on smooth and creamy. Lasts forever. Doesn't smudge much. Looks great. Can't got wrong with this one.

title: Attractive Rose Tattoo
text: Nicely sized, very attractive and long lasting temporary tattoo. These go on really easy and last an exceptionally long time. This set is four of the same tattoo design so you and three friends can have matching images or you can renew your tattoo over and over to keep it around for a while. Also be good for movies or photoshoots where you need to look the same several times in a row.

title: Well Made
text: Very sturdy, well made, a bit heavy. An attractive crown. Gotta have a good amount of hair to hold this in place. Short hair may not hold well and this crown being heavy could come off.

title: Good Unisex Scent
text: I'm a guy and I really like this scent. It's named woody and does have hints and overtones of the forest. I know, I spent a lot of my life wandering the woods. The scent is never overpowering lasts an okay amount of time. I'd be happier with it if I got a few more hours out of it but I really like this.

title: Well Made, A Little Light
text: Could use more weight in the base, when I got this the bottom was wet with some oily substance that had me nervous so I washed it like mad with isopropyl alcohol and it looks like I got all of it. Currently using this as a spooky decoration. For next Halloween I think I'll be doing some painting and I I have a crown I want to attach to the top. Going to have to see how things go. Neck is excessively long for some reason.

title: Poor Shave, Great Nose/Ear Clippers
text: These multihead razors work best when held in reverse, the blades in your palm and the body on the backs of your fingers. This razor does not fit well in that position at all. Worse the three heads conform very poorly to the scalp. Shaving my head was painful, rough and it did not provide a very close shave. Even worse than that when pressing down to try and get a close shave even in high power mode (this has two power modes) you can hear the motor struggling to keep up. As a razor it's not great. It works okay as a face scrubber with the white brush. I found using it as a set of clippers to be very awkward. The round body is strange to hold when trying to do precise trimming. The one adapter I found to be very useful? The nose and ear hair trimmer. The ball shaped motor housing it quite easy to hold when stuffing the cutter into your nostril or running it around the edge of your ear hole. With the high power mode mode it does this job nicely and the battery life when trimming just your nose and occasionally the stray ear hair. Otherwise this unit is fairly useless. I'm going to keep it as a nose/ear hair trimmer.

title: Not Horrible, Not Fantastic
text:
I don't know if my images will upload in the correct order, Amazon has had a problem with mixing them up. I've uploaded nine images taken over eight days. These go on VERY faint and take quite a while, two days or more, to darken up properly. Do understand that the film is not on the wrong side. The dark black image is just to let you see the design the very dim side is the proper side to apply to your skin. I suggest doubling or tripling the application time as stated in the instructions on the product listing. NO instructions are included with the package. There's also something else to be advised of. It's mentioned in the listing but important enough to mention again. Once applied there is NO way to remove these temporary tattoos. Be careful where you put them as they're going to be there for a couple weeks.
The one I applied I followed their 10 second instructions and the final product darkened up fairly well but there's a bit of. . . bad photocopy look to it. I think if I'd left it in place longer it would look better. From a distance or in lower lighting it still looks okay. A decent temporary tattoo.

title: Close Shave, Needs Work
text:
As other reviewers have found and mentioned if you hold the body of this razor in the two finger grip like the instruction suggest (they don't illustrate the technique) which is holding the blades on the palm side of your hand, the shaft of the razor between fore and middle fingers and the body of the razor on the back of your fingers. I added a couple photographs for detail.
I don't think the sellers know what they have or are selling. First it says five heads, then four. When I contacted them they said the product had recently been changed. *I* received a 5-head unit. There were no instructions on removing the center head (you turn it then pry it up) I thought it was just a spacer to help the razor glide across your skin but when examining the razor I found the center clogged with several shavings worth of hair. So, check your razor carefully. It could be a 4-head, it could be a 5-head like mine.
Unit holds a charge for a while. I've gotten 5 or 6 shaves out of it. That's my whole head, cheeks and throat. I wear a goatee. Speaking of that. If you have facial or hair anywhere near where you're going to shave, use caution! This will grab hair and yank it out.
The unit doesn't conform all that great to my skull but the two-finger grip gives me way better control and I can get a fairly decent shave from this razor especially on the back of my head near my neck. I have to say that holding the razor the way I show in my photos I can get the back of my head shaved better than just about any razor I've tried.
The razor, like most, needs to be lubricated after cleaning so it runs and cuts properly. Unfortunately the seller, without telling people has removed the bottle of oil from the box on units for sale in the US. After several uses this razor became uncomfortable to use. I found a bottle of oil in a kit from another razor and was able to lubricate this unit and make it much more comfortable to shave with. I don't know what's going on with the seller. Good luck with whatever you get!

title: Not Very Good At All
text: I tried six applications of this using quite a bit of the small tube that was provided. I wasn't even doing a full beard just my goatee which is almost entirely grey/silver. I have left it in 5 first  two times and then for 10 minutes thereafter sitting in the shower. As you can see in the photos there was next to no change in my beard. I could use a half dozen tubes of this before I saw any real color change. Not something worth trying.

title: More Decorative Than Useful
text: It's sharp, I'll give it that. About 95% of the edge is, well, razor sharp. A section by the handle was missed by one or more passes of their sharpening process and about an 1/8th of an inch isn't sharp. I tried this on my arm and just couldn't get a comfortable feel enough to shave with. I'm not sure I'd trust using this on the curves and contours of my face and really not going to try it on my scalp which I keep shaved with an electric razor currently. I've always wanted a straight razor in this style. I think I'll find a place for it with my other collected cutlery.

title: Very Nice Moisturizer
text: I've had dry skin issues for decades. Especially now with the heat on and the air super dry my skin is parched, flaky and dry. This lotion goes on nicely, absorbes quickly and doesn't leave you feeling greasy. I've got a lot of tattoos I'm trying to protect as well. I was very pleased with this product. A little goes a long way.

title: Excellent Smell, Dries The Skin
text: The scent of this soap is amazing. One of the best sandalwood scents I've come across. There's two problems I've come across using it. I really dries out my hands leaving them tight and a little itchy. The other issue is a little esoteric but it's so incredibly slippery I have trouble holding onto it. The other night I spent 15 minutes trying to dig it out of the disposal in the kitchen sink. I ended up needing a fork to extract it. Still. I do love the scent.

title: Hard To Apply Alone
text:
I got the 'unisex' selection of tattoos. I didn't realize (having only been tattooed for nearly 30 years) tattoos were gender specific. Strange. Anyway. . .
The designs are pretty, striking really and a couple, the owl specifically, have inspired me in the planning of my next, real, tattoo. I mostly got these to play around with and maybe help clear the brain block that's kept me out of the chair for months now.
My problem is these come rolled, better than folded but not a lot better. I was able to get the smaller ones to apply but the full sleeves, which I was applying to my legs, just wouldn't go on right. Parts would lift or not apply. The really big ones are a two person job and unfortunately I didn't have anyone around to help. You can with decent lighting see the sticker outline of these a dead giveaway they're temporary tattoos. I didn't care for that model plane shiny decal look. I know they sell softener for models to help decals better conform to whatever you're putting them on. I wonder if that stuff would work with these? I've tried another brand that actually lays into your skin, going on green and darkening over 24 hours. That temp tattoo lasted weeks. You'd be luck to get two days out of these before they start looking patchy and flaking off.
Pretty, not long lasting, difficult to apply alone.

title: Stunning, Very Attractive
text: She's worn the medium size/length lashes. They're noticeable from quite a distance. Even though knowing her I was able to spot the false lashes they seemed realish, she said everyone at work noticed, co-workers and customers alike complimented her on how they looked. She was very happy with the product.

title: I Like These Clippers
text: These have some serious weight to them giving me to believe there's a better than average motor in there. The pirate skull is a big plus. I like skulls, have several tattooed on me. One thing I really liked about this set is there's a one inch (1") guide in the set. Almost no clipper sets these days. Most have at best 3/4s of an inch and when I trim my goatee I like it longer than most clippers give me the option of. These are probably my favorite clippers over the last ten years or so and I've tried quite a few sets.

title: My Back's Clean!
text: I'm a big guy and some back scrubbers are too short for me to comfortably use. This was long enough for me to use without an issue. The material holds soap nicely and lathers my back and legs very well. It rinses out okay though it takes a little to get it completely soap free. I'll save you the horror of pictures of me using it. :)

title: Lasts Incredibly Long, Image Lacks Quality
text: This went on easy except for peeling the edge piece off once the main body was stuck down. That took some fumbling about to get off but I was finally able to do it. The ink goes on greenish and as the instructions say turns black after approximately twenty four hours. The temporary tattoo looks real. There's no shine to the ink. It's very matte like real (of which I have an extensive collection) tattoo ink appears. Unfortunately the tattoo looks like it was done in somebody's basement by a guy that bought supplies from the back of a tattoo magazine. It's not very high quality as tattoos go. Not horrible but I've seen many that look so much better. I like the pine design  just wish it were drawn better. . . I also kinda wish it would wash off already. It's been on a week and it looks like it just turned black. The last picture was after several showers and numerous scrubbings.

title: My New Favorite Shower Pouf
text:
What I honestly like about this shower pouf is the way it fits my hand. So many poufs these days are huge and while that can feel indulgent and luxurious I have spinal nerve damage that causes weakness and severe numbness in my hands. Holding onto giant shower poufs can be difficult and it's annoying to have to retrieve them from all corners of these shower.
That's not to say these poufs aren't luxuriant, they're among the softest I've tried over the years. They feel good on my skin. Lather up nicely. As almost universally the case, the cord to hang them from is rather too short but I can make due. 50% longer isn't a lot to ask and it would make a world of difference to me. Still, I would recommend these without reservations.

title: Too Short
text:
I didn't like this, a smaller, more lithe person may have better luck. I found the back scrubber to be too short. I'm a big guy and my flexibility is poor it was uncomfortable to try and use this.
The material is soft and doesn't hurt the skin. The item is two sided. One side is made up of short densely packed bristles that are about 1/4-1/2 inches (6-12m m) long. These hold soap okay, not great but if you can use the scrubber then it can get your back, butt and backs of your legs clean. The other side of the scrubber is covered in staggered rows of rounded bumps that are very short. I guess these could provide a mild massage of sorts. Being smooth this side has no chance of holding any soap.
Each end of the back scrubber has a sturdy, comfortable and easy to grip handle. They're made in a way to facilitate a strong grip even with soapy hands. The colors are mellow and not garish. The blue sort of matches my bathroom and the purple is nice.
Not great for extra large people.

title: Good For Cracked Feet
text:
I had a BAD crack in the sole of my foot. Walking was excruciating. I tried using a good lotion but my podiatrist said the only thing that would really work was 40% urea cream. I request this and started using it two times a day and within a week I was walking fine and my foot felt as good as new. I still have more than half of the jar left so if this happens again, and knowing my feet it likely will, I'll be prepared.
This does dry to a white powder that doesn't stain but does mark up the sheets and the carpet next to my bed. It washed out of the sheets and easily vacuumed up from the carpet.

title: Somewhat Hard to Use
text: I struggled with this trimmer some. You can cut a straight line but the way the head pivots one side is really only good on long down strokes and the other side I found awkward to trim under my chin evenly when edging up my goatee. They do trim well but eat batteries rather quickly. I put a brand new battery in the unit, used it three times and just as I put it down the trimmer started running slower like the battery was going. I would have much preferred a rechargeable unit but this works so I'll use it to edge my beard for now.

title: Fairly Decent Clippers
text: These clippers aren't bad. They have a nice heft which makes them feel premium. They cut well and close without binding or grabbing. The only thing I didn't like was the combs are double ended. That makes them harder to get on the clippers. I also disliked the lack of a carry bag to keep the kit together or take it along when you travel. They do their job and hold a charge for quite a while.

title: Okay. . . Nothing More
text: The scent is nice, in the shower. Once out of the shower you can barely detect it ten minutes later. It lathers well and gets you clean but most soaps these days do. All four bottles leaked a little, one a little more than the others but all had some soap coming from under the caps. I don't know if it was bad handling or the heat here in Florida and in the shipping vehicles. Cleaning them was rather easy as, well, it was soap. . .

title: Amazing Razor
text:
I love this razor. Nothing has given me a shave, especially on my head, as close as this Braun Series 9. I was using a three-head rotary razor from another major brand and had thought that was as good as it gets, then this came along and wow. This is as close to a barber's cut as I've ever gotten at home with an electric razor. It feels great in the hand, maneuvers well even over my lumpy scalp. The head is a nice size that covers your face (and skull) quickly and efficiently. Battery life seems great. It's never gone down a bar during use but I haven't travelled with it and I store it on the charging stand. There's a nice carry case but it doesn't have room for the wall plug & cable and the charging stand so a good battery life is a must if you want to travel with this or you'll need means to carry the charging system. The head can be 'locked' into position to shave hard to get at areas, it doesn't lock so much as provide detents to hold the head lightly in place but it can be pressed and moved when 'locked'
So, all that praise why not five-stars? First unlike my rotary razor this doesn't collect and hold the stubble. When I go over the top of my head no matter what angle I try to keep it at the stubble rains out. A couple times I've gotten it in my eyes. It's an annoyance, not major but just annoying nonetheless. Second, there's no protective cap for the razor's head. I've never owned a razor before that didn't come with some type of cover to protect the foils. And finally, third, as with most electric razor the trimmer is next to useless. It's low on the back of the handle, you press a release and slide it up but not really past the top of the razor's head so it's more or less impossible to use.
So, three reasons a great razor just doesn't deserve five stars even though it gives an amazing shave.

title: Wait, What?
text:
Tropical Splash! It smells like coconut oil. You know what smells like coconut oil? Suntan lotion. Although the scent is mild, very mild, it still makes me think I've grabbed the wrong product and I'm about to wash up with a suntan product.
It didn't leave my skin dry but it didn't leave it feeling loaded down with moisture. On the label it says 2in1 and I have no idea what. It doesn't mention being two of anything, doing two different anythings. It just says 2in1 for some reason.
There's only 6.76oz (200ml) in this can and no idea how much will be left when the propellent runs out. That's half of my average bottle of body wash and at the time of this review many times the price.
It's vegan, don't eat it, I guess that means it contains no animal products?
The cap is annoying. Almost every bodywash I use the lid is attached to the top, you don't have to chase it, a small, clear piece of plastic, all around the shower floor when you eventually drop it.
Product does make a lot of foam when dispensed but that breaks down into the body scrubber to be a lot less than it looked like, expect to need to reload.
I really didn't care for this.

title: Great Scent, Not For Dry Skin
text: I really like the scent. I wish it lasted longer but most soaps don't. It leaves my skin feeling smooth, it does exfoliate quite gently but the problem I run into is I have dry skin and this just doesn't offer enough moisturizing. If you have regular to oily skin and want a bodywash designed for men then you should definitely check out this product.

title: Did Nothing, Useless, Stinks
text:
First and foremost after their maximum seven (7) minutes the test patch I tried on the side of my head had the same hair it had seven minutes prior. This did nothing. Well, not nothing, it was a mild irritant and stunk to high heaven. I've smelled something chemically similar in the past but I can't recall what. It smells revolting. Whomever coined the 'light fresh scent' statement on the tube had one evil sense of humor.
I'm not sure that had it worked I'd have wanted to use the product. I tested a bit bigger area on the side of my head and even after washing it off three or four times and using a spritz of cologne I could still smell it! I can't imagine the stench had I covered my scalp with this stuff. Shaving with my electric razor is much preferable.
The irritation was a mild burning sensation and a bit of redness that lasted a few hours. Nothing dramatic but just another reason NOT to use this.
Not recommended.

title: Confusing
text: I get a lot of blackheads around my nose and on my forehead. Nothing gets rid of them and they just keep coming back. Thought this would be a game changer but it's complicated, messy and confusing to use. For all the effort it's just not worth it. Yeah, I'm a guy but I'd like to have nice skin too just not at the effort and time this device takes. Just storing it is a pain since no case is provided.

title: Excellent Scent
text: My mom loves this scent and wears it all the time. It's become her new favorite perfume. Scent lasts quite a while and is never overpowering while tapering off nicely. Very pleasant and light.

title: Never Run Out of Soap Again!
text: We have home health aids, support, physical and occupational therapies as well as the occasional visiting nurse in and out of the house. All these people use sanitizer but most want a chance to wash their hands. This means we go through quite a lot of liquid soap. These large refill bottles are great for ensuring we never run out. The scent is nice and the soap doesn't dry the skin badly. A good find.

title: Not Up to the Hype
text: Hard to use, easy to rip. Scent was okay but nothing special. As for the claims my confidence wasn't empowered, nor was my self-esteem boosted and my inner peace was in no way promoted.  Skin felt little to no different afterwards. Truly unimpressed.

title: Nice Disposable Razors
text: For a disposable razor these have quite a few features found in regular razors. These are comfortable and give quite a few shaves per razor before you need to switch to a new one. The comfort means they're even good for use on the scalp which I've found rough to shave. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend these.

title: Nice Scent, Tends to Clump
text: This has a nice, manly scent and lasts quite a while my only problem is, being a big guy I sweat a lot and powder tends to clump and cause some mild irritation. I've found this works good as a carpet deodorizer. I sprinkle a little around a short time before I vacuum and the room smells nice for a few days. They don't make a lot of manly scent products for cleaning. This improvises nicely.

title: Works Really Well
text: The only thing I'm not crazy about is the size of the bottle. With the short nozzle and tall ungainly bottle it's easy to tip over when dispensing. Scent is a little strong for men but nice for women. Moisturizing and absorbency are as good as any brand name product. I've even use this for healing a tattoo.

title: My New Favorite Scent
text: I truly like the citrus notes in this eau de toilette. It's very light and breezy. My only disappointment is the scent seems to dissipate somewhat quickly. More so than several others I own. Other than that I really like wearing this scent and my friends agree it suits me well.

title: Clearer Skin
text: Sometimes they'd stick, sometimes they'd STICK, the latter times they're a bit painful to remove. They do a good job either way at removing blackheads. The cleanser left my skin smooth but a little dry. A good product.

title: Volume? Turn it Up. . .
text: My mother whom I care for has thinning hair at age 87. She likes shampoos that improve volume. This, failed utterly. her hair was flat, lifeless and greasy appearing after just a single day. Smelled good, worked worse than generic store brands.

title: An Old Friend
text: Years ago I loved Drakkar, it was, unfortunately, the scent was wildly popular. These days it's more affordable and less known. I've begun wearing scent whenever I go out. It makes me feel better about myself. When I found this 6.7oz bottle at a great price I couldn't resist going back to an old friend instead of trying something new. Very happy with this purchase.

title: Good Razor for the Scalp
text: I gave up on hair a few years ago after a really bad accident left me unable to care for any length of hair. So I went bald. But because that takes visits to the barber because blade shaving was also beyond me got expensive. I came across this razor and because it's a wet or dry shaver I gave this a shot at knocking down several days of stubble both on my scalp and cheeks. I was very surprised at how well this worked on my scalp. My cheeks were also closely shaved with only a pass or two. Complaints are the position of the power button right in the middle of the handle where, when trying to say, reach the back of your head, you hit over and over. There's also a sensitive skin button that slows the rotation of the blades, I hit that several times as well. Clean up under the faucet was okay if a little tedious. Quite happy with this shaver.

title: A Little Slow
text: Had a couple bottles of gel polish around that was sent in gifts and unused due to not having a UV light to set the polish. This light came along and we broke out the polish. Tried a couple times to paint her nails and even after an extra dose of light her nails were still wet. It took two 60 second runs and a 30 second to get just about set. Light output is not spectacular but will, eventually, get the job done.

title: Smells Incredible
text: I love this scent. My mom loves this scent. The cashier at the grocery store commented on how she liked it. It's. . . manly, without being overpowering. It's got Earthy tones with some sweetness. For an eau de toilette the fragrance lasts a long time. Will last the whole day. Very pleased with this selection. I rarely give five stars but this deserves them.

title: Less Than Stellar Results
text: My mom used about half to three quarters of the bottle following the instructions. While it did seem to produce a stronger nail she also complained about a drastic increase in deep hang nails down into the quick. Painful, hard to resolve, often bloody messes that took time to heal. She stopped using the product and while she still has the occasional issue it's not like when she used this every day. Didn't do enough good to outweigh the discomfort.

title: Messy Sun Protection
text: While this went on easy enough and you can get a small amount to go a long way one of the things I honestly disliked was how thin this product was. Even after shaking to make sure it was fully mixed you had to make sure you opened the package with the cap facing up otherwise you end up with a dribbly mess with product going where you don't want or need it, making a mess of cap and clothes. Does do a good job protecting skin from the sun. I use this exclusively protect recent forearm tattoos from the Florida sun.

title: Dye to Die For
text: Not too hard to apply. Thick enough that it didn't run too much so not a lot of clean up in unexpected places. Color of course goes on light or bleached hair much better but you can get some stunning effects putting dark dyes onto dark hair. Lasted well. All in all a fun dye with really nice color.

title: Good Shampoo
text: This Head & Shoulders for men has an interesting and distinct scent and works well against flakes leaving hair clean and conditioned. Not a lot more to be said. . . do avoid getting it in your eyes as it can sting painfully. Otherwise it's a good shampoo if you have dandruff.

title: Very Nice Scrunchies
text: These forty (40) velvet scrunchies are pretty, durable and have a nice shine to the cloth. They're attractive and hold even fairly short ponytails securely. There's a very nice variety of colors in the forty pack which will go with most outfits and seem like they'll last a long time.

title: I Love This Stuff
text: I'm a guy and I've been down using this for a few weeks in place of my oatmeal body wash and I've got to say this is nearly as good at moisturizing and superior in scent. I've tried numerous body washes for my dry skin and I really enjoyed this product. My skin feels great throughout the day and the scent which for most washes disappears in minutes can linger for hours. It's a nice clean scent. Soap less content gets you clean and was gentle enough to use on fresh tattoos.

title: Hit or Miss Temporary Tattoos
text: The designs I received were interesting and well done. Had some issues getting them to adhere to skin. My arms have light hair, even my tattoo artist doesn't bother to shave before he works on me but these stood up on some of my hair and ruined the design. My mother has rather papery and wrinkled skin and it was next to impossible to get anything to stay on her. These are great when they work, not so much when they fail. I think I'll stick with the real thing.

title: Convenient Pump Bottle
text: We're split on how we feel about this product but as I'm the one writing the review it gets four stars. My mom who also tried this wasn't quite as happy with it as me. She likes a wash with a stronger scent while I really liked the subtle watermelon scent (it didn't draw one bee unlike my strawberry shampoo did years ago). She prefers a wash that has a thick, heavy lather while I liked how the lighter than typical lather rinsed off quickly and completely. The pump bottle is very convenient for use in the shower. Different, interesting. I enjoyed using this.

title: Not Very Good
text: My mom, whom I live with and care for, has, at age 87, developed thinning hair and searches for volumizing  products to help her look as nice as possible. This shampoo left her hair stringy and lifeless with a greasy look the same day she washed her hair. Getting a pleasing lather took quite a bit of product and effort. It did rinse easily but did nothing for her hair. We've had store brand products give better results.

title: A Little Goes a Long Way
text: I've recently started collecting more tattoos. The majority of my recent ones are on my forearms and this 60spf sunscreen is great at protecting my expensive investment in skin art from fading and damage. I won't leave to go anywhere where I'll be out for more than an hour or so without applying a sunscreen to my ink. It goes on easily spreads well and absorbs very quickly leaving behind only the slightest residue. Very little is needed to cover each forearm.

title: Slightly Rough on the Skin
text: I hate blade shaving. Almost every time I get skin irritation especially in the Florida heat and humidity. So, for years now I have relied on clippers to get a mild, I shaved yesterday look. I have gone through numerous sets of clippers from full size hair clippers which, since I also keep a goatee, are a little large to quite a few smaller models like this Wahl set. This is up near the top. Not quite the best only because they are a little rough on my skin. They are powerful and will mow through 3/4s of an inch of beard without even slowing down. There are a nice collection of attachments to manage hair length including some rarely seen scruffy look combs. The travel bag is too small. You can't fit everything in in. In fact if you want to take the clippers and the nose hair trimmer, a decent quality addition, along you'll end up leaving most of the other accessories behind. It's too bad as this would be a great travel set. All in all though it's a solid workhorse and seems like it will last for years.

title: Gets You Clean, Doesn't Dry Skin
text: This wash lathers well and gets you clean without drying your skin. It doesn't hydrate much but it doesn't dry. I've got fairly dry skin and always look for the best moisturizing body washes I can find. This Dove Men+ is good, not great. My skin didn't feel dry and tight but it wasn't smooth and supple like other washes have. The scent is nice but like most products it doesn't last much longer than the shower.

title: Just About as Good as Name Brand
text: These are good swabs. There's a decent sized bud that holds it shape fairly well and stays on the stick. The stick is sturdy, bends just enough and the typical length for cotton swabs. From crafts to make-up and even useful as a makeshift paintbrush. These are less costly than the name brand swabs and just about as good in all situations.

title: Just About as Good as Name Brand
text: These cotton swabs are pretty good. The stick is durable and can hold up to decent pressure. The cotton bud holds together almost, though not quite, as well as the name brand cotton swabs. They clean well. Have a decent amount of padding at each end. I've used them in crafting, cleaning my 3D printer, in a pinch I've painted with one and even cleaned my ears out with them. I really can't tell the difference between these and the much more expensive name brand ones.

title: Horrible!
text: I like most colognes. I'm always open to new and different scents. . . until I tried this. Expecting something nice I was foolishly liberal with my first application. I was in the shower five minutes later. The first scent that came to mind was celery which, while not a terrible smell, is not a scent I want to wear. I sat for a few minutes to give it a chance and then I picked up the distinct odor of rancid watermelon (I unfortunately know all too well what that smells like). It wasn't strong but it was there. I asked my mother whst she thought. She both checked out how I smelled and tried it on herself. While she didn't rush to wash it off like I did she said she didn't care for it and wouldn't wear it. My neighbor was over for a visit, it gave her a headache and she disliked the scent. Definitely something I hope I never smell again.

title: Mediocre Body Wash
text: Smells really nice and the scent lasts pretty good after a shower. Gets you clean and lathers nicely but left both of our skins feeling dry and tight. Expected better from the label. If you've got dry skin and need real moisture in your body wash look elsewhere.

title: Okay, Not Great
text: I expected better moisturizing. While it didn't leave my skin tight and taunt feeling it wasn't what I had hoped for. It lathered up okay but again, nothing impressive and the soap itself isn't appealing, a slimy white cream that just is not visually appealing. The scent wasn't bad. It's a basic soap that while it doesn't, at least for me, give a lot of moisture to the skin it won't dry your skin completely out.

title: Impressive Shave
text:
I don't often give five stars on reviews but this razor deserves it. I used it with soothing aloe Barbasol shave cream while shaving in the shower. I have, in the past, not 'shaved' unless I was at the barbershop and relied on clippers for a slightly scruffy look. My first try of this razor was on way more than stubble, closer to two weeks growth (it does come in fairly slow) and I had to check to see if there were blades in the head. It was SO smooth I couldn't believe it was shaving. No pull, no tug anywhere, not on my neck not even up close edging my goatee. It also rinsed clear unbelievably easy. Multi blade razors always clogged up on me, especially when I let some time go between shaves. I used to keep an old toothbrush around to clear out stubborn bristles. This razor? A quick flick under the shower stream and it was clear and ready to go. The lubrication strip really helps this slide along and I had far less razor burn out in the chilly breeze than I've ever had before. My barber uses a straight razor and this shaves nearly as close.
Best razor, ever.

title: Gets You Clean, But. . .
text: The body wash lathers up nicely, doesn't take a large amount of the product for a shower. It rinses clean and doesn't seem to leave a residue. The label says it contains moisturizers (it might be one of the number of unpronounceable chemicals on the ingredients list). And while my skin wasn't dry and taut it like some soaps leave it I did feel a little. . . tacky. Almost dry but slightly moisturized. The scent is nice, unisex with a bit more of a masculine edge. Not the best body wash and some of the ingredients disturb me but I've used far worse.

title: Pretty Good Body Wash
text: It's really thick and takes just a small amount, less than just about any body wash I've tried, to make tons of lather. The large bottle will go a long way! It lathers nice and gets you clean. It claims to be an  ultra-hydrated wash and while it doesn't leave your skin feeling dry and tight it's okay at making you feel moisturized. It does rinse clean leaving no residue or tacky feeling. The scent is masculine enough but I don't notice it five minutes after I get out of the shower.  I really can't say how well or not it works on hair, unless you want to count my beard (normally I go bald or nearly bald) which it does a good job on. An all around good body wash.

title: Good For The Lips
text: Like most Chapstick products this is good for your lips unfortunately the tint is a bit ugly on the lips. The tint's a rather dark brown on the lips and a couple times I thought something medical was wrong with my mother who has fairly pale skin. She likes how it feels but doesn't like how it looks.

title: Kinda Cheap
text: The plastic feels thing and fragile. It's hard for me to turn the knob to open or access the batteries which makes it nigh on impossible for my 87 year old mother to operate. the design is poor, one knob on the bottom, turn it  one way the trimmer wand extends, or retracts, turn it the other way and it ejects the battery compartment. My mom was constantly getting it backwards and getting a handful of batteries. As a trimmer it's sub par, it took the hair off my arm requiring three passes to clear one small swatch. On my beard it struggled to cut the thicker, stiffer hair. After each of us tried it several times and were disappointed we pitched it in the trash.

title: Just Okay, Really
text: The shampoo gives a someone less than expected lather though it does clean the hair well it doesn't look or feel like it is. The scent is like the lather, a little less than expected for the premium look and claims. The pump handle is useful if you have the proper place to put it. One of our showers lacks a decent shelf so bottles have to sit on the ledge next to the doors. This puts the bottles a few inches above your feet and it's somewhat awkward to use a pump in that position and it's not easy to use holding it in one hand. Still, it's an okay product.

title: Fun Temporary Pop of Color
text: This was fun. My mom has silver white hair and this went on insanely bright and vivid. A little goes a long way. I would use half, maybe less, the recommended amount to comb/brush into the hair at the start to get a feel for it as even a small amount colors a lot of hair, especially when it's vivid white hair. It washed out with two applications of shampoo and some vigorous scrubbing. After being applied it didn't appear to smudge off on clothing or bedding which was nice.

title: Very Nice Lotion
text: Does an amazing job moisturizing and nourishing dry skin. Scent is more for women but acceptable for men. Goes on easy and absorbs quickly leaving skin feeling moist and not greasy. A little goes a long way.

title: Needs Some Changes
text:
With a few changes this could easily be a four or five star item but it has some flaws that, in my opinion, drag it down.
* The Hinge is weak on 10x mirror. Mirror will not maintain position.
* Power switch does not lock out when closed. Very easy to hit, even in bag, and turn on unaware.
* One button for everything. One light, two lights, on/off, dimmer.
If they fixed those problems this would be a far better product. The mirrors are clear and I didn't notice any defects. The lights are bright but can be dimmed down nicely. Works well in many situations even as a room/flash light.

title: Pretty Color
text: This review is specific to the Paris & Vine Classics Collection Color: 091 Limitless, Bright Blue Crème. The bottle is squat and modern looking. The polish goes on smooth and clean. One coat was enough. Durability was good with minimal chipping after a week and still fair coverage after ten days. A very nice polish in a different color that's striking and eye catching.

title: Good Antiperspirant Okay Scent
text: I tried both the Alpha and the Stunner varieties of the Right Guard Best Dressed antiperspirants. The Stunner has a stronger more potent scent that I wasn't crazy about. I could wear it but if I had the choice I'd wear the Alpha which has a less potent scent. Oddly neither scent stays strong after being applied though as much as twelve hours later I could catch a ghost of both scents. The antiperspirant feature works quite well. Hours after applying the product I started working around the house and worked up quite a sweat. My armpits stayed pretty dry.

title: Exceptional Perfume
text: I love sandalwood. I buy sandalwood stick incense by the case I use so much of it. This perfume smells as good if not better than the Japanese incense I buy. It's potent but not over the top. Woodsy but not overly dark. Sweet but not cloying. Practically the perfect woman's perfume. It lasts quite a long time but doesn't go on super strong and finishes lightly. The container is even very attractive and you get a lot in the 3.4 ounce (Why? Why not 3 or 3.5?) package. Pricy but worth it.

title: Low Quality Trimmer
text: My first impression on opening the package was "This can't be a Braun." my second was "Wow, that's cheap!" Lightweight & very thin plastic. I'm disabled with nerve damage that has caused serious issues with my hands; I found the adjustment dial to be quite hard to turn due to it being so low and nearly flush with the body of the trimmer. The comb has trouble staying on the clippers when you change lengths rapidly or move from short to long and back. It binds and comes part or all the way off. It's easy enough to put back on but still annoying. There's no visual charge level and only a single light on the charging plug to tell it's operating. The power switch is also hard to operate but does lock positively on and off. As clippers, with the comb on, they work okay. I trimmed my goatee to a good length with the longest setting. I'd like longer but that's rarely offered. My biggest problem arises when the comb is removed. I like the slightly scruffy, clippered look and hate razor burn on my cheeks so I've used clippers in lieu of shaving for decades the back of the blades which is supposed to glide across your skin is made of ribbed plastic which caught and stuck on my face and was very actually painful to use. I can't believe a company like Braun would put out a product as cheap and badly designed as this.

title: A Good Scent For Most Men
text:
I like the scent, I can't say I love the scent, there's some woody notes, a bit of sweet muskiness and just a tad too much vanilla. The product, being a toilette instead of a parfum doesn't last a long time but five or six hours after applying just a few spritzes (it's a spray bottle) I could still catch a whiff of it. Scent is not overpowering on first application like some, although I'm sure you could over apply. Application I found to be a bit awkward. The bottle at 6.7oz. is huge and made from heavy glass but the spray head is small with a very short travel. I had to use two hands.
On an aside, my bottle came with a silly black wristband with the brand and maker's names on it. It was so cheap it snapped before I could get it over my knuckles. The box it comes in isn't much of a presentation piece.

title: Terrible Shampoo
text: Probably one of the worst shampoos ever. The DAY it's used the hair is limp, lifeless and looking stringy and greasy. Care was made to completely rinse the product out but after multiple uses this product does a horrible job on the hair. The scent wasn't all that great either. Very unimpressed with this product.

title: Okay Body Wash
text: I wish we could do half stars here on Amazon. I'd be a lot more comfortable giving this body wash three and a half but I'd rather round up than down so four stars it gets. It's nice soap, gets you clean, smells good for a short amount of time and doesn't dry your skin out badly. My biggest disappointment is the scent does not last long at all. Without a strong scent it's just about any other body wash on the shelf.

title: Good, Not Great
text: A nice neutral color that lasts the entire day. Very good when you don't want to stand out but want to add a little understated color to your look. One downside was even though it claims to be intensely hydrating it made the lips feel very dry. Not much else you can say, physically it worked like every other lipstick forever. Packaged in a boring cardboard box. Sleek black case/applicator. Good but not great.

title: A Nice Body Wash
text: Not bad. Fully twenty-four hour after taking a shower and my skin still feel soft and smooth. The scent is a little too flowery and feminine for a guy but it's not too bad. I could live with it and I wouldn't be embarrassed to use it. It suits my mother better but both of us can use it and we both enjoy the way it makes our skin feel.

title: Great Scent, Ugly Candle
text: The scent is just shy of intoxicating. Light & floral but not overly sweet or feminine. I had never smelled or even knew tobacco flowers had a scent much less a very nice one. The reason for the three stars? Soot. We trim the wick to the instructed height. We never burn it longer, and often 3/4's the burn time mentioned in the instructions an still the entire top of the candle has an ugly black sooty coating on it. While the candle is no display piece, to be honest it looks like a water glass you'd have in the bathroom the layer of soot makes me want to find some place to hide it so company won't see it. Honestly, I don't even like looking at it.

title: Smooths & Softens Skin
text: Only a one ounce tube which is rather small the but a little of the product does go quite a long way. The scent is rather potent but it does even better than Lubriderm, which I've used for years, at smoothing and softening skin. I like this but I don't think I'd pay the price unless it comes down. Besides, as a guy the lavender scent is a little too feminine for me. A good but pricy product.

title: A Very Nice Polish
text: On a somewhat pale white person this isn't going to be a 'color' so much as adding a sheen to the nail. filling in rough spots and covering any scars or low spots. The polish goes on very easily and only needs a single coat for perfect easy coverage. It makes the nails looks very lovely and bright. It's subdued but very pretty. Even without a sealer or top coat the polish is quite durable and resistant to chipping and scratching.

title: Very Nice Mirror, Unreliable Hook
text:
The protective covering was a royal pain to get off without scratching the mirror but once I got it started it came off fairly easily. The mirror itself is incredibly clear and reflective. I couldn't see any reason to spend six or seven dollars more for a picture of water drops on a colored background so I bought the plain 'unclad' background which is plain grey and fine by me. The five feet of para-cord is more than enough to hang the mirror from the shower head although it doesn't hang flat against the wall but I plan on holding the mirror while I shave with clippers not a razor.
My one real complaint is the Command strip copy they included that had no protective covering on the sticky part. It wouldn't even hold it's own weight for more than a minute before falling off the tile. Luckily I was able to use the shower head extension coming from the wall to hang the mirror. A little sad the hook was completely useless but glad I was able to work around the problem.

title: Very Nice Waterproof Trimmers
text:
This is the second Remington trimmer I've tested this week and by far the superior of the two. The blade tips making these far more comfortable than anything but the professional trimmers my barber uses and I have no idea how much money they cost him. These trimmers are fully waterproof and can through an ingenious cutout easily be cleaned under running water, even in the shower. They're supposed to trim as close as 0.2mm which is nearly blade close without the burn razor shaving especially here in the heat and humidity of Florida. I have a shatter-proof mirror on order so I can trim my face in the shower and if I can work up the nerve I really want to try doing my scalp with them. While I prefer a professional straight razor shave of my scalp my hair grows in fast and either I look fuzzy like someone recently out of boot camp or I'm spending a fortune to keep myself truly bald. I've also been too chicken to try any depilatories and can't find any made for the scalp anyhow. Will update if I get brave enough to try my scalp with these trimmers.
Some of the best I've used and with a full sixty minutes per charge you'll likely never run out of power.
Sadly, once again Remington has included three beard/moustache combs that are all (especially if, like me, your skin is fine and your goatee is silver) much too short. But since they didn't bother to include a blade protector I kept the longest comb to keep the blades from getting damaged.
There's also no charging cradle included just a rather poorly fitting power adapter and plug that just doesn't seem to seat right. But it charges so that's what counts. I'm quite happy with these trimmers so far.

title: Mediocre Scent, Doesn't Last, Not Impressed
text: Where's the scent? I took a shower and had a great lather built up. Got out, dried off and you could barely smell the product on your skin. Gets you clean and doesn't leave your skin feeling  all that dry and tight. Definitely not an 'armor of man scent' you need a bloodhound to detect it. I've got it so I'll use it but i won't be buying it again.

title: Okay Quality Clippers, Not Great
text:
I have always used a set of clippers instead of a razor. With good clippers you get a reasonably close shave and far less razor burn. I found these clippers to be rather harsh, almost painful against my face. It hurt plain and simple. The unit comes with several auxiliary attachments. I found putting them on and taking them off somewhat difficult. The body hair and fine edge attachments I found to be next to useless. The only attachment I found useful was the included nose hair trimmer. The combs included for the the trimmer head are the typical super short, way too short and who really wants their beard this short? Lengths. I've kept the longest comb because Remington didn't bother to include a protective cover for the blades. I still won't use it on my beard which I wear longer than most devices come with.
The clippers do give a close trim but even properly oiling the blade it was still fairly harsh on my skin. I did like and will continue to use the nose hair attachment as long as I can get it on and off. . . I may just leave it on and have an expensive nose hair trimmer. I honestly wasn't that impressed with this set.

title: Really Softens Your Skin
text: Incredibly heady scent oif vanilla both in the bottle and the amazing amounts of lather this make either using just your hands or a nylon lather builder. It made my skin feel quite a bit softer than my regular moisturizing soap but the sent though okay is far more feminine than masculine. Going on day two and my skin still feels soft and silky. They need to make a man's version of this body wash. I'd buy it in a heartbeat.

title: I'm Unimpressed
text:
Had to wait to write the review because the first one appeared defective. I was told this would work fine for the whole body but my first unit would just stop and need to be switched to a slower speed to continue to work. I think if it spun instead of just vibrating it would clean better. It barely brings up any lather where a nylon shower scrubber with the same amount of soap generated five times the lather. And what's with the silly beeping telling you it's time to move to a different part of your face? Who decided how long each area of my face is dirty for? I can tell when my face is clean on my own thank you very much.
I must admit warranty replacement was quick and painless although I received a pearlescent white unit to replace my original floral designed one. It definitely holds a charge better but I just wasn't impressed with the unit. One of the things I found truly outrageous is even through the device has a three year warranty after the first year you're expected to send $15 to cover postage and handling during the second and third years of warranty coverage.
Yes, my face feels clean but to be truly honest I feel no cleaner than if I'd used a two dollar nylon lather builder. I'm just not impressed by this device. Kudos to the company for the speedy and painless warranty replacement although if I were in year two or three I'd seriously have thought twice about paying to cover shipping and handling on an item under warranty.

title: Same Old Q-Tips, different Packaging
text: Packaging was far different than shown. Very much used to the plastic case with the bottom you pop open and closed. Received four cardboard boxes with 'drawers' that open in either direction. Not a deal breaker. Just something I've never seen before. Inside are the same old Q-Tips. Extra soft cotton ends far thicker than the generics attached to very stiff cardboard rolled shafts. 2,000 will last me probably a few years but the price at the time couldn't be beat for a name brand product. Couldn't pass up the deal.

title: Poorly Designed Packaging Ruins Decent Product
text:
Lathers well, rinces away quite well. It does make fine, thin hair appear somewhat thicker and more luxurious. Not quite scented for a guy, it's much more feminine than masculine but in a pinch it will do for anyone's hair.
The reason for three stars? I'm not forgiving like some other reviewers. The container this comes in is horrible. It's incredibly soft and. . .squishy. Trying to get a solid grip on this with lathery hands and you can end up with shampoo everywhere, all over the floor making a slippery, dangerous mess or on the walls or shower doors leading to a good long clean up. The first time this got used a third of the container was lost. And the cap, ugh, you have to get it just right. Press a little forward and strongly down or it just won't close. It's a royal pain to close.
Good shampoo, deplorable contain design. As good as it works we still won't be regular users just because of the packaging.

title: Not A Product I'd Recommend
text: It goes on silky smooth then after a few moments it get somewhat tacky and within a quarter of an hour you can't even tell you put anything on your lips. You get a lot more than Chapstick .49oz in the Vichy VS. .15oz in the Cherry Chapstick but still,  nine bucks a tube and the product feels like it's worn off in less than half an hour. Sure it feels great going on but it doesn't last and doesn't feel all that great after a while. Honestly you get basically the same amount for about the same cost (do the math) but the Chapstick has a better long term feel and lasts longer. This is great for all of five or ten minutes then. . . nothing. We'll be sticking with the old standby Chapstick it, by far does a better job and lasts longer.

The scent is very masculine, woodsy with a touch of musk. I'd be interested to find out if they made a similar air freshener spray. I had no skin reaction from the application of the product it did a fair job of blocking perspiration (and I can sweat quite heavily) and the scent lasts hours. I'm really impressed by this product.

title: The Razor Is Great. The Accesories Are. . Useless.
text:
Four stars for the three head razor. The rest, the brushes, etc., two to three stars at best they just don't seem to have any real function or to be useful in any way. The razor itself does a pretty good job shaving. The pop-out trimmer built into the body is awkward to use but can quickly trim a moustache evenly faster than pulling the razor (or brush if you've wasted your time with them) head from the body and snap in the larger trimmer which has an adjustable attachment to change the depth of the cut of the clipper from really short to pretty short. So few trimmers have length settings to allow you to trim a beard reasonably long, this, unfortunately is another one where the trimmer only allows short trimming. The grip looks funky but myself with large but stubby hand and my mother with small and dainty hands had no problem controlling and using the razor at all. Charge time so far appears to be six or so shaves before it starts to act like it needs more power.
So, Remington you've created a great, comfortable razor unfortunately you've thrown handfuls of useless accessories in the box with it.
I just realized, you could use the multiple brushes to clean the chrome of your sink faucets as well as the bowl of the sink and the shower head and controls and maybe even grout! Seriously, the brushes are useless. The trimmer attachment is okay if you don't have a dedicated set of clippers but it just doesn't have enough depth settings to really be useful. The pop-out trimmer is awkward but can do a decent job on trimming a moustache evenly. Great razor, everything else is just junk or nearly so.

title: Decent Trimmer, Unimpressive Case
text:
Okay, it's a complete kit, you get the trimmer handle which comes with the beard cutter mounted on it. A slim trimming head for shaping and getting into small spaces and there's also a 'stubble' head I assume is for that scruffy look. Along with the three cutters comes a somewhat wimpy cleaning brush, a small tube of mineral oil to lubricate the blades with and a length comb that adjusts longer and shorter via a dial you spin on the trimmer body. Everything comes packed in a huge plastic case that has a military finish and feel to it. According to the product description; 'Each piece of the kit stores securely in the durable plastic storage case.' but they really don't. There's non place to lock down or 'secure' any of the parts at all. The inside of the case holds a fitted cardboard box with two sides that you can put the different bits but, again, there's nothing secure about how the parts are stored and I have doubts that the cardboard is going to last long in a damp bathroom environment.
That being said the trimmers, once lubricated, do a great job of giving you a close trim. I hate to blade shave and have used trimmers for decades. Once I ensured the adjustable comb was solidly in place (my first attempt, not so well) the trimmer mows through long beard hair like crazy. Granted my goatee is a bit shorter than I intended I chalk it up to a learning experience. I got things in place and set right and it did a great getting my cheeks smooth and my goatee (albeit a bit shorter than expected) trimmed evenly. It was even quieter than most other trimmers I've used over the years. The case is a bit of a disappointment and the adjustable comb is thin and brittle feeling but it feels good in my hand and does it's job well.

title: Terrible Clipper, Mediocre Shaver
text: Ouch! I have a small trimmer with a similar sized head so I was excited to try out this model which has a longer reach. I don't shave, I go for the close scruff look done with no attachments on the trimmer. The first thing I noticed was this hurt, quite a lot. It didn't get better as I did both cheeks and around my goatee. I couldn't believe how painful this was to use. No other trimmer and I've used many over the decades, has ever been this rough on my face. The three combs that come with the trimmer are too close in size to be very useful or versatile. The foil head that comes with this kit does a mediocre job. After going over my face with the trimmer the foil head seemed to take off next to nothing and left my face looking like a clipper cut.

title: Not For Me
text: I really disliked this shampoo.
