text:
I am not currently a false eyelash wearer, but I would like to learn how to use them properly.

My first impression was intimidation. There was a box full of mostly-unknown items. So, I had to investigate what they were and how to use them. There were no instructions included in the box I received. The only recognizable thing were the disposable mascara wands.

After finding out what all of the things were (but nit necessarily how to use them), I think this kit is best suited for those who like to put on individual eyelashes, rather than a strip of lashes.

There is a bag of little plastic rings which have a tiny "bucket" on them to put on your finger. This is supposed to be for holding eyelash adhesive. It seems to me that you would waste a lot of adhesive if you used these little rings.

There are sets of patches to put under your eye to give a place for the upper lashes to rest while you work on them. In other words, you won't glue your lashes to your face. Ha ha!

The rolls of tape are still a mystery to me, so use it as you wish. There are two tweezers included, each with a different angle, so you can choose what works for you.

There is also a small, hand-held fan to help lash glue dry faster. The package back also suggests you could use it to try nails as well. It does not take batteries, but instead is yet another thing that is USB-chargable. You'll have to charge the fan before your first use.

I don't know - this all seems way too complicated to just stick on false eyelashes! No lashes or adhesive is included...this is strictly a kit to help you not glue lashes to your cheek and to dry them faster. I would not personally opt to buy this one again, although the disposable wands are nice (and you can buy those separately on Amazon).

title: Crumbly cubes
text:
Well, these smell great. Very refreshing.

But...once I opened the box, I had an endless supply of "scented sand" with which to deal. There were several cubes that looked intact, but if you touched them, they crumbled. The box had powder-like material falling out of the box. I quickly closed it and reopened it over a trash can!

So, we never got to use any in the shower...we couldn't get one out of the box they were packed in.
Great idea, but a crumbly mess is what we received.

title: Nice ingredients
text:
This is a box of home hair color.
I chose "7.0 Blond" to try. My hair is currently a mousey brown with a healthy dose of gray mixed in at the front.

This brand has botanical extracts in it, and is supposed to be gentler on your hair. It is ammonia-free, which should be nice for the eyes and nose! It claims 100% gray coverage.

I have not had the chance to use it yet, but when I've actually tried it, I will come back and update my review with before and after photos.

title: Lots and lots and lots of ingredients
text:
You Dew You is a facial cleanser.
My first impression was what a nice design and fonts on the bottle. (I love graphic design.) Then I noticed how heavy this bottle is relative to its size. It is a glass bottle. Definitely not a favorite thing to have on our tiny bathroom counter.

The ingredients list should cause most folks some concern. Water is the first ingredient. It then rolls in to a very long list of chemical ingredients. If you have sensitive skin, I think you should just save yourself upfront and avoid this one. It does have several ingredients you often find in acne medications, such as benzyl salicylate. A few ingredients are to not make this smell like medicine. Some are sudsing agents. There were a few ingredients I've never seen in anything else. So, it is a roll of the dice on this one.
But, nice bottle.

title: A nice medium quality wig
text:
This is supposed to have a frosted look to it.
The hair itself is a decent quality. It doesn't feel like plastic, and lays on my hand like real hair would.

The color is sort of what we used to call "strawberry blonde", and has streaks here and there (but not a lot) of an almost-white blonde color.

Overall, it is a nice medium-quality wig.

title: Very good color, nice hair texture
text:
This is a nice quality wig. The hair feels close to real hair, but to my touch, still has a very faux feel.
The color is deep (I got black) and shiny.

I need to note that I do not use wigs to wear - I use them for crafting purposes. Therefore, I cannot comment on the comfort level of wearing this wig.

title: Cute little storage bag
text:
This was a very cute bag. A little odd, but cute.

I think it is meant to be a makeup bag. I gave this as a gift to a favorite nurse, and filled it with little snack bags of her favorite cookie.

title: Nothing special
text:
This was an interesting product. You apply a dot that has medication on it to a blemish.

My daughter tried them. They make shiny spots on your face, of course, so you wouldn't wear them outside of the house.

She put them on while hanging around the house. She said they did seem to help some, and definitely reduced the redness of the blemish.
But, we both agreed that they were not impressive enough to buy again.

title: Pass. But the color is great
text:
I love the bright color on these. They are easy to find in the bottom of your makeup bag.

But, I found them to be awkwardly ground. I've been using tweezers for 40+ years, but had a hard time catching eyebrow strays without pinching my skin.

Overalk, these are ok and will get out a splinter, but definitely not a top of the line product.

title: Definitely not for thin hair!
text:
Well, I have to say that I was disappointed. I have thin hair, and use bobby pins to create a curl with damp hair, rather than rollers.

The tin is very cute. (My daughter already claimed it.) The bobby pins/hair pins come in plastic bags inside the tin.

The pins themselves are very sturdy and nicely coated. However, I could not get them opened with just one hand, like I need to to put them in my own hair. I had to use two hands to get them open, which means I had to drop the section of hair I was going to pin up. When I tried to get a pin to stay ib my hair, it would not. I have thin hair, but these pins would not stay on any amount of sectioned hair. It wouldn't even hold back a simple side pull up.
It was a no-win situation.

So, while they look well-made, there is something off about these hair pins. I don't know if it is the material that was used in the manufacturing process, or just bad engineering, but they won't work for me. Maybe if you have super thick hair, or someone to help you, you could get them to work. For me, they are just useless, but the tin is nice.

title: Too hard to use unless you have an extra set of hands
text:
These short hair pins come in a cute metal tin. The pins are in plastic bags inside the tin when you first get them.
The tin is cute enough, but the lid does not fit super tightly, so don't trust it for picking it up if it is full.

The pins themselves are ok. The short length can actually be very helpful. BUT...these pins are very thick, and hard to open and use. I had aheck of a time getting them opened, and they would slide right back shut or totally slide apart, making them incredibly hard to actually put in my hair.

If you have a second set of hands who could perhaps put your hair up for you, they might work fine. But for me, they just turned out to be annoying.

title: Nice texture, bright colors
text:
First off, please know I use faux hair, but not for my head - I use them in crafting projects.

These orange strips are really nice for crafts, but I could never see wearing them, except maybe for costume purposes.

The faux hair is very soft to the touch. Don't get it near a heat source or it will melt. The orange color is bright and consistent all the way through.

I definitely like these a lot for my purposes. The price is fair for the item at the time of this review.

title: Not the best, but looks good
text:
This is a set of two nail clippers, one small and one larger.

The odd thing is that the small is actually a regular fingernail clipper size. But the large is NOT toenail clipper size, just a morph of the inbetweens.

They have color inlays, one in blue and one in green. Both clippers are plenty sharp, but not sure how long that will last.

The backs of the tops of both clippers have nail file inserts. Well, supposed to be nail files. That part did not work worth a hoot. I had to get out a regular file to smoothe a rough edge.

Overall, you can't have too many nail clippers. However, there are plenty of better sets out there, and I hope you take a look. These are okay, but just okay, and I would not buy them again.

title: Just not pretty
text:
Well, got to be honest...
I did not like this one.

I did not care for the colors at all. It doesn't look like white fading into gray. What I expected to be white or light blonde is actually an ugly shade of "whatever". If you've ever dealt with someone with white hair that needed a good shampoo and purple color-correcting rinse, the "before" describes the color. Not good.

It doesn't even have a nice feel to it. Very waxy.

I did not like this one at all, and would never recommend it.

title: Definitely green! Fun wig for cosplay or holiday parties
text:
Well, this is a fun wig!
When they say green, they mean green.

This one is a bright, nearly-neon green. The hair itself seems very plastic-y. Sure, it is synthetic, but some wigs are still very soft. This isn't one of those. The hair is a little stiff.

There are a few shades of green that blend in to one wig. If you want to be a female grinch for a holiday party, this is your wig! It is definitely a fun color.

title: Great for thick hair
text:
These have an unusual texture to them. They are much thicker than the ones we usually buy.

If you have super thick hair (lucky you!), these should work very well for you.

title: Very cute but hard to use
text:
These are so cute!!
BUT....

There is a learning curve on actually using these things. They are thin mylar-like strips. Think of the tinsel used on Christmas trees - it is very similar.

There are basic instructions that still don't really tell you how to put these things in. We watched several online videos, but it still never worked the same way for us. I did the knot method to attach them. It finally worked, but made an ugly spot where the knots were, and they were difficult to remove later.

In the photos, we put red, silver and blue strips in my daughter's hair for the 4th of July.

Loved the color selections and the idea behind it, but unless you have a skilled hairdresser at your home, good luck with these! Haha!

title: Not really baby sized, but fine for kids and adults
text:
I actually thought these were going to be much smaller, based on the term "baby" used by the manufacturer.

These are actually just your basic wrapped hair ties. They are smaller than regular hair ties, maybe 1/3 their size. But, adults can certainly use these. (The turquoise item a band is sitting on in one of my photos is a small sticky note for size reference.)

I would say they are geared more towards kids, or for braiding hair, but definitely NOT for babies.
They have a decent stretch and worked just fine.

title: Great looking, pretty heavy in my hand
text:
This is a gorgeous hair clipper.
It makes you feel awesome just to hold it, given the majority of the ones I've had were plain black.

I've been informally cutting hair for over 30 years. My mom was a beautician, so I learned quite a bit from her.

That being said, I only have one negative thing to say about this one is the weight. It is VERY heavy in my hand. I would only be good for one haircut at a time with this one! The vibration is also uncomfortable, but that is my situation, not necessarily yours. The clipper looks awesome and does a nice job on haircuts.

title: Scrubbies are soft, but the colors are ugly
text:
We all use nylon shower scrubbies at our house.
These are softer nylon than the ones we normally buy, so that might be a good thing if you have sensitive skin.

The only thing I did not care for were the colors...not a pretty one among them! All were boring, muted and looked like they had been dipped in leftover water from dying something else. But if color doesn't matter to you, these will work just fine.

title: Smaller but very sturdy
text:
I really like these little sprayers.
They are well made, very easy to fill, and have a textured bottom so they do not slip as much.

We received one purple and one turquoise sprayer. Since the colors are so great, we can easily distinguish them from our other sprayers, making them great for custom uses. We have the purple sprayer specially filled with a water and peppermint oil. We spray around our front door, around the dryer vent and by the windowsills. Why? Most insects hate the smell of peppermint. It is a natural and pet-safe repellant for ants, spiders and mice.

title: Looks better than it works
text:
This set looks nicer in photos than it feels in the hand. The handle is ok, but nothing awesome. The bristles are the part I did not care for. It looks like it would be a natural bristle, but then they are tipped in the little beads, which are massively cheap and come off pretty easily.

The best thing about this set was the fine tooth comb with the lifting tip.
While not the worst set ever, I would never buy it again.

title: They work better for shorter hair. Not a fan.
text:
[[VIDEOID:d2cd0633602634d9c37bf5b80667da1e]] These are a velcro-like curler set, and the curlers were light purple.
You get six (6) each of four (4) different sizes. They come in a small ckear vinyl bag for storage. They also came with a handful (I didn't count) hair clips to help hold hair out of the way while rolling.

We tried these out on my daughter's hair, as a recent haircut left my hair too short to use them on. She has shoulder-length hair, and she could have used several more of the medium sized curlers.

I wrapped her hair in them (damp after a fresh shampoo). The first thing I learned was that these curlers do NOT like a lot of hair at a time. You can only do a small pinch, or the hair falls off to the sides. I also had to push the hair into the curlers to get it to stay.

I think things would have gone better if we had used a blow dryer to dry her hair faster. The curlers have good air flow. But, we went for air dry. They were left in until she could not stand having them on her head any more, about 45 minutes. They could have used a longer time.

So, I started to unroll her hair for her at her request.
- First lesson: the hair goes ON smoothly, but does NOT like to come off! If there is any dampness left in your hair, it acts like super glue with these curlers. Yikes!
- Second lesson: start taking curlers out from the bottom, so there is no extra hair to lay on top of any other curlers. That seems basic, but I somehow missed 3 of the smallest curlers, and it was NOT fun to get the loose from their hiding places.
- Third lesson: your hair will come out much better when it is totally dry. It seems to release better, although I still had to remove it from each curler a tiny section at a time.
You CANNOT just unroll these things.
Ever walked through a patch of cockleburrs? Yeah, they are like that.

So, she got a little curl from the ones that had dried, but not enough to be worth using all the time. I'll stick to the pink foam guys with the snaplocks on them! These purple curlers were a nightmare to get OUT of her hair.

title: Nice texture and color, but oddly cut
text:
This is kind of an odd wig. It has good texture, kind of like what your hair looks like when you've had it braided and undone the braids.

The top is much shorter than the back. It was very comfortable for the short time I had it on. The hair texture was good, definitely lots of body. It isn't as plastic-y feeling as some, although it is very unlikely this could pass as natural hair while wearing it.

I think this would need some trimming and/or styling to actually wear it. It is very "Billy Ray Cyrus" in the 1980's. Our thought on it was if the comedian Carrot Top had a musician son, this would be his hair.

I don't know how complementary this might be to actually wear. I plan to use this for craftin purposes. The color I got said "brown", but it is a medium brownish orange.

title: Very thick, a joke to wear daily
text:
The bottle is beautiful.
When they say "medium coverage", they are not kidding. It covered an age spot on my hand...not completely, but it didn't stand out.

But this product just isn't for me. This highlighted every crease and wrinkle on my skin. It was way too thick. I tried it on my hand first, and it made my skin look like alligator skin. Ugh!!

So, I am not sure who could use this.
It is too thick and opaque for face foundation, but too translucent to cover up varicose veins or tattooes. Perhaps it would be a good stage makeup where the audience does not get too close to you.
I cannot recommend this item, at least not for daily wear where other people can see you.

title: Nice texture, great color
text:
My review refers to the Jaystar prestretched synthetic hair in color #T1b/350.

The color is beautiful. It has a slight gradient effect that runs from a deep brown to a coppery brown. The strips are long, and you get a generous 8 packs of hair per package.

The texture was nice as well. It feels thick without being stiff. It also has a nice shine. I can't comment on wearability, because I do not actually wear this hair - I get it for crafting purposes. But this is one of the higher quality hair packs I've had, and look forward to using it. It looks to be one of the most natural-looking faux hair I own.

title: Good quality, cute favor idea, tastes like buttercream frosting
text:
This would be a perfect set to buy for a birthday party for favors.

The tube wrappers say "Happy Birthday" on them. The flavor is supposed to be birthday cake, but to me, it tastes more like buttercream frosting. Definitely sweet, which is a nice thing.

There is no tint on this one, so it goes on clear. Of course, you have Chapstick quality. There really is no downside to this one.

title: Love the texture, so soft
text:
I really like these particular braids.
They are very thick and super soft.
Note that I cannot speak to the ease of wearing them - I do not wear these hairpieces. But I do use them for craft purposes and love the texture.

title: Too dark, too opaque, zero 'natural' look
text:
I have problems with my eyebrows due to undertreated hypothyroidism...they end up being very sparse, so I like to try new waysto make them appear complete.

These pencils are NOT it.

I did not like how they went on at all...too solid and dark. All the colors I received were very dark. I could have used a fine point sharpie with more desireable results. The pencils go on too thick and dark no matter how you apply it. It is next to impossible to get a realistic brow look with these.

Maybe these would work for costume or theater purposes, or if you rock a unibrow look, but for the rest of us, these should be a hard pass.

title: Cute enough
text:
These are really cute. They are larger than expected and very colorful.

The directions are to place it where you want it (color side down of course) on a dry skin, and wet the tattoo, holding it in place for 30 seconds. I would suggest a soggy wet paper towel.
I'm saving some for September 19, Talk Like A Pirate Day. :-)

title: Individual wet wipes
text:
[[VIDEOID:cc7d0f86a05b39f86b30fe73af89c07a]] These are not compressed, dry cloths, but more like individually packaged baby wipes. They already have moisture in them - just tear open the packet.

They do a nice job of basic cleaning. These would be great to keep in a glove box for a quick clean after a drive-through lunch.

title: Don't bother. Not so much a loofah as a mitt scrubbie
text:
These are odd little scrubbers. Calling them loofahs are a stretch. These are small mitts that slide on to your hands. There is a small opening on both sides for your thumb, so it is good for right or left hands.

Loofah? Not really. Not like any I've bought over the last few decades. If anything, it is VERY mildly abrasive.
But the oddest thing is the blob of nylon they have sewn to the middle of the glove. I use nylon scrubbies all the time. This is softer than the ones I buy in the store.

The mitt is too small for most men's hands and most ladies wouldn't want this.

Honestly, I cannot think of any reason to buy this item. It is not a real loofah, not a real scrubbie, just a mashup of what they had on hand, it would seem.

title: Actually cleared up a dry patch.
text:
There are so many things out there to help your skin, it is hard to find something that actually helps and is reasonably priced.

This one actually had a good effect on my skin. I don't have really bad skin to start with: no acne, no scarring, etc. I do deal with some rosacea, and while I usually have the oily t-zone, I do have a dry patch on my forehead that arrived after I turned 50.

I used this for a couple weeks before writing my review, so I could give my actual experience with it. I found that this one actually did make a difference. The serum does not go as far as I had hoped. It takes more than other types I have tried. I'm not sure if it is just this product, or if my skin was soaking it up quickly.

I do have allergies and sensitive skin, so I am cautious about what I put on my face. The first week, I only did a small spot on one cheek to be sure I didn't have any reactions. I didn't.
Note that this is very viscous...it looks almost like water. One of my photos is of a few drops on my hand. There is also no noticable fragrance or scent, which I appreciate.

After 2 weeks, my forehead dry patch is gone. My cheeks feel baby-soft. I only used it on my face, and not around my eyes. I'd say that this one actually has made a difference, and works.

title: Nice makeup. Just watch the color
text:
Well, unless you know what color actually works for you, good luck ordering this kind of makeup online.

I wanted to try it, as it has sunscreen in it, and my old foundation is too old to use.

If you have seen the episode of the show "Friends" where Ross goes to the tanning booth, you will understand how the "soft honey" color looked on me! Haha! Huge fail.

But, the makeup went on smoothly and felt ok on my skin...it was just a horrible color match.

title: Not for fine hair.  Heavy clamps that need thick hair
text:
The plastic used to make these is very pretty.
However, these clips are SO HEAVY, they won't stay in my hair or my daughter's hair. Perhaps if you have super thick or super curly hair, these might work for you. But for us, they slid out of our hair merely turning our heads or walking. So, just know if you have fine hair, don't bother with these clips.

title: Very cute, nice colors
text:
Very cute package of small hair clamps in the shape of butterflies.

These are great for fine or thin hair. I used them on my own hair, which is baby fine and getting very thin. They held my hair back pretty well.

There is a nice assortment of colors, so if you want these as an accessory, you'll find something that will match or coordinate.

title: Great texture and soft feel, colors really nice
text:
This is great faux hair!
I've tried several kinds (I don't wear them myself - I use for crafting purposes), and most have had an unpleasant texture or feel to them.

This hair is very lightweight and super soft. It was very easy to work with. In my photos, my daughter put one braid on her hair just for fun. These braids would be perfect for costume uses as well.

Overall, very happy with the colors, the texture and the feel. I'll be buying this one again in other colors.

title: Ok, but would not repurchase
text:
You get two packets each of several kinds of cleaning cloths. Most are makeup removers.
I can see these being perfect to toss in a backpack, purse or gym bag. Since you need to tear them open, they won't leak like a bottle of something might.

Overall, a convenient item.

title: Too hard to open
text:
Well, the idea behind these is nice...lifting your hair roots while they dry to get more volume in your hair.

I am not sure if they would even stay in my hair - it is pretty fine.
But I'll never know.
I could not get these things open!! I tried one-handed, then tried using both hands. Nope. The clamps are so tight, I could not get them to open at all.

So, be aware you need a lot of hand strength to use these.

title: Not a color I normally buy, but I like it
text:
This is a Sally Hansen nail polush from their Color Therapy line. The color is "Lips Tulips".

This is a little brighter color than I normally wear. It is a pearlized color, which is why I wanted to try it. Of course, color is subjective, which is why we have so many colors from which to choose. I have pretty fair skin, so it looks ok on me. Forgive the unmanicured hand, but this is what two coats looked like on my thumbnail, going over a chipped clear coat (why there are so many bumps!).
The polish was a little too easy to just lift off my nail a couple days later, but to be fair, I did not put any sealer over it, as I needed to do my nails in general.

I actually liked this one, despite it being darker than what I normally purchase.

title: Kind of highlighter pink, plain finish not pearlized
text:
This is a Sally Hansen Extreme Wear polish. The shade is "Watermelon Felon".

How it looks on you will totally depend upon your skin tone. I have very fair skin, and it looks a little like I used a fluorescent pink highlighter on my nails. (Sorry for the bad picture - I need a manicure! But, it gives you an idea on how bright pink this polish is - and it is regular polish (not matte or pearl).

This isn't my cup of tea, but I am sure plenty of people would enjoy the bright shade.

title: Ok, but not great. Soft to the touch
text: Soft, but the actual overall texture was not what I was looking for.

title: Works well. Good size. Plastic frame.
text:
This is a nice, small mirror with magnification on one side. I chose rose gold, and I like the color.
The frame is plastic, and I thought it was going to be metal. But it will still serve its purpose, which is providing better magnification to put on eye makeup.

title: A bit heavy, but great looking design, cuts well.
text:
[[VIDEOID:33a651af8e0ead4e422ea4d4950b7674]] I've cut hair non-professionally for decades (although my mom was a beautician for several years and always did everyone's hair). As such, I've used a lot of different trimmers and clippers.

I have to say that I really like these trimmers. They look different than anything else I own. The burnished gold finish and decorative design is something I really liked.

This is very heavy in my hand. If I was doing a lot of hair every day, it might be too much for me. But for the occasional haircut and/or trim, it is great.

This comes with three different clip-on depth controls. I never use them, but they are there if someone needs them. You get a cord for USB charging.
The gold part appears to have ovals that look like a button to push, but it is just part of the design. The actual on/off switch is in the bottom of the handle, next to the charging port.

Overall, I am very happy with these clippers. They look good, work well and no cords to drag around someone's neck.

title: Thick, heavy clippers
text:
This is the first time I've seen nail clippers come in a special box. These come in a tin with a black flocked insert.

The clippers themselves are very nice. They are the large (toenail) size. They are pretty heavy, so they might be a little awkward if you have small hands or arthritis.

There is a nice nail file on the flip side as well.

title: Well made, but did nothing for me
text:
I've never used a facial roller of any kind before, so was curious as to what, if any, benefit there might be.

The roller and attachments seem to be well-made.

This feels very nice on my skin...a cool, smooth roll. Bur I have to say, I did not see any real benefit to using this. I have oily skin. Perhaps if someone had very dry skin and used this with a moisturizer, they could see some visible results. Sadly, it seemed to make no change for me.

title: Great set to have on hand
text:
Most ladies like their nails to look nice. We also know how it is to break a favorite buffer or file, or lose them and go without until the next time we can shop.

This kit actually will solve some of those problems. You get plenty of various kinds of files and buffers, ready to smooth out big rough areas, or just take care of a small snag.

This is a great kit to have on hand. I really like it.

title: Great files for toenails, mens hands. Very heavy duty
text:
These are truly heavy duty nail files. In fact, these would be great for guys. Men get rough, snaggy nails too. These will take care of those, and are large enough to hang on to, even with large "man hands".

For women, these are pretty rough, but would work well for toenails and even edges of your heels.

These are nice additions to your home nail kits, but definitely too big and rough to be the only files. Love the green color too.

title: I really like this one
text:
I wanted to actualy use this for a while before writing a review.
I have sensitive skin, so am always a little leery of new skin products, yet always looking for something I can safely use.

The serum is cloudy, but you don't see that - it goes on clear. It absorbs fairly quickly. There is a slight scent to it, but it is pleasant.

The biggest results I have seen personally is on my forehead. This serum has made it much smoother. After a week of use, I started seeing skin flaking, and almost stopped using it. But I realized my skin was not red or irritated, so continued use to see what would happen. The flaking continued for a week more, then smoother skin emerged.

Right now, my forehead feels nice and soft, and the skin looks good. I have not experienced anything negative about this serum, and will likely continue to use it.

title: Not bad for the price
text:
This was super easy to put on, and glided without pulling delicate skin.
I didn't have an allergic reactions to it, so that's good.

I also drew on my hand so I could literally check on the longevity, to see how it handled being washed, etc. It did a pretty good job. I had to rub my hand really hard to get it to come off at all. Overall, pleased with this eyeliner.

title: Nice looking, feels good in the hand
text:
[[VIDEOID:992cf67b54f1d35441f31fb8d815079e]] This is a really nice-looking rotary head razor. Now, I don't personally use this type of razor, so I am going to let my hubby tell me if it is good or bad.

It feels great in my hand. Very nice balance. The color is great! The heads feel kind of cheap and light to me, but that is not necessarily an indicator of how well they shave.

This has a pop-out sideburn trimmer. It comes with a small brush to ckean out the heads, but you can use water to clean this razor out as well.

Overall, this is not a super top quality razor, but it is definitely nice looking. I'll update my review should any big negatives (or positives) surface from regular use.

title: Surprisingly strong. Held my fine hair
text:
I have to say, these little guys surprised me!

I have baby fine hair, and haven't had much success in finding a clamp that will stay put. So, I really was not expecting much from what appears to be a cheap plastic clamp.

Well, I was surprised!
First off, these translucent clamps are made of a very sturdy material. I really like the translucent part as well.
But what was most surprising was the strength of the clips! These are not super easy to open - not from being poorly designed, but from having a very strong clamp.

I am both surprised and very happy to report that this is the first clamp that has actually held and STAYED in my very fine hair. Don't let the appearance fool you on these hair clips - they can and do get the job done.

title: Very nice, and a great color too. Extra long uptake tubes reach all the liquid
text:
These are actually really nice spray bottles. The bottle is a softer plastic that is sturdy, but still has some give to it. The color will keep you from seeing actual liquids inside clearly, so if you put different contents in them, you'll need to label the bottles (no labels included).

The sprayer is a hard plastic. It has a very long uptake tube, so no more leftover liquids inside because the tube was too short to reach it. The sprayer is properly labeled, with the "spray" spraying and the "stream" is actually the stream. (It might sound basic, but the last set we got, the sprayers were labeled the exact opposite of what they did.)

These bottles are 16 ounces, so they hold roughly the equivalent of a bottle of water.

Overall, I like them. They work very well, and look good doing their jobs.

title: Great set for home use
text:
I am very happy with these hair clips.
They have a matte metallic finish that looks very nice.

The grip us secure enough to hold up nearly any type of hair. It even held up my baby-fine hair.

This set comes with both long and shorter clamps, and a plastic rattail comb for parting your hair.

Overall, very pleased with this set.

title: Large enough to be useful
text:
Finally...
A back scrubber you don't have to be a contortionist to use! Most I've tried have been so short, they are totally useless.

I like the length on this scrubber, as well as the texture. I need to put a hook up in the tub area to hang it on to dry though...I had to fold it in half, which won't allow good air drying.
Overall, I was happy with this one. I felt clean, was able to use it even with a wonky shoulder, and the texture was perfect for showering.

title: Did NOT like this one
text:
Smells yucko. Lots of ingredients I don't expect in a facial serum. It is creamy, but very odd.

It promotes itself as "organic". It lists New York as home base. The thing is, there are currently NO USA legal definitions or regulations on what can be called organic. You can slap that label on anything without legal repercussion or accountability, so it means virtually nothing in America. For an "organic" product, they have a lot of weird things in their formula.

I used it a few times on one side of my face, to see if there would be any sort of difference or reaction. Happy to report that there was no inflammatory response, but not keeping this one. Why? The smell. A huge "nope" from me. While it doesn't smell like garbage, it does not smell good either.
I just cannot recommend this product. Their idea behind it is ok, but the real benefit with most vegetables is their INTERNAL benefit from consuming them - not rubbing a carrot on your face.

There are more buzzwords than benefits on this product. Pass.

title: More youth sized than adult. Wouldn't stay on my head
text:
I had higher expectations for these headbands. They are advertised as adult sized bands. I thought they would be great for holding my hair out of the way while doing facials.

Nope.

These will stretch over my adult head, but that doesn't mean they will fit. I can get a big rubber band to stretch enough to fit - doesn't mean it can do the job.

These are closer to youth size tyan adult. I got it stretched out over my normal-sized head. But every time I moved or turned my head, the headband would start shifting off my head, seeking to return to its original small size.

I tried it on both dry hair and after a shower with wet hair. Same results...too small. The only thing this worked for was to wrap around my daughter's ponytail.

Hard pass on these if you are an adult. The rest of them went into the trash can.

title: Easy to use, blends nicely, no skin reactions
text:
I've never tried makeup in a squeeze bag before, so wasn't sure what to expect.

I was pleasantly surprised. It was easy to use, didn't drip, and sealed back up well.

The makeup itself was just fine and did a nice job of covering and smoothing out skin. I do have sensitive skin, and did not experience any redness or breakouts with this makeup.

title: It looks nice, a little goopy, but doesn't last long on its own
text:
I've always liked Revlon products, so expected this to be no different. I am also a little more "old school", and do NOT like the matte lip effect - it looks like you need to drink more water!

This is a fairly soft lipstick. I was very cautious on how much I "dialed up" to apply. This is very glossy and moist (ew to that word, but it is true! Ha!). It didn't feel super sticky like some glosses, although it is more "wet" than I personally prefer.

This color, "So Sleek Pink" looks okay on me. Not my personal favorite, but it was a nice, neutral shade.

Overall, these are nice lipsticks. It just isn't my personal favorite texture.

title: Nice bead filling, but it smells so bad!
text:
The first noticeable thing about this mask was the smell. Oh my gosh...did they find this under a compost bin?

Once you can get past the obnixious smell, the beads actually shape nicely around your face. The back has a hook-and-loop adjustable closure, which is nice.

We stuck the mask in the freezer (per directions, they say to freeze, not refrigerate, and says the beads will stay loose). We shall see if it helps kill the smell.

title: Too heavy, awkward
text:
This is a set of three metal nail tools.
The metal has a rainbow patina that looked really cute.

These are actually cute with the coloring. But, on the two straight cuticle tools, the metal is so heavy, they are more awkward than comfortable to actually use. I had high hopes for this set, but they are just not something I want to use on a regular basis. (They also made my hands smell like metal, which I did not care for either.)

title: Cute enough
text:
This is a fun little hair braid. It has a "gradient" color appearance. The braid is nice and thick, and could definitely add volume to thinning hair. In the photos, we did a simple clip-on onto my daughter's hair. Then we did a loose bun just to see what it would look like.

Overall, I like the quality and texture.

title: Nice texture
text: I don't have a whole lot to say about this as far as wearing it. I actually bought this for crafting purposes.  The hair is very soft and workable. It doesn't feel straw-like or rough.  I like it quite a bit, and will probably get other colors in the future.

title: Great for keeping hair pieces tangle-free
text:
I don't use a lot of hair extensions, but I do like to use them for craft purposes. I'd had them stored in a box, but these bags make a lot more sense.

They are what I call "hot pink" - very bright. That's great. They are roomy, and have large tassels at the ends of the drawstrings for easy closing and hanging.

I tucked a hairpiece into one today. Super simple, and will help keep them tangle free.

title: Too out of balance, awkward
text:
[[VIDEOID:78c5e3c29c1cf5a408675e86f50f5614]] It has been years since I had a lighted makeup mirror and thought this might be good to try.

This comes all folded up, and you unfold the various mirror sections. The magnification part is ok, but the mirror itself is awkward. It sits up on a stand, but is too top-heavy to be stable on any surface but a flat, hard one. In other words, you are not going to be able to sit on your bed and use it for putting on makeup...you'll have to hold it up with one hand and use your free hand to try to put on makeup.

It is really odd and awkward to use if you can't leave it out on a bathroom counter or makeup table. It was disappointing.

title: Really nice set. Easy fit in my hands
text:
[[VIDEOID:b013cd518ef34cac5e91a17fcd2c8475]] This is actually a very nice clipper set.
It feels good in your hand, and the length attachment guides are easy to put on and take off.
It comes with a small container of oil to keep blades at their maximum functioning, as well as a small brush for easy cleaning.

The shaver itself is nice looking, and has good design. I had no problems cutting my son's hair down short to a modified buzz cut for work. My big clippers tend to put my hand to sleep, so these are a great alternative. They look great, they are designed well, and were very easy to use.

title: Definitely fun for costume use
text:
This is a novelty item, but still fun.

A baseball cap has artificial women's long hair sewn inside. There is a little hair sewn over the inside opening of the back of the cap to continue the illusion.

The cap itself is kind of awkward to adjust and doesn't have a lot of flexibility. If you have a strangely large head, the cap probably won't fit.

This comes with a mini metal-tooth comb, presumably for wig care, a hook-n-loop patch to hold back your bangs, a wig cap and a spray bottle. No idea what the spray bottle is for - there are no care directions of any kind included.

This is fun for a costume use. The hair is pretty heavy, so be aware of that. Other than that, have fun with this!

title: Great idea...WAY WAYY too short!
text:
I was looking forward to this item. I could use some back help in the shower. Well, I need to keep on looking.

This is a silicone strip with two different textures, one on each side.
It has handles on both ends. Easy to keep clean, should do a decent scrub job.

HOWEVER...this is WAYY too short! I don't have super flexible shoulders. I could not get this item situated so both hands could grab it. If one hand had an end, the other end was out of reach. Seriously, who has such a tiny diameter? Kids? That's my best guess...it would be ok for a kid's back scrubber.

So, it is impossible for most adult humans of average size to use this thing.
I'm thinking of ways to make a cat toy out of it. They like to rub their faces on all kinds of textures.
But it fails as a bath/shower back scrubber.

title: Excellent clippers
text:
It is kind of hard to get excited over a pair of nail clippers. But, if you've ever used a bad pair...well, if you are reading reviews about nail clippers, you've had bad pairs!

These are truly NICE clippers. I love the sleek black handles. They come with their own brown leather holster, apparently to keep the black surface from getting scratched up.

There are also built-in nail files on the flat surfaces that did a better and quicker job on a rough piece of nail than any file I've ever used. The clippers themselves easily cut through both fingernails and toenails. (I broke my thumbnail yesterday and thought I'd have to start over. These saved my nail from having to cut it completely level with the quick.)

If you are wondering if you should really spend this much money for a pair of clippers, the answer is YES, yes you should. These are absolutely worth it

title: Doesn't cut any hair of any thickness any where!
text:
The idea behind this one is okay...it is like a man's rotary shaver that has three shaving heads, and ONE was removed and put into a plastic tube.

The idea is good, but the execution is a fail. I'm not sure what this is supposed to shave off, unless it is peach fuzz. There are SO many women who deal with hormone issues and find unwanted hair growing in places it never did before. We seek shavers that will take off that rogue hair without cutting our skin.
This razor is useless for that.

First off, this is another USB charging item. I find that really annoying to not be able to just pop a fresh battery in there as needed. If you had an extended time without electricity for some reason, all these USB-powered things would die quickly with regular use, and you'd be stuck with them. Anyway...

Your skin is protected - we (both my daughter and I tried it) did not get any cuts or nicks - so no worries about getting hurt. BUT... it also did not remove hair! We tried several areas where rogue hairs or extra fuzz has been showing up. For this menopausal mama, it meant weird chin hairs and random mustaches showing up. For her, it meant hairs under her chin on her neck (under-dosed thyroid issues and PCOS). This razor took off a few tops from the neck hairs, but left rough stubble. It did NOTHING for my lady 'stache at all.

So, while the design is nice, it feels nice in your hand, and the theory behind it is good, this thing is majorly under-powered and therefore, just a trinket for the junk drawer. I can't recommend it.

title: Large quantity of basic nail brushes
text:
There is not a whole lot to actually review regarding nail brushes. If they are fairly sturdy and bristles embedded well, it is pretty good.

We received eight nail brushes - two each of purple, blue, pink and teal. They were not packaged up, just 8 brushes tossed in a mailing envelope. The bristles are a fine clear filament. They would not be strong enough to deal with dried mud or clay, but are certainly good enough for basic or daily cleaning.

With eight brushes, it makes it easy to keep them near every sink. I also tucked one in my manicure case.

The colors are translucent with a little bit of glitter in them. Nice looking, and I'm sure they'll do the job.

title: Too runny, would NOT repurchase
text:
I bought this to try, on the mistaken assumption that soap is soap. Nope!

I am sure it does just fine in cleaning.
I bought this because I wanted a clear soap to go in my dispenser.

Softsoap is reasonably thick, and I thought this would be the same. I was wrong. The viscosity is barely different from water!
After I had filled my pump, I noticed a lot of soap had run down the side, which was odd, but I shrugged it off, washed off the bottle and put it away.

When I went to wash my hands, I found the difference. I pumped once, like I've always done to get a little soap in my hand. This stuff shot out of the dispenser, bypassed my hand entirely, and hit the opposite side of the sink! It is SO runny, it is ridiculous.
It is like water. Now I barely pump and keep my hand OVER it so it doesn't shoot across the counter!

I will not buy this again.
Very runny, not a real savings.

title: great tips, worth buying name brand.
text:
It;s Q-tips. There is not a lot to be said about them, except that there really IS a difference when it comes to the amount of cotton on the swab, as well as how well it stays on the swab. Q-Tip brand has a nice amount of cotton - you won't scratch your ear with the stick on these.
I've also not had the cotton come off in my ear like one of the cheap brands.

This is one of those little items that are worth paying for the name brand.

title: Great stuff - love it!!
text:
This is some of the best stuff out there for rough skin treatment.
They do sell it at a nationwide department store, but they've been out for months. I turned to Amazon and easily found it.

Many people don't seem to understand how to use this product, so I'll explain it.
Start with dry hands (clean, no lotions or soaps).
Shake the bottle very well to mix up the contents - otherwise, you'll get runny, thin white watery liquid that leaves behind the good stuff.
What should be in your hand is a thicker white liquid that feels grainy. Use about a nickel-sized blob in the palm of one hand.

Once you have that, rub your hands together, palm to palm. Keep rubbing.
You think you are done? Keep rubbing. The liquid will dry out and you'll have a textured feel left over. Keep rubbing.
This is the stuff that removes the dry or dead skin from your hands and fingers. You can rub one finger at a time with it.
You SHOULD be seeing junk flaking off, if you have done it right. Do this over a trash can! :-)

Once you are done and all the white stuff is all gone, you can now wash your hands with soap and water.
What you'll have left is very smooth skin!

title: Wooden handles make it easy to control the swab
text:
I love these!

I used to use this sort of swab back in the dinosaur ages when you had to demagnetize your 8-track and cassette players!
I used this type to apply the cleaning fluid to the rollers! Ha!

What I use them for now is for cleaning kitty cat ears. The extra length really helps, and the wooden handle doesn't bend, causing a swab to flip into the wrong area. I'll always buy them for cat purposes, although they could have great use for crafting as well, with paint applications or fussy gluing.

title: Great for cleaning pet ears.
text:
I haven't bought this type of swab since I had a ton of stereo equipment all over the house and was keeping the cassette decks demagnetized!

But, we got two new kittens, and decided that an unbendable swab might be just the thing that could help keep their ears clean.
Sure enough, our kittens (adopted from a shelter) came complete with very dirty ears, a scabby outbreak that required medicated shampooing weekly, and adorable personalities. These things are wonderful for easily reaching into a damp kitten ear and pulling out the dirt. (Not all dirt is from eat mites - kittens are born with nasty stuff in their ears that eventually works its way to the surface.) No mites, but lots of dirt. Right after their medicated baths, it is a cinch to use these to wipe out the brown goo from their little tiny ears. No bending and flipping like a regular swab would, and I can keep my hand far enough away from their ears to be comfortable for them. (Remember to not dig in too far - just wipe out all that surface dirt!)

I was very happy with these and will definitely buy them again.

title: Love the scent, feels nice on my skin
text:
This is probably my new favorite body wash!
I love Oil of Olay products already, but didn't care much for their other Ribbons scents.
This one has a great fresh scent. It feels great against my skin too.

I saw some other negative remarks in regards to this "not being moisturizing enough".
Well, I think it is perfect. I don't want to feel greasy or slick when I get out of the shower! If you have horribly dry skin, you need a separate body moisturizer.. showers are already a little bit drying. It is unrealistic to think that soap will cure dry skin.

My only slightly negative note is that these bottles were much smaller than I expected. It is sometimes hard to visualize liquid ounces. But now I know... the ones I normally see at the store are 18 oz... these are only TEN ounces, so be aware they are small. I probably would not buy them again, but I will DEFINITELY buy this scent again. It made the entire bathroom smell great!

title: Better for hands than face, but not a bad one
text:
I bought this one online because my OofO bottle was getting low.
As it turns out, it was NOT the same one I buy when shopping in person.
This one is a little thicker and creamier, and it would be too much for my oily skin
on my face.

BUT.... this one is GREAT for your hands and arms!
Hands are one of the first places to look old, and we often neglect them.
This has been fabulous for my hands.

title: Not bad at all for the price
text:
We first smelled this in a WalMart. They had the aftershave named after several big cities.
Cute theory.

Anyway, this one (Vegas) actually smells pretty good on my husband. He normally wears
either Preferred Stock or Photo, and was looking for something less expensive for wearing to
his work.

The only complaint he has is how quickly it fades. It is gone in a very short amount of time,
and that is for anyone, not just the wearer.

title: Smells really good on my husband
text:
Well, it is a little hard to write a review about a scent.
After all, each fragrance will smell different on each person,
thanks to body chemistries.

My husband wanted to try this one after smelling it in person in
a Wal Mart store. He went back to get it after Christmas and they were
sold out. So, we turned to Amazon. Of course they had it!

Our order arrived quickly, packed carefully and was fresh product.
This scent smells very clean and mildly manly, if that makes sense!
(In other words, I wouldn't wear it... some colognes are almost unisex,
but this is not one of them.

My husband smells great in this.
If it helps anyone, he also smells wonderful in Preferred Stock,
and Lagerfeld's Photo. So, if those scents are pleasing to you
when worn by your male, then you'll probably like this too.

I think it will make a good cologne for summer as well.
The scent is not overwhelming, almost less than I'd like, but it
seems to have lasting power. You can still faintly smell it on his
neck when he gets home from work (and he has a very physical job).
At the current price point, it is hard to not at least try this one.

title: Not as much of a frost as I had hoped for
text:
That's the problem with buying nail polish online - unless you are reordering
a favorite color, it is a roll of the dice as to what you will really get.
It isn't a fault of the seller - monitors display different colors all the time.

The color is a nice deep pink. However, I would not really classify this one as a frost.
I guess it is a little lighter than a plain color, but it isn't even close to the pearly look
of many of my frost polishes.

The polish itself went on smoothly, and has lasted very well.
I didn't do a formal manicure - I just popped it on to see what it would look like with
my skin tone (fairly pale white chick with blue undertones). It looks really good.

I have a fuchsia colored t-shirt, and when I put my hands up against the shirt, the nail
polish almost looks like a match! It definitely coordinates well with it.

I probably would not buy this one again on purpose, but simply because I like a bigger frost
appearance than this one gives - I would call this more of a pearlized finish than a frost, but
it could be just semantics.

The quality is standard Sally Hansen, and I have zero problems with that.
The tips have chipped a bit after a week of wear and daily typing, but that's pretty good,
since I didn't put any type of sealer coat on it - just this polish.

title: This looks like a frost, but isn't.
text:
Okay, so you are probably thinking "who buys nail polish online?".
Lots of folks, especially when you can't get certain colors in your area.

Anyway, loved the appearance of this shade. Being a great brand, there
was not really too much risk involved. Sally Hansen makes a great nail polish.

I am leaving a review for those who might be wondering about what this shade
actually looks like on your fingernails.

While it LOOKS like a frost in the bottle, this is not really a frost color.
It is a very pretty pink, to be sure.

I thought the diamond referred to the strength and chip-proofing. Not sure if that is all it refers to.
This color is a translucent pink with a lot of sparkle. Not like the children's polish
with glitter chunks in them, but a very fine sparkle.
I'll load photos as soon as possible.

I have two coats on, and you can easily see the nail tips still.
I don't think you can get a solid color coverage at all with this one.

Of course, everyone has a personal preference on how they like their fingernails.
I like a solid frost color for the majority of the time.
This is very pretty, but I think I'd use a coat of it OVER another frost polish
that gives more coverage. (I like a solid look with no tip visible.)

No regrets at all about the purchase, but did want to be sure someone else who was shopping
online would know that this isn't going to look like the bottle shade on your nails -
just lots of sparkle.

title: Good but not great
text:
I love a man who smells good! We have no decent stores or malls in our area, which is why I often shop online.
So, I had never smelled this one before. I decided to take a chance, since it had pretty decent reviews, and of course, a great looking bottle! LOL It was a fair value here on Amazon, so it was worth the price.
Our former favorite men's cologne was Lagerfeld's [[ASIN:B000C214OW Photo By Karl Lagerfeld For Men. Eau De Toilette Spray 4.2 Ounces]], but they have changed the formula on that one, and we didn't much care for how light that fragrance is now - it's gone within the hour after putting it on. It is like they have weakened it beyond belief for reasons unknown. So, I've been searching online for a new scent. Not an easy task, I might add, since I can't just smell them. I have been reading reviews and fragrance layers to get an idea of what might be good.

We received our order very quickly and in great shape. It was obviously fresh stuff, so that was great.

My husband has been wearing it all week now, and here is my take on this one:

It smells very fresh and clean, in a non-soapy, just-showered way. I hope that makes sense.
It does not smell like soap or shampoo, but smells like fresh laundry, perhaps.

So far, only one person has mentioned the new fragrance to him at work, and that was a guy, so not so sure about the "sexy" qualities of this one! Ha ha! It does seem to stay for a few hours, but by the end of the day, you can't really smell anything except on the collar of his shirt.

Would I buy it again? Both my husband and I vote nope.

While good, it isn't great, and doesn't create that "who is that hunk" sensation.
I realize everyone is different, and skin oils, even medications taken can affect how a scent smells on an individual.

That being said, it isn't what we were looking for for us, but if you like a clean, the-washing-machine-just-finished
type of scent, then you'll like this one. We'll keep looking for something a little more to our liking.

title: Fabulous brush for fine hair
text:
I have very fine hair that takes a miracle or a perm to curl.
However, this brush has been great!

I heat it up first with my hair dryer. Since it works on thermal principle,
you need to get it warm to get the best action from it. Once warm, I
let the brush grab a section of hair. I curl it backwards, then use the blow dryer
on that section for maybe 20-30 seconds max. Repeat all over your head.

You'll have nice curls!
Of course, fine hair doesn't hold curls for a long time, so I always use hair spray.
Some might have success with a mousse holding products.
When I do have a perm, this brush also works to give the curls control and direction,
then I don't need any spray. It's a win-win item.

I am just now buying another brush. I've had my other one for maybe
7 years now, purchased at a beauty supply house. The bristles are finally getting
pushed in, and you can't get them back out. But I'd say that it's been a great brush,
and lasted plenty long! : )

The one I have, as well as the one pictured, has a pretty blue metal barrel with black bristles.
I sure hope the new one has the same color combo, because I love it.

title: It's okay, but wish it ran on AA batteries instead
text:
Our old beard trimmer finally gave up, so I was in the market for a new one.
I bought this one because I loved the way it looked and it said battery operated.

Well, be aware that when you buy "battery operated", it simply means there is no cord.
This one is a LITHIUM battery. That means that you have to CHARGE it, and often.
That part has been a big disappointment to me. I wanted a trimmer that you just popped new
batteries in as needed.

The problem with this model is that it dies randomly. You can't use it while it is charging
either. Yes, it will turn on, but there's no power behind it. We don't use it every day, so
don't have the need or space to keep it plugged in all the time. That means it's a roll of the
dice any time you want to use it as to whether or not it will have enough charge to do the job.

Yesterday, we hadn't used it for a while, and I went to trim my husband's sideburns.
Dead in the box - no power at all. I charged it for maybe 10 minutes, thinking that would at least
give us enough oomph to trim those little spots of hair. Nope. Started up fine, but died before I
could complete the second sideburn.

The other thing is that this takes an adapter, so it is yet another adapter that needs to be stored
some place! I keep all our hair cutting things in a box (I do our family's hair at home, having had
a beautician in the family, I learned plenty from her). It is uber annoying to pull out the box
to work on hair and have no power, despite having not used it. So, the battery discharges itself
whether you use it or not. I hate that!

The design is wonderful - it feels so good in the hand, easy to use, ergonomic.
If they would just go back and rework the battery part, this would be the perfect trimmer.
As is, it annoys the heck out of me. The blade cuts cleanly, and the plastic length guide
does a good job as well.

So, if you use a trimmer daily and can keep the charger close by, then you'll love this one.
If you only use it from time to time, be prepared to plan a day ahead and charge it, or be
tempted to toss it into the trash can.

title: Love Photo, but not the bottle we received. Fake or old?
text:
Very disappointed in the purchase.
I am not sure what to write in the review here, because I believe this is where you review the product,
not the seller. But I cannot help but bring this matter up in here, to perhaps keep someone else from
being ripped off.

My husband smells wonderful in Photo.
It has been a while since we bought any, because it is fairly expensive and we've been through a rough patch.
I thought I'd celebrate a change in the situation with a bottle of his favorite cologne.

There is barely any scent in the bottle we received.
I don't know if what is being sent out on this listing is older than dirt and therefore
weak, or it has somehow been watered down or forged and resealed.

Whatever is going on with it, it barely smells like Photo at all.
I guess it was indeed a deal too good to be true.
The shipment was quick, and it LOOKS like a new, sealed bottle, but when sprayed,
you about have to stick a nostril directly on it to smell anything at all.
DEFINITELY not like regular Photo!! The real thing can be smelled very clearly and you don't have
to be super close. Even after a direct spray and sniff, almost nothing.
Something is very wrong here.

Lagerfeld Photo is an amazing scent that smells fantastic on men.
We used to purchase ours at Dillards, but no longer live near a mall.
However, the bottle I received (and apparently others as well) purchased from THIS listing
barely resembles the Photo scent. If I was blindfolded and asked to identify the scent,
I would wonder if someone was kidding with me - yes, it is that weak.
On my rating - if it was based on this purchase alone, I would rate it one star.
(Actually, less than one, but you can't do half-stars.)
If it was based on true fresh Photo spray, I would rate it a five.
Therefore, I went with a two, because this is not a fresh product,
and I feel a bit ripped off. It can't be returned.

BE FOREWARNED:
The regular Photo is fantastic, but what is being sold in THIS particular listing
is either tampered with or older than dirt itself.
Buy it someplace else if you want the true Photo scent.

UPDATE JULY 2011:

title: Really great product! A must-have for dry hands
text:
I wish I had seen this listing before I bought the three-pack! ; )

Here's my review of this item from the other listing:
Well, I've been using this stuff for many, many years.
I can't say for sure that they have changed the formula. I do think that it worked a little better,
or perhaps a little quicker, when it was in the light blue normal bottle.
It is almost impossible to find in stores any more. We used to purchase it at WalMart, but they never
have it in stock. There's still a spot on the shelves, but never any product.

I really, really HATE this "foot" shaped bottle! The exfoliating part of the mix tends
to settle around the pink base, so be sure to shake the heck out of it EACH time you use it.
To the people who have said it was a little watery, it is probably from the stupid bottle design.
While it might be a little artistic, it is not practical, and make the liquid harder to use.
Good luck getting the last of the liquid out at the bottom of the bottle too - I had to put my
little finger in the bottle to get it to come out. I even added a little bit of warm water, which used
to help remix the drier part. Not any more - I had gunk and water. Shame on them for this lousy design!
We get it - you wanted it to look like a foot. It is still a bad design for the lotion inside!

Meanwhile, the product itself is still wonderful. I've tried making home versions, but it never works as well.
There is a trick to this stuff. You don't just put it on like hand lotion. Use it on DRY SKIN (not wet from the
shower) and you'll get better results. Do this over a trash can the first time you try it! Anyway, continue to rub,
like you were rubbing something that had to be ground in to your skin. You'll want to continue to rub even after
you can't see the lotion any more. Keep rubbing. That's it - keep going. You'll start to see little bits of white.
That's the dead skin cells. Keep rubbing - they'll continue to come off. Brush them off as they come off into your
trash can. Sound gross? It's just your dead skin cells - don't worry. Once you aren't getting any more junk off,
you can either try again with some more of this lotion, or if you think you're good, go wash your hands with
soap and water, dry them, and put on your normal hand lotion. Especially work this stuff in to your knuckles.
It is amazing how dry skin can get there! My hands feel like the proverbial baby bottom after a good round
of this lotion being worked in.

It is amazing how much this stuff really does work. In addition to hands, you can really use it anywhere.
I use it on my legs for dry winter skin, my face for the dry patches that have somehow started showing up where
regular skin used to reside, elbows and knees, and of course, feet and hands. It is really great.

But whoever designed this current bottle needs to be fired!
I don't want art, I want lotion. The bottle does NOT function well and adds a certain
amount of annoyance to the product.

Very happy with these.

title: Simply the best ...
text:
I've been using these elastics for years for a reason: they're the best available.

I have waist-length hair that I need to keep off my face, so I use a variety of hair accessories, ranging from headbands to simple elastics (like these). I love the color selection here and you get a lot for the price.

Most important for me: they have NO metal! Why is that important, you ask? Well, you can't wear anything metal when you get an MRI. As a brain tumor survivor, I have to get annual (at least) MRIs to check for possible recurrence. And keeping my hair off my face while I'm going through the "tube" is important to me. So ... I can use one of these without any problems at all.

That may seem like a small thing, but it's important to me. Also, since there's no metal "connector," these are easier on your hair and not as likely to cause breakage.

And they last FOREVER. Seriously -- my hair is relatively thick, and one of these will last at least 6-8 months of daily use.

Still my #1 choice. Scünci is doing it right.

title: Very pretty, but ...
text:
I have waist-length hair and use a variety of hair accessories to keep it out of my face, including headbands.

I really like the design of these -- they're very pretty, and getting two makes them an economical choice (black and tortoiseshell). They're also well made -- no sharp edges, the intricate design is well-formed, etc.

My only issue is that they're a little too tight for my head. I can wear one of these for about 2 hrs or so before I have to remove it. This isn't any fault of the manufacturer -- my head is probably a bit larger than "normal" and there's no way to determine how something like this will fit without trying it.

So -- if your head is small- to normal-size, these will probably be just fine. If your head is a bit on the large side, these might be a little tight for you.

title: Definitely impressed!

title: So far, no problems at all ...
text:
I have very long, very thick, very curly hair, and keeping it "corralled" and out of my face requires the use of either an elastic or a hair clip. As I've gotten older and developed fairly severe osteoarthritis in my shoulders, using an elastic has become more problematic. So that means finding hair clips that are sufficiently large and strong to keep my hair secured.

These looked promising, so I decided to give them a try.

So far, I'm quite happy with them. They're easy to use, big enough to hold my hair, and stay in without slipping. Bear in mind I have a LOT of hair, so that helps with keeping them in place with no slippage.

I like the colors -- I tend to wear black or navy slacks with jewel-toned tops, and these colors fit very nicely into that. No problems with breakage, either. No complaints at all. Very happy with this purchase and will purchase again if needed (or if they come out in new colors).

title: Work great for long thick hair ...
text:

These, however, are the exception. They work great! They open wide enough to enable me to secure all the hair and hold tight enough that there's no danger of slippage. I've also slept with one of these still in place (I usually do a side ponytail), and there were absolutely no problems at all. They're sturdy enough to withstand a lot of abuse.

I just ordered the second set of these so that I'll have all the colors. The sparkle is subtle, so they work great with both casual and "dressier" attire. I took the first set on a truncated World Cruise in Jan 2020, and got a lot of compliments (before we had to disembark after making it to Australia). Definitely good quality and attractive.

This one is a great size, VERY sturdy, and doesn't rip the hair -- it just teases out the tangles. It has a "softer" feel -- not like the typical hard plastic wide-tooth comb -- so it's gentle on the hand (I have osteoarthritis in my hands so things like this help).

At the price point (less than five dollars), it's a good value as it's sturdy enough to withstand a lot of use/abuse. Five stars.

text:

title: Working great in the South Pacific...
text:
I’m currently 14 days into a 28-day cruise through the South Pacific, round trip out if San Diego, CA, so there are a lot of ”sea days” with no ports of call which means lots if time near the pool and on my balcony. And lots of sun! I’m a fair-skinned descendant of Welsh ancestors and I’ve experienced some rather spectacular sunburns over the years. Doc has recommended using sunscreen with an SPF of at least 50.

Enter this La Roche-Posay Anthelios Melt-in Sunscreen SPF 60.

So far, I’m very happy with this product. It’s ”thinner” -- more ”liquid” than other lotion-type sunscreens, and the temptation is to use more than is necessary to achieve the desired result. Don’t give in to the temptation or you’ll encounter some if the issues mentioned in other reviews (milky residue with perspiration, greasy feeling, etc.). Using a minimal amount works fine and it holds up very well over time. Using the minimal amount necessary also helps make this a little more economical since I’m not using as much per application. I have very sensitive skin and even some skincare products that purport to be ”hypo-allergenic” have caused hives in the past. Not this one -- no issues at all.

I don’t spend a lot of time in the sun, but
when I do, this will be my sunscreen of choice. Solid 5 stars...

title: Wowsers!  Really nice scrunchies ...

I've been using them for my long (almost hip-length) hair since the 1980s (yes, I'm that old), since they do a good job of keeping my hair pulled back and out of my face without making too much of a "fashion statement."
